sessions.abstract:
Morning Movement for Stronger Bodies, Sharper Minds & Better Days

sessions.title: Is IP Right for You? Women Leaders Share Real‑World Paths in Patents
sessions.abstract:
“Is IP Right for You?” invites women in tech into a candid conversation about real career paths in intellectual property, from patent architect to patent attorney. With a moderator leading the way, three women representing in-house, law firm, and technical IP roles will reveal both their success stories and the real tradeoffs they face in workload, advancement, connection to technology, and worklife boundaries.
Panelists will share their journeys into IP, walk through a day in the life, and discuss what they find most energizing and challenging. They will also examine how core skills like curiosity about technology, comfort with ambiguity, strong communication, advocacy, and resilience are valued differently in each setting. Attendees will gain practical insight on how to break into IP from technical careers, how to choose among law firm, in-house, and technical IP tracks, how to grow into leadership, and concrete next steps to explore IP after Grace Hopper.

sessions.title: Agentic AI in Pharma & Life Sciences: Designing Trustworthy AI for High-Stakes Decisions
sessions.abstract:
Generative AI is rapidly evolving, yet in pharma and life sciences, adoption requires more than impressive outputs, it requires trust. Decisions in these domains affect patient outcomes, regulatory compliance, and high-stakes business strategy, making transparency and accountability essential.

This session introduces agentic AI, an approach where multiple AI agents collaborate to plan tasks, reason step by step, use tools responsibly, and involve humans at key decision points. Attendees will learn how agentic AI differs from traditional generative AI and why governance, safety, and evaluation frameworks are critical in regulated environments. The session focuses on practical system design principles that enable trustworthy, explainable, and responsible AI for high-impact decision-making.

sessions.title: From 6 Internships to the Trading Desk: Building a Career Where Finance Meets Code
sessions.abstract:
Trading firms hire software engineers to solve some of the hardest distributed systems, optimization, and data engineering problems in the industry, yet this career path remains nearly invisible to most CS graduates. At the intersection of two male-dominated fields, the representation gap for women is especially stark.
This talk draws on a career spanning 6 internships across prop trading firms, big tech, and traditional finance, followed by engineering roles at Robinhood and Old Mission Capital. Attendees will learn what engineers actually build at different types of firms, how to evaluate radically different company types during a job search, and practical strategies for breaking into trading technology. The talk is further informed by years of mentoring students and early-career engineers — through founding Prosperitas Consulting, leading women-in-tech communities at two companies, and recruiting at top universities, ensuring the advice goes well beyond one person's story.

sessions.title: Leading Through Loss: 12 Miscarriages & the Corporate Climb
sessions.abstract: While building a corporate career, Anne Marie endured twelve miscarriages in silence. In this powerful session, she shares what it means to lead while grieving, perform while breaking, and redefine success when life does not go as planned. This is not just a story about loss. It is about resilience, faith, identity, and the courage to show up in rooms that rarely make space for pain. Attendees will leave with a deeper understanding of strength, compassion, and what true leadership looks like behind the title.

sessions.title: I’m Doing Great Work. Why Am I Not Moving Up?
sessions.abstract: Many engineers believe promotions are earned purely through technical excellence. In reality, advancement depends on visibility, timing, scope, organizational context, and sponsorship. This talk breaks down the mechanics behind engineering promotions and provides a practical framework for progressing with intention rather than guesswork.

sessions.title: Engineering the Quantum Era: What Every Builder Needs to Know
sessions.abstract:
Quantum computing is often framed as a distant, physics-heavy frontier, but engineers and product builders are already shaping its future. This session demystifies quantum computing for technical professionals without a physics background and explores what it actually means for software engineers, AI practitioners, and engineering leaders today.

We will break down how quantum computing differs from classical systems using intuitive engineering analogies, examine where quantum is being tested in industry, and clarify what “quantum advantage” truly means beyond the hype. The session will also outline practical entry points for engineers, from software tooling and hybrid systems to emerging roles in quantum product and infrastructure.

Attendees will leave with a grounded understanding of the technology, its realistic timelines, and how to position themselves for opportunities in the next computing revolution.

sessions.title: Networking Jedi: How to use “the force” of networking to land your next job.
sessions.abstract: Research consistently shows that networking is one of the most powerful drivers of career opportunity. Yet women’s networks tend to be small and relationship-deep. At the same time, women are frequently socialized to be modest, more outgoing or "like-able", yet not overly self-promotional. In this workshop, you’ll hear examples of how women can amplify their talent and skills and get a job through networking, even if you’re an introvert or have an identity insecurity. You’ll learn from a LinkedIn jedi actionable advice to claim your individual power, be your authentic self, and network in-person and online to get that next job. We will role play as a group for some tough situations, and to build your personal board of directors. You will leave the room with follow-up actions to take and a larger network than when you entered.

sessions.title: An Actionable Plan for Your First 30/60/90 Days/Weeks/Months
sessions.abstract:
Starting a new job can be exciting, but honestly, also scary. Inner monologue kicks in immediately: "Am I qualified?" "When will they figure out I don't know what I'm doing?" "What should I even be focusing on right now?" We say this to ourselves, but rarely aloud. Feeling like you’re not enough, imposter syndrome, and finding your place in work are real; the feelings don't discriminate by experience. Whether you're landing your first role or pivoting into leadership, the unknowns can be overwhelming. You may look up one day and realize weeks have passed without clear direction, or worse, that you've been working on the wrong things entirely.
The goal of this session is to change the cycle of self-doubt, lack of direction, and quiet struggle to help attendees find their footing. Through goal setting and open dialogue, we will discuss practical milestones for those critical early weeks and months in a new position, and strategies for navigating ambiguity when no one hands you a roadmap.

sessions.title: Vibe Coding for Visionaries: Building Your MVP at the Speed of Thought with AI
sessions.abstract:
The traditional barrier to entry for tech entrepreneurship—finding a technical co-founder or mastering complex syntax—has officially crumbled. Welcome to the era of Vibe Coding.
In this session, we explore how Gen AI and Natural Language Programming are shifting the entrepreneurial landscape from "how to code" to "what to build". We will define the "Vibe Coding" workflow: a high-level, intent-driven approach to software development that allows non-technical and technical founders alike to manifest complex applications using LLMs as their primary interface.
Attendees will learn how to leverage the "Vibe Coding" stack (Cursor, Replit, or Claude) to move from a napkin sketch to a functional Minimum Viable Product (MVP) in hours. We will specifically address how this democratization of tech bypasses traditional gatekeepers, secure early-stage funding, & retain greater equity.Join us to learn how to lead with logic, architecture, & "vibes" to build the next generation of AI-native startups.

sessions.title: Agentic AI in Enterprises: From Fundamentals to Production Implementation
sessions.abstract:
Agentic AI is rapidly transforming enterprises, shifting the paradigm from reactive chatbot deployments to autonomous, goal-driven systems capable of reasoning, planning, and acting across complex business workflows. While early enterprise AI initiatives focused on conversational interfaces and scripted automation, a new class of systems is emerging intelligent agents that combine large language models with memory, tools, planning strategies, and orchestration frameworks to execute multi-step tasks with minimal human intervention. These systems are not merely answering questions; they are achieving objectives.

What makes this moment particularly critical is the pace of change facing developers and architects building these systems. The agentic tooling ecosystem—spanning frameworks like LangGraph, AutoGen, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP)is evolving at a rate that demands continuous adaptation. Developers must now navigate shifting abstractions, rapidly deprecating APIs, and emerging patterns such as multi-agent orchestration, tool calling standardization, and dynamic memory architectures. Adaptability is no longer a soft skill; it is a core engineering competency. In this technical talk, Agentic AI in Enterprises: From Fundamentals to Production Implementation, we take a structured journey from first principles to fully operational enterprise systems delivering measurable return on investment. The session begins by establishing a clear conceptual foundation for what makes an AI system "agentic" and how developers can build systems that remain resilient and maintainable as the underlying models, protocols, and platforms continue to evolve beneath them.

sessions.title: Beyond LeetCode: Building a Career That Outlasts the Hype
sessions.abstract:
The era of the "code typist" is ending. While mastering data structures remains a core requirement for entry, thriving at tech companies now requires a radical shift in mindset. As industry workflows transition from manual coding to directing AI agents, the value of a Software Engineer is shifting from syntax knowledge to high-level reasoning and system design.

In this session, we will explore the shift from a programmer to architect. We move beyond simple code completion to explore agentic AI workflows while witnessing success as a software engineer in our new augmented landscape. This transformation is especially relevant for students, new graduates, and early-career engineers navigating a rapidly changing technology market.

Bringing together engineers from Google, Microsoft, Meta, and NVIDIA, this panel offers a cross-industry view of how engineering careers are evolving in a fast-paced world across different roles, organizations, and technical domains.

This session features a structured discussion on how engineers can build durable careers, maintain long-term technical impact, remain grounded in fundamentals, and responsibly leverage emerging tools to adapt to a rapidly evolving technology landscape. We will explore the following themes:

I. The Shift: From Programmer to Architect

a. Why the software engineer role is evolving: Moving from "how to write" to "what to build."

b. Core Hypothesis: If you want to build a career that lasts, resilience starts with how you build skills, adapt to change, and plan for long-term growth.

II. Responsibility & Quality Control

a. The Engineer as the Guardian: Preventing algorithmic bias and ensuring security.

b. Practical methodologies for testing AI-assisted code.

c. Quality is no longer just about whether code runs. It is about whether the system can be trusted.

III. Building a Foundation That Outlasts Hype

a. Why data structures still matter (the "logic" behind the AI).

b. Developing the "Architect’s Eye": Focus on system design, scalability, and code quality.

c. The future belongs to engineers who can combine speed with depth, using automation without becoming dependent on it.

Why This Session?

For students, new graduates, and early-career engineers, the tech market can feel uncertain. AI is changing how software is built, and many people are wondering what skills will still matter. This session turns that uncertainty into a clear strategy.

Instead of viewing AI as a replacement, we will explore how engineers can use it as a powerful tool to move faster, think bigger, and focus on higher-value work. The goal is to help attendees grow from simply writing code to thinking like architects: people who understand problems deeply, make strong technical decisions, validate results, and take ownership of systems.

Attendees will leave with a practical mindset for building careers that can adapt, sustain, and grow through the next decade of technological change.

Key Learning Objectives :

a. The Foundation: Understand why "LeetCode" skills are the baseline, but "System Thinking" is the differentiator for long-term career growth in Big Tech.

b. Work Smarter with AI: Learn how to pivot from writing raw code to orchestrating AI agents that handle mundane tasks, redefining your personal productivity.

c. Be an Architect: Learn how to review, test, and improve AI-generated work instead of blindly trusting it. This includes setting guardrails, checking security risks, reducing bias, and making sure software is reliable and maintainable.

sessions.title: Career Compounding: Designing Your First 5 Years Like a Product Roadmap
sessions.abstract:
Your first five years are not about experience. They are about slope.
Early careers feel busy. Promotions happen. Skills improve. At the same time, technology including AI is reshaping how work gets done. Execution is faster. Tools are smarter. But long-term success is still shaped by trajectory, not activity.
Small decisions compound over time. The projects you choose, the ownership you accept, the visibility you build, and the skills you stack quietly shape your future. In an environment where AI can accelerate execution, the real advantage comes from building leverage that tools cannot replace.
This session introduces the Career Compounding Curve, a product-inspired framework for intentionally designing early growth. Attendees will leave with a practical roadmap to build leverage, not just experience, in a rapidly evolving workplace.

sessions.title: Get Hired : Practical Ways to Get Seen as Hiring Marketplaces become Agentic
sessions.abstract:
Hiring has moved beyond “post and pray/apply and wait.”
Today, your profile often acts as a 24/7 passive application as hiring increasingly happens through talent marketplaces and proactive sourcing, not just job applications.
Think navigation apps: they don’t give everyone the same route. They adapt to live signals like traffic, delays, and detours to help you reach your destination.
Modern hiring works similarly, responding to signals like clarity, alignment, credibility, responsiveness, follow-through. Two similar résumés can see very different outcomes depending on how clearly those signals show up.
Based on patterns observed in real hiring workflows, ATSs and talent marketplaces, this session shows practical ways to strengthen those signals, how recruiters use assistive workflows without automating decisions or replacing human judgment.
Attendees leave with a repeatable playbook to get seen and hired. No jargon. No algorithms. Practical guidance seekers can apply immediately.

sessions.title: Price Manipulation Detection in High-Volume Time Series Data
sessions.abstract: Meaningful events in time series rarely respect fixed time buckets. A price swing can start between bars, end early, and last seconds or minutes, yet it still needs a clear, explainable window for investigation. The challenge is scale: with 1 second sampling over a regular 6.5 hour trading session (23,400 timestamps), there are about 274 million possible start–end windows for a single instrument. Across millions of instruments, the search space grows to well over a quadrillion windows, before accounting for noise, mixed timescales, and the need to connect a move in the primary signal (price) to unusually concentrated aligned activity (participation/volume). This talk breaks down why “dynamic event windows” are hard in real systems and how to frame scalable, interpretable detection. The ideas generalize to other domains like system monitoring and healthcare signals.

sessions.title: Architecting Agentic Platforms: Scaling with Integrity and Human Empathy
sessions.abstract: Digital transformation has reached a pivot: the mandate for leadership has shifted from deploying AI for efficiency to architecting for Human-Agent Symbiosis. While agentic platforms offer unprecedented scale, success hinges on moving beyond "black-box" automation toward Agentic Integrity. To bridge the gap between technical capability and societal trust, we must address three pillars: rigorous data accuracy, proactive societal education, and empathetic design. This session provides a blueprint for "Human-First" autonomy via a 3-step Strategic Framework: 1.The Integrity Engine: Engineering agents that validate data through multi-perspective reasoning to eliminate "Shadow Logic." 2.Cognitive Restoration: Leveraging platforms to absorb robotic tasks, restoring human capacity for empathy and judgment. 3.The Societal Bridge: Strategies for educating stakeholders to move from AI-anxiety to AI-fluency. This lead a transformation that scales output while empowering the human spirit.

sessions.title: Better Together: Turning Cloud Migrations into Impact That Matters
sessions.abstract:
Cloud migrations are complex, high‑stakes efforts that rarely go exactly as planned. Success depends not just on technology, but on how well technical and financial decisions are aligned from the start.
In this session, we go behind the scenes of a real cloud migration from initial assessment through optimization, sharing a practical playbook built through close cross‑functional collaboration. We’ll discuss the trade‑offs that mattered most, the lessons learned, and how aligning architecture and cost strategy lead to better outcomes.
This talk is for cloud practitioners, technical leads, and anyone working in environments where engineers and finance don’t always speak the same language. Attendees will leave with actionable insights, a collaboration model they can apply in their own organizations, and real examples of how women are driving large‑scale cloud transformations with clarity, confidence, and impact.

sessions.title: Responsible AI Is Not Fluff: How Governance and Regulation Are Redefining Technical Leadership
sessions.abstract:
Responsible AI is often dismissed as abstract or theoretical. But as global AI governance frameworks solidify and regulatory pressures intensify, responsible AI practices are becoming operational requirements and not just optional values statements.

This session explores how AI governance is reshaping technical roles and why engineers, researchers, and product leaders who understand responsible AI are gaining a strategic advantage. Attendees will learn how to translate responsible AI from principle to practice, how governance frameworks affect product design, and how to leverage responsible AI expertise as a career differentiator.

sessions.title: They said Yes: How to find, ask, and keep a mentor that changes your career
sessions.abstract:
For many women and underrepresented technologists, the biggest barrier to finding a mentor isn't a shortage of willing mentors but the paralyzing fear of asking. What could I possibly offer someone so senior? Am I wasting their time?
This panel dismantles that fear. Voices spanning career stages, mentorship styles, mentees who have had successful mentor relationships, and diverse lived identities share the full arc of the journey: finding the right person, making the ask, sustaining it, and knowing when (and how) to move on. Critically, we include the mentor's perspective because hearing what mentors actually hope to gain is the most powerful antidote to imposter syndrome.
GHC is the perfect moment for this conversation. Attendees are already surrounded by people who want to support them. This will be a Q&A heavy session for attendees to leave with real strategies. It will give them the language, the frameworks, and the permission to finally make that ask.

sessions.title: Millennial Meets Gen Z: How Two Latina Sisters Broke Into Tech Their Own Way
sessions.abstract:
What does breaking into tech look like across generations? This session explores the journeys of two Latina sisters, 13 years apart, who entered tech through very different paths. One transitioned into software engineering midcareer through a full stack bootcamp after working in higher education and nonprofit spaces, while the other followed a traditional route through college, tech internships, and an IT degree. 
Together, they examine how risk, access, mentorship, and timing shaped their confidence, career decisions, and growth. Attendees will gain practical insight into navigating tech entry points, embracing non linear careers, and building cross generational mentorship that supports women across stages.

sessions.title: From ‘'Late Start’' to 2x Google: A Strategic Guide to Cracking Technical Interviews
sessions.abstract: Breaking into competitive tech roles can feel overwhelming, especially when you feel like you started late, lacked access, or do not fit the “typical” tech background. In this session, I share the strategy I used to navigate technical interviews and break into Big Tech twice as a student. Attendees will learn how interviews are evaluated beyond coding, how to build a focused preparation plan, solve problems with clarity, and craft strong behavioral stories. Participants will leave with a repeatable framework, practical confidence, and the reminder that where you start does not define how far you can go.

sessions.title: Mentors Help You Grow - Sponsors Help You Advance: A Mentorship Playbook for New Grads
sessions.abstract: Early-career technologists are often told to “find a mentor,” yet many new graduates and early-career professionals still struggle to gain visibility, access opportunities, or advance in their first roles. The missing piece is sponsorship & advocacy - the professionals who actively advocate for you when decisions about projects, promotions, and leadership opportunities are made. This session focuses on helping young women understand how mentorship influences career growth and how graduates can begin building these relationships early on. The aim is to share practical strategies for identifying potential sponsors, building credibility, and increasing professional visibility.

sessions.title: Bridging Human Expertise and AI: Scaling Secure Workflows with MCP Servers
sessions.abstract: As organizations accelerate digital transformation, the challenge isn’t just integrating AI — it’s doing so securely, intelligently, and at scale. This session explores how Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers connect AI models to real-world infrastructure, enabling developers and architects to build context-aware, secure, and automated workflows. We’ll break down practical patterns for integrating MCP with platforms like HashiCorp Vault and Terraform, showing how to design systems where AI acts as a trusted collaborator - not a black box. Attendees will leave with clear strategies to implement AI-enhanced workflows that are auditable, permissioned, and adaptable across teams. Whether you’re modernizing infrastructure or scaling customer experiences, learn how MCP unlocks the balance between automation, compliance, and human oversight.

sessions.title: Prompt. Judge. Decide. A Workshop on Engineering Judgment with AI
sessions.abstract:
AI-generated technical proposals often look impressive: polished language, multiple architectural patterns, exhaustive sections. But beneath the surface, they mask weak assumptions and pages of confident-sounding text with little substance. When a 50-line feature becomes a 500-line design document, the bottleneck shifts from writing to discernment.

As AI makes it easy to generate more content, engineers must get better at judging what actually matters. Without this skill, teams risk approving unclear designs and building systems that are hard to maintain.

This hands-on workshop builds two essential skills: designing effective prompts for technical problems and applying sound judgment to evaluate and refine AI responses. Through guided exercises, participants learn to separate signal from noise, surface assumptions and trade-offs, and shape AI output into concise, decision-ready proposals.

Participants leave with practical frameworks and prompting patterns they can apply immediately.

sessions.title: Why Networking Is So Exhausting: How to Talk to Strangers Without Burning Out
sessions.abstract:
This interactive workshop translates research from social psychology, dialogue modeling, and cognitive science into practical tools for navigating networking conversations at conferences, career fairs, and professional events.
Designed especially for students and early-career technologists who find large conferences energizing but overwhelming, this session explains why networking feels cognitively draining — and how to make it easier.
Participants will learn a repeatable framework for:
Starting conversations confidently
Moving toward a meaningful goal
Ending interactions gracefully
Through live demonstrations and structured pair exercises, attendees will practice energy-efficient conversation strategies and adapt them to their own communication style. Participants will leave with concrete scripts, a personalized networking plan, and research-backed techniques to reduce burnout while advancing their careers.

sessions.title: 7 Lessons in 7 Months: How Motherhood Made Me a Better Product Leader
sessions.abstract:
After becoming a mother, I realized something unexpected: motherhood wasn’t a pause in my leadership journey; it was an accelerated leadership lab. In seven months, I developed deeper resilience, sharper stakeholder management, stronger prioritization, greater empathy, and the ability to navigate uncertainty. From operating on three-hour sleep cycles to calming a crying newborn who cannot yet communicate, motherhood strengthened core leadership muscles every early-career technologist must build. 

This session reframes motherhood not as a career trade-off but as advanced leadership training. Through candid stories and research-backed insights on working mothers in tech, I will share 7 lessons that strengthened my product thinking and how they apply to building teams, shipping products, and leading responsibly in AI-driven environments. Whether or not you are a parent, this talk will reshape how you think about growth, ambition, and leadership under constraint.

sessions.title: Your Job Search, From Prep to Offer
sessions.abstract: Landing a job doesn't start with applying: it starts months earlier. This hands-on workshop walks early-career technologists through the full job search journey: from building a standout LinkedIn profile and personal website, networking with intention, and applying strategically. Attendees will learn how to prepare for and follow up after networking events, use an iterative resume process, and reach out to recruiters in a way that builds real relationships, not transactional ones. The session ends with a live partner activity where participants review each other's resumes and LinkedIn profiles, then practice writing a cold outreach message to a recruiter. Attendees will leave with actionable feedback on their materials and a ready-to-send message draft. What makes this different: real feedback on your actual materials, from a peer, in the room, plus a live look at what a winning recruiter message looks like.

sessions.title: Post SaaS: Building at the Frontier of AI and Physical Systems
sessions.abstract:
The software moat is compressing, and roles that have defined the last decade of tech careers are being automated or commoditized faster than the industry can follow. The fastest-growing, highest-leverage opportunities in tech are shifting orientation: applying AI to physical systems. The industries that underpin the global economy (chips, infrastructure, power, robotics, autonomous machines) are being reshaped by AI, and they need a new kind of thinker and technologist to build what comes next.

Normal Computing sits at this frontier, building AI for silicon engineering and developing unconventional computing architectures. 

This panel brings together two leaders from Normal Computing. Faris Sbahi, co-founder and CEO, will share why the convergence of AI and physical systems represents the defining career opportunity of this generation, and how unconventional skills will be needed to meet future demand. Hanna Yip, who came to Normal from an AI and machine learning background and now leads Normal's EDA product development, will speak about what it's like to build an AI platform for chip design engineers, and developing deep domain fluency in chip design on the job.

The session will also address the honest, practical realities of what it takes to work in product and engineering at a startup that is building completely novel tools for expert users; and thriving in a culture that values intellectual curiosity and adaptability over traditional pedigree. Normal operates a forward-deployed model where engineers work on-site with customers and own outcomes end to end, and people carry more responsibility than their titles would suggest at a larger company. Normal is one of the most difficult places to work, probably in the world; but this type of frontline engineering with customers is an opportunity to learn quickly and build domain expertise in an applied AI setting. 

Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of where the highest-leverage careers in tech are heading , concrete strategies for navigating career transitions into deep tech and semi engineering, and an honest view of what it takes to build in novel computing paradigms.

sessions.title: AI Roadshow Experience
sessions.abstract: Get hands-on with the future of AI! The AI Roadshow Experience features five interactive stations where you'll rotate through cutting-edge demos and workshops. Perfect for all skill levels—discover how AI is transforming technology and learn practical skills you can apply immediately.

sessions.title: Celebrating Technologists of Color
sessions.abstract: Join us for a powerful celebration honoring the incredible technologists of color who are redefining the tech landscape. This is your space to unite with a vibrant community of diverse trail-blazers, share your triumphs, and spark the collaborative networks and leadership opportunities that drive systemic change and elevate our collective power.

sessions.title: Leading Through the AI Shift
sessions.abstract: From agentic development to AI-powered planning, the software development lifecycle is rapidly evolving. Join engineering leaders and founders as they share the career-defining experiences that shaped their leadership journeys and how they are driving responsible AI adoption to transform engineering strategy.

sessions.title: IBM Power 11 - Next-generation, AI-optimized server platform designed for high-performance
sessions.abstract: Financial services now demand real-time operations, AI‑driven decisions, and nonstop availability, pushing traditional systems to their limits. This session introduces how IBM Power11 meets these demands with zero planned downtime, sub‑minute ransomware threat detection, and AI acceleration placed directly where critical data resides. As a Performance Engineer on the IBM Power Systems team, I share how we achieved over 55% performance gains on key financial workloads through deep workload analysis, memory‑bandwidth tuning, and cross‑stack optimization. Attendees will learn practical methods to boost throughput, reduce latency, and build resilient, hybrid‑ready architectures. Through intuitive examples and system‑flow insights, this talk empowers practitioners to modernize mission‑critical financial platforms with confidence, clarity, and performance‑driven engineering discipline.

sessions.title: Antifragile Careers: What Startup Failure Taught Me About Thriving in Big Tech
sessions.abstract:
Most career advice emphasizes avoiding failure. But in rapidly evolving industries, the opposite can be true: the right kinds of early-career challenges can create long-term advantage.

Drawing on Nassim Taleb’s concept of antifragility, this session explores how structured exposure to uncertainty—when approached thoughtfully—builds skills, judgment, and resilience that compound over time. I’ll share my experience as an immigrant working across startup and large-scale technology environments, and how navigating change and ambiguity accelerated my professional growth.

You’ll learn how to evaluate asymmetric opportunities where downside is limited, how to manage risk through “sandboxing,” and how to position nontraditional experiences as strengths in competitive hiring markets. This session is not about taking unnecessary risks—it’s about designing a career that benefits from change.

sessions.title: Stop Breaking Your Team: Healing-Centered Leadership for a More Equitable Tech Culture
sessions.abstract: Technical excellence alone cannot sustain teams navigating burnout, rapid change, and the weight of inequity. This session introduces a healing-centered, equity-driven approach to leadership designed for technologists who manage people, projects, or products. Drawing on 15+ years leading cross-sector initiatives and advising executives on culture and DEI, I will share practical tools for building psychological safety, strengthening psychological agency, and creating conditions where people can speak up, challenge assumptions, make choices, and contribute with intention. Attendees will explore how trauma and systemic inequity show up in tech workplaces, practice scripts for hard conversations, and learn meeting and decision-making practices that reduce harm while increasing voice, trust, and shared responsibility. You will walk away with a simple team-rituals checklist and a 30-day leadership experiment you can implement immediately.

sessions.title: The Influence Equation: Communicate with Power Without Changing Who You Are
sessions.abstract:
Most communication training tells women in tech to adapt, speak more confidently, be more assertive, command the room. But constantly performing someone else's communication style is exhausting and unsustainable. This interactive session flips the script. Whether you're in corporate, freelancing, founding a startup, or transitioning between paths, you'll leave with a personalized communication playbook that works for YOU. 
You'll identify your natural communication strengths across four dimensions: energy pattern, information style, interaction mode and processing speed. Through demonstrations and real-world scenarios, you'll practice adapting your style for high-stakes moments, pitching ideas, leading teams, negotiating rates, advocating for yourself, presenting at conferences, while staying rooted in your authentic voice.
This isn't about faking confidence or mimicking leadership stereotypes; it's about wielding your natural communication power intentionally.

sessions.title: The Ally Audit: Are You Building Ladders or Maintaining Walls?
sessions.abstract:
"I had to fight for everything I earned—why should it be easier for them?"
This mindset, often unconscious, perpetuates the very barriers that held us back. As women who've succeeded in tech through grit and resilience, we face a critical choice: Do we smooth the path for those behind us, or do we unconsciously maintain the walls we had to climb?

In this interactive workshop, you'll conduct an honest "Ally Audit" of your own leadership behaviors. Through structured self-assessment, peer dialogue, and real-world scenario analysis, you'll identify unconscious gatekeeping patterns and develop concrete strategies to shift from "earning it the hard way" to "lifting as we climb." You'll leave with a personalized action plan for inclusive leadership that breaks cycles rather than perpetuates them.

This isn't about guilt—it's about awareness, growth, and consciously choosing to be the leader you needed when you were starting out.

sessions.title: Can I Cry At Work? Mother Daughter Tech Leader Duo share the BEST Career Advice
sessions.abstract:
Guaranteed to accelerate your career advancement. Tech leaders and mother / daughter duo Christine and Madeline share unexpected and high impact advice and stories around key aspects of your career growth: 
• Finally the answer to - Can I cry at work?
• Sponsors and Mentors, and finding both
• Clear is kind - high impact feedback 
• Power in Stories, especially for women and non-binary technologists
• Norm on High Performers - Evaluate yourself well in your org 
• Priority is the insider’s secret
• Telling your story, tight now
Many of us are, or will be, the ‘only’ in our teams, or one of few. These two approachable, practical, and funny speakers are YOUR resource: they fast track sharing advice and help you close the gap in pay, leadership and influence. 

While aligned here for mid-career, this advice is a great guideline for early career, and even seasoned leaders who accompany their teams to talks remark that they take away ideas.

sessions.title: Build Your AI-Powered Company Research & Interview Prep Dashboard in 60 Minutes with AWS
sessions.abstract: This 60-minute hands-on workshop is designed for Grace Hopper Celebration (GHC) attendees to build an interactive AI-powered dashboard for company research and interview preparation. Participants will gain practical experience with vibe coding using Kiro, Agentic AI integration, and AWS services while creating a functional application they can use for their own career development. The workshop targets women in tech at all career levels and requires no prior AI or cloud computing experience. Using the Kiro platform with AWS services, the session will deliver both technical skills and immediately applicable career development tools.

sessions.title: Translating Tech: Language, Access, and Non‑Traditional Paths into Cybersecurity
sessions.abstract: An exploratory presentation of the findings from women and non-binary people who entered security and adjacent tech roles from non-traditional backgrounds, including sign-language and spoken-language interpreting, teaching, entrepreneurship, and creative work. An examination of how spoken, signed, and technical language shape access to security careers; how communities like WiCys, WISP, WTE, and DWEN can bridge gaps; and what leaders can change in hiring and onboarding. Through dialogue and concrete examples of findings, attendees will leave with practical strategies to enter security from another field and to make their own teams more accessible to career-changers.

sessions.title: From Visibility to Impact: Building Tech Personal Brands That Open Real Opportunities
sessions.abstract:
In today’s tech ecosystem, personal branding is no longer optional, it’s a powerful tool for career growth, leadership visibility, and community impact. As an engineer, community builder, and speaker who has mentored thousands and worked across startups and tech spaces, I’ve seen how authentic storytelling and strategic positioning can unlock real opportunities beyond resumes.

In this session, I will share practical frameworks to help students in tech build personal brands rooted in clarity, credibility, and consistency. Rather than focusing on vanity metrics, I will explore how to use storytelling, community engagement, AI-assisted workflows, and growth systems to create meaningful professional presence.

This talk aligns with GHC’s mission of empowering individuals in tech by helping them take ownership of their voice, build leadership pathways early, and create inclusive communities that uplift others while advancing their own careers.

sessions.title: You Are the Most Qualified — Why Are You Still Invisible?
sessions.abstract:
You outperformed. You overdelivered. You exceeded every standard they set… and they raised the bar anyway. Because maybe you just got lucky. So you go back to prove that you didn't.

You don't lack confidence. You don't have impostor syndrome. You simply lack positioning.

In the AI era, output is being commoditized. What AI cannot replicate is your judgment, your perspective, the unconventional way you solve problems, your mindful approach to building relationships, and how you lead through collaboration. The leaders who will shape the future are those who have learned to make their identity their competitive edge.

This session is for the senior leader who is done proving her worth and is ready to become the obvious choice.

You will leave with the LEAD Framework: a four-step system built from 20 years of engineering and executive leadership that offers you a clear path from unseen to undeniable.

sessions.title: Enabling Accessibility through Firmware Feature Development
sessions.abstract:
Ever struggled with keyboard shortcuts or fumbled with a thermostat in the dark? That moment of frustration can easily be addressed by enabling accessibility through mindful firmware requirements.

Accessibility is one of the most creative challenges in product development. Hardware adds a layer of complexity. Firmware controls how users physically interact with your device, yet accessibility at this level is often overlooked. Together, we'll explore how Universal Design Principles (UDPs) can guide firmware requirements. Attendees will work through defining the firmware requirements for an end-to-end product. 

You will learn how integrating Universal Design Principles at the firmware level supports flexible, maintainable products that adapt to users. By the end, you will walk away with a practical, repeatable blueprint for defining firmware requirements that address accessibility early in the product development lifecycle.

sessions.title: From RIF to IF: Leading Through AI, Automation, and Workforce Disruption
sessions.abstract: Layoffs aren’t just workforce decisions—they’re leadership signals. In this session, Michelle introduces the RIF to IF framework, a strategic approach to navigating AI-driven disruption, restructuring, and organizational change. Attendees will learn how to protect their influence, stabilize income, and maintain strategic relevance—so they can reposition before disruption makes the decision for them.

speakers.name: Michelle Medious-Washington
speakers.title: CEO, Elevated Encounters | Author | Executive Advisor

sessions.title: Leading Beyond Work: Join a Nonprofit Board at Any Career Stage
sessions.abstract:
Women often undervalue their abilities, and the same holds true when it comes to being a board member. During this engaging, energetic and peer-centered workshop, we will empower women to claim their space in nonprofit board leadership where they’re still underrepresented. Today, women make-up 48–52% of nonprofit board members, despite being the majority of nonprofit workers. 
Nonprofits struggle with all aspects of running an organization. The main requirement for board service is PASSION. During this workshop, participants will be inspired and activated for board service. Each segment moves participants from awareness → clarity → confidence → commitment → actionable steps. They’ll understand how non-profit boards work and how their skills translate to board assets. This renewed clarity on their qualifications will enable an actionable plan for board membership that can be implemented at all career levels.
No board experience is necessary, and ALL career levels and skills are welcome.

speakers.name: Christine Grobarcik
speakers.title: Industry Partner Sales Specialist, Financial Services

sessions.title: Flipping the Script -Beyond the Code: Decoding the Interviewer’s Rubric for Early-Career Success
sessions.abstract: The transition from a classroom to a technical interview is often jarring. Students focus on "The Solution," while interviewers focus on "The Colleague." This session aims to bridge the gap between candidate performance and interviewer expectations, demystifying the "Hidden Rubric" used to evaluate emerging talent.

sessions.title: Scaling Stability: How to Build Resilient Human Systems
sessions.abstract:
In software engineering, resilience traditionally focuses on a system's ability to withstand component failure. This session shifts the focus to the engineer. Led by Senior Software Engineers from Pinterest and Uber, The Human Stack framework applies systems-design principles to mental health and team stability, especially during industry shocks like layoffs. It moves beyond standard "wellness tips" to build a robust engineering culture that prioritizes Innovation and Impact.

We will break down how to:
- Identify Single Points of Failure: Recognize high-stress burdens from siloed institutional knowledge
- Implement "Human Failovers": Build peer-support networks and documentation to allow engineers to step back without system collapse
- Monitor "Mental Latency": Use engineering metrics to detect and prevent burnout

Attendees will gain a technical mental model for resilience, ensuring the most critical part of the tech stack (the people) remains high-impact in a volatile environment.

sessions.title: From F-1 to Hired: How I Got Noticed on Campus When Nobody Was Looking
sessions.abstract: Two months. That is how long it took me to go from landing in the U.S. with zero domestic connections to securing my first on-campus research role - on an F-1 visa, in a new country, with a resume no one here had context for. This talk is not a FAANG fairy tale. It is the honest, specific playbook behind that two-month window: how I got professors to actually read my emails, how I reframed my AI and data science projects to be impossible to ignore, and how I cracked the on-campus job system that most international students do not even know exists. If you are doing everything right and still hearing nothing back, this talk is for you.

speakers.name: Yashvi Kommidi
speakers.title: MS Data Science Student & Student Research Associate, University of Arizona

sessions.title: Career Pathway: Practical Toolkit – Performance, Visibility, Influence, Sponsorship, and Momentum
sessions.abstract:
In today’s dynamic workplace, career growth requires more than strong performance. It requires intentional visibility, strategic influence, and the ability to build meaningful sponsorship and momentum. This interactive workshop is designed to equip participants with practical guidance and actionable tools to take ownership of their career pathway and accelerate their professional development.
Participants will gain clarity on how to enhance their job performance, increase their visibility within the organization, and build influence with key stakeholders. The workshop will also explore how to cultivate sponsorship, communicate value effectively, and position oneself for future opportunities.
Through facilitated discussion, self-reflection, and practical exercises, participants will learn how to create an advancement ecosystem map; and develop and leverage sponsorship relationships.

sessions.title: From Burnout to Belonging: Employee-Led Wellbeing as a Culture Differentiator
sessions.abstract:
In today’s dynamic landscape of technology and business, effective performance is driven not solely by intellectual capability, but also by personal energy, sense of purpose, and genuine sense of belonging. This session presents wellbeing as a key aspect of organizational culture and a strategic asset, rather than just an employee benefit. The session explores how organizations can move from burnout to renewed energy by managing energy over time. 

The session highlights how bottom up wellbeing culture drives inclusion, retention, and high performance. Participants will reflect on what it means to reset, recharge, and refocus in the midst of fast-paced AI-powered work environment, and how everyday practices such as movement, breathwork, and mindfulness can strengthen focus, resilience, and decision making. 

At Grace Hopper Celebration, Asti and Rakhi strive to bring a powerful message: when wellbeing and inclusion come together, diverse technologists can stay bold, resilient, and ready to lead.

sessions.title: From Impact to Influence: How Women in Tech Can Prepare for Board Roles
sessions.abstract:
In today’s tech landscape, board experience is a powerful lever for influence, impact, and long-term economic power—yet many women in tech don’t know how to access it.

This interactive workshop reframes board readiness from something you wait for to something you build. Attendees will learn how to translate their existing experience into board-level value, shift from operator to director thinking, and craft a clear, concise board-ready narrative.

This is a working session—not a panel. Through a structured, hands-on format, participants will build a board positioning statement and identify three concrete next steps to increase visibility, strengthen relationships, and access board opportunities.

sessions.title: Architecting Your Career: Building Technical Portability Across Domains
sessions.abstract: Career transitions in tech don’t succeed because you decide to move - they succeed because you prepared before the opportunity appeared. This session explores how to intentionally upskill across technical layers so you can pivot quickly between roles and domains. Drawing from real shifts across AI SaaS, safety-critical medical systems, front-end engineering, and AI infrastructure, we break down the foundational competencies that truly transfer - and the exact areas interviewers probe when evaluating cross-domain candidates. Attendees will leave with a practical roadmap for identifying high-leverage growth opportunities, building portable technical depth, and reducing ramp time when making their next move.

sessions.title: From Developer to Engineering Manager: The Technical and Emotional Shift No One Prepares You For
sessions.abstract:
The transition from software developer to engineering manager isn’t just a promotion - it’s a career change. After years of debugging code, you're suddenly "debugging" human dynamics, cross-team influence and emotional intelligence, often with zero documentation.

As a female engineer turned leader in a male-dominated field, I’ll share how I redefined technical credibility beyond coding, embraced the emotional complexity of leadership and learned that management is a balancing act: leading down, collaborating across & managing up.

In this session, I’ll share lessons from my transition from developer to engineering manager, including the mindset shifts and practical frameworks that helped me move from individual contributor to team multiplier.

Through candid stories and practical frameworks, you'll leave with a "README.md" for engineering managers, to stay technically strong, measure success beyond personal output and lead the human side of engineering no CS degree prepares you for.

sessions.title: Scale Up - The Best Kept Secret to Early Career Advancement
sessions.abstract:
Most early career advice focuses on two options: small startups or big tech companies. Few people realize there is a powerful middle path: the scale up.

Scale ups have moved past the high-risk stage of early startups. They have proven demand, secured funding, and are growing rapidly, but they have not yet built the full structure that enables a large company to thrive. This stage gives early career professionals unique opportunities to design processes, influence cross functional systems, and expand scope faster than in enterprises.

This session will show why scale ups are one of the fastest ways to accelerate your career and how to spot them when evaluating your next move.

sessions.title: Trust at Scale: How We Built Voice AI That Knows When to Ask for Help
sessions.abstract:
When AI answers a support call, it's not just handling volume, it's embodying your brand when customers are most vulnerable: a missed flight, a disputed refund, plans unraveling in real time. Voice AI has evolved from rigid scripts to systems that take real actions. In production, automation shapes trust and financial outcomes.

We'll share how we built voice AI that resolves routine issues while bringing humans in when empathy and judgment matter. You'll see our technical decisions: evaluating capabilities against experience needs, balancing performance with quality, solving for real-world noise and interruptions, and progressing to agentic AI that moves beyond scripts.

We'll explore patterns from production: confidence thresholds triggering escalation, guardrails preventing poor experiences, interruption-friendly design, and agent copilot reducing handle time while preserving empathy. You'll see what makes handoffs seamless versus frustrating. Applicable across industries where voice meets critical moments, you'll leave with a blueprint for launching voice AI that customers, agents, and leaders trust.

sessions.title: Quantum at Scale: Why Illinois Invested and What the Future Will
sessions.abstract: Quantum technology has progressed beyond theoretical concepts and is now emerging as a critical component of future innovation infrastructure. In this session, Dr. Harley T. Johnson, Executive Director and CEO of the Illinois Quantum & Microelectronics Park and professor at the University of Illinois, explains why Illinois made a landmark investment in quantum and microelectronics, what infrastructure is being built, and what breakthroughs are expected across computing, materials science, sensing, and national security. Designed to cut through hype, this talk provides technologists and leaders with a grounded understanding of quantum’s real-world implications and the workforce, research, and economic systems required to realize its potential responsibly.

sessions.title: Workforce Transformation & AI: Building a Sustainable Career
sessions.abstract: In a world where AI is advancing rapidly, many organizations are still wrestling with what to do first—and how to lead people through the resulting shift in work, skills, and culture. This Women in Tech panel brings together industry leaders from EY and our client partners to explore leadership in the age of AI and what it takes to build future‑forward, resilient careers and organizations as work is redesigned—not just jobs. The conversation will bridge practical AI adoption choices (identifying high‑value/low‑risk use cases, validating data and knowledge readiness, making build vs. buy vs. partner decisions) with the human realities of transformation (reskilling and internal mobility, manager enablement, responsible AI and trust, and how productivity and performance are being redefined). Designed to be meaningful for professionals at all stages of their career, this session aims to spark thoughtful dialogue, share real‑world lessons, and create meaningful connections.

sessions.title: Three Leaders. One AI Stack. Hundreds of Millions of Users.
sessions.abstract:
Every company is asking the same question: how do you move from AI experimentation to AI that delivers real customer value?  As AI capabilities reach new heights, turning that potential into experiences customers can use is still the hard part. Closing the gap requires knowing where to bet, what to build, and how to scale.​

Three women own these three critical layers of PayPal's AI stack serving hundreds of millions of users. Uma Kona makes the strategic bets: which to take, when to invest, and how to build a strategy that holds up when AI capabilities are evolving fast. Linsey Pang builds native AI solutions from scratch, fine-tuning models on decades of proprietary data no competitor has. Connie Miao leverages research and strategy to build innovative agentic AI products, creating the consumer experiences that PayPal users rely on every day. This panel is no hype, no theory. Just an honest look at what it takes to move fast and deploy AI at enterprise scale.​

speakers.name: Aarti Ashok

sessions.title: Demystifying the Interview Process: How to Master Technical and Case Interviews in the Tech Industry
sessions.abstract:
Stepping into the tech industry requires more than just great coding skills, it requires knowing how to communicate your problem-solving process under pressure. In this interactive workshop, Capital One professionals will guide attendees through two critical components: the technical interview and the technical case interview. Attendees will be able to practice their newly acquired skills by getting into the mind of interviewers when evaluating mock interviews role-played by Capital One professionals and by practicing questions in peer-to-peer conversations.
This workshop is engineered to build your confidence, refine your strategy, and enhance your readiness. Don’t just show up to your next interview – master it!

sessions.title: Staying Grounded in the Age of AI: Skills to Carry Your Career Forward
sessions.abstract:
AI is changing how work gets done, but the fundamentals of building a strong career in tech still matter. For students and early-career professionals entering the workforce, the question is no longer just how to use new tools, but how to build the judgment, curiosity, resilience, and technical foundation needed to grow alongside them.

In this panel, leaders from Bloomberg's Product, Data, and Engineering departments will discuss what they look for in team members and how expectations are evolving in the age of AI. They will explore how early-career professionals can strengthen core skills, navigate uncertainty, ask better questions, understand customers and products, and use AI thoughtfully without losing sight of their own problem-solving abilities.

Attendees will gain practical insight into how to manage AI anxiety, build confidence in changing environments, and take intentional steps toward a career that is adaptable, grounded, and future-ready.

sessions.title: The AI Attack Surface and the People Who Defend It
sessions.abstract:
AI is rapidly reshaping what it means for cybersecurity experts to protect an organization against bad actors. This talk covers securing AI systems and using AI to defend them, with a real-time view of what it's like to operate on this frontier. 
COVERS
– Prompt injection, model poisoning, and data leakage through large language models (LLMs) 
– Agentic AI risks and emerging attack vectors
– How enterprise security teams are adapting their threat models
– What “AI-native security” looks like in practice at scale

sessions.title: AI as a Decision Layer: Redefining Trust, Risk, and Competitive Advantage
sessions.abstract:
As enterprises accelerate digital transformation, traditional security and access models built on static rules and one time decisions are increasingly misaligned with real world risk. This session explores how AI can evolve from a tactical analytics tool into a strategic decision layer that continuously governs trust, access, and risk across the enterprise.

Designed for senior leaders and executives, the talk examines how adaptive, behavior based AI systems enable organizations to reduce risk, improve operational resilience, and build durable competitive advantage without sacrificing stability, explainability, or governance. Attendees will gain a practical framework for evaluating AI driven transformation, understanding its business impact, and avoiding common failure modes as automation scales.

speakers.name: Vaishali Nagpure
speakers.title: IT Network professional expert

sessions.title: How to Ace the Big Tech Interview
sessions.abstract:
Landing a role at a top tech company requires more than technical skills—it demands strategic preparation, authentic storytelling, and confidence under pressure. This presentation brings together experienced tech interviewers from Amazon Web Services (AWS) and OpenAI to demystify the big tech interview process. Whether you're preparing for your first tech interview or aiming to level up to a senior role, this session provides insider perspectives on what truly makes candidates stand out.
Our presenters will share real-world insights on navigating behavioral interviews, technical assessments, and the unique aspects of big tech hiring processes. You'll learn how to craft compelling stories using proven frameworks, and avoid common pitfalls that eliminate otherwise strong candidates. This isn't generic interview advice—it's actionable intelligence from those who make hiring decisions at scale.

sessions.title: From Cloud Native to Multi-Cloud Native: Write Once, Deploy Anywhere
sessions.abstract:
While "Cloud Native" promised portability, that promise often stops at a single infrastructure. The traditional definition rarely addresses multi-cloud realities, leaving enterprises tethered to vendors through fragmented SDKs and proprietary APIs. We must evolve to Multi-Cloud Native, a paradigm where applications are provider-agnostic from day one.

In this session, I explore architectural principles for portable applications using driver-based design patterns. I will demonstrate implementation through MultiCloudJ (Salesforce’s open-source Java SDK) and Go Cloud (Google’s library), which decouple business logic from provider code to enable true "write once, deploy anywhere" capability.

Drawing from Salesforce’s journey across AWS, GCP, and Alibaba Cloud, I share the engineering challenges of this shift. Finally, we examine how AI Native development can automate refactoring legacy code into multi-cloud native standards.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: How to Make Tech Better
sessions.abstract:
Telle Whitney is the co-founder of the Grace Hopper Celebration of Computing and former President of the Anita Borg Institute.  Fran Berman is Director of Public Interest Technology at UMass and former Chair of the AnitaB.org Board of Trustees.  This unique session will focus on insights and wisdom from Telle and Fran on how to improve both the culture and the impact of today’s technologies.  The session will feature a conversation with Telle and Fran, highlighting key points from their new books:

“Rebooting Tech Culture:  How to Ignite Innovation and Build Organizations where Everyone Can Thrive”, Telle Whitney, Harvard Business Review Press.

“Better Tech:  Putting People First in Cyberspace,” Fran Berman, MIT Press.

Telle and Fran will discuss how tech innovation and the environment in which it is developed are intertwined.   Together, they offer a way to address the risks of tech and pragmatic advice to make tech both more impactful and innovative.

speakers.name: Telle Whitney

sessions.title: AI as an emotional support tool - Rethinking Product Design in a Tech Driven World
sessions.abstract:
AI-driven products have evolved far beyond automation and recommendation systems. As AI becomes increasingly embedded in decision-support experiences, product design must move beyond efficiency and metrics toward a more human-centered lens.

This session brings together examples from consumer apps and enterprise systems where “emotional lifecycle gaps” emerge — moments that impact customer trust, retention, and overall user experience.

Drawing from product thinking, this talk explores how traditional frameworks can be extended to better identify and bridge these gaps in AI-powered products.Product managers, entrepreneurs, and technologists are invited to think beyond features and analytics to create more meaningful human impact in an AI-first world — and explore how technology can better support the people using it.

sessions.title: The Engineering Leadership Stack: From IC to Global Team Leader
sessions.abstract: In 2020, I joined Sonos as a Junior Data Engineer. Six years and four promotions later, I lead a global team of 15 across Data Engineering, Analytics, and ML spanning the U.S. and U.K. Nobody handed me a playbook. The skills that made me a strong engineer were not the skills I needed to lead engineers. This talk shares four lessons from that transition: navigating the IC-to-manager identity shift, making technical decisions across teams processing billions of daily events without becoming the bottleneck, designing a hybrid global team model that overcame organizational skepticism to deliver $1.5M+ in savings, and building inclusive culture as infrastructure, the structural practices behind 80% retention and 70% faster delivery. Attendees leave with actionable frameworks they can apply immediately.

sessions.title: Find Your "AH HA" Moment - Onboard Your Own Chief Of Staff Agent
sessions.abstract: This session equips the next generation of women leaders to not only onboard an AI employee but to develop, coach, and scale that employee into a true extension of their leadership. Through a high‑energy, hands‑on experience, participants build their own AI Chief of Staff agent—a personalized digital strategic partner shaped by their values, work style, and leadership goals—using the proven Soul Code methodology to ensure clarity, emotional intelligence, and purpose guide the relationship. Beyond onboarding, participants learn to grow their AI Chief of Staff like a real employee—giving feedback, correcting misalignment, developing new skills, and embedding real work artifacts to deepen capability over time. The session closes with the human side of AI transformation: effective change management. Leaders leave understanding that AI success is not about the tech, but about helping people—starting with themselves—move past uncertainty and into empowered, sustained adoption.

sessions.title: Gotta Cache 'Em All: Cache-Aware Coding for Real-World Performance Gains
sessions.abstract:
A 10x performance improvement by changing two lines of code? This happened in our production system!

We share a real performance issue that surprised experienced teams. The root cause? A gap in understanding how modern hardware actually runs programs. Many processors rely on built-in CPU caches, yet the way code interacts with them is rarely taught.

Why does this matter, even if performance isn't your primary focus? These blind spots appear in data pipelines, backend services, and everyday application code, quietly affecting latency and cloud costs. Understanding cache behavior provides a powerful advantage when diagnosing bottlenecks and scaling systems.

Through concrete examples, attendees learn how to harness these caches using memory layout, data access patterns, and iteration order. Practical, language-agnostic techniques are presented, with guidance to avoid micro-optimization.
Designed for early to mid-career technologists, with insights for anyone building production systems.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Letting Go of the Keyboard: Lessons from the Move to People Leadership
sessions.abstract:
One day you’re the go-to individual contributor. The next, you’re the people leader others look to for clarity, momentum, and confidence. That shift is often called a promotion, but it’s really a reinvention: you move from doing the work to leading the people who do it. Your technical expertise still matters, but it shows up differently through guidance, decision making, and enabling others instead of direct execution. The work becomes less tangible, ambiguity increases, and impact is measured in months rather than moments.

In this talk, we share lessons from two perspectives: a leader wrapping up their first year managing people and a seasoned leader reflecting on that same transition. We’ll dig into operating without constant validation, adjusting to delayed and indirect feedback, finding fulfillment in others’ success, and building relationships as the primary lever for trust.

sessions.title: The Friction Between Us: Leading Across Roles in Tech Transformation
sessions.abstract:
Why do smart, experienced teams still struggle during transformation? It’s rarely a lack of talent. It’s misalignment, and often it’s invisible. When we don’t understand each other’s constraints, we mistake behavior for resistance or incompetence. What looks like pushback is often someone doing exactly what their role requires.

In this panel, senior leaders from across the org unpack the incentives driving cross-role friction. They surface real tensions and model how to navigate them constructively. You’ll learn to recognize friction early, approach disagreement with curiosity instead of frustration, and assume good intentions — seeing colleagues as capable professionals operating under real constraints, not obstacles.

This isn’t about “better communication.” It’s about building the cross-role instincts that define influential leaders. Because leadership isn’t about having the answer; it’s about understanding the system.

speakers.name: Charla Kunkel

sessions.title: Lead Me Like You Mean It: The Unspoken Guide to What Employees Wish Leaders Knew
sessions.abstract:
Most leadership sessions focus on how individuals should adapt. This workshop flips the script. We start with a powerful premise: leaders are well intentioned, but without clear input, they default to one‑size‑fits‑all leadership that limits engagement and performance.

In this workshop, participants will articulate what they need from leaders to do their best work and learn how to communicate those needs clearly and confidently. Through guided discussion and practical exercises, attendees will develop language to strengthen manager‑employee relationships and improve day‑to‑day effectiveness.

Designed for professionals at any level, and for managers who want to better enable their teams, this workshop creates value on both sides of the leadership equation. Insights gathered from participants will also inform a post‑conference white paper, extending the impact well beyond the room.

sessions.title: Architecting a Career: Staying Technical in a Rapidly Changing World
sessions.abstract:
You finally carve out time to start that cloud certification or GenAI course. The first night goes well —then deadlines and life take over, and two weeks later you’re restarting the same module again. With GenAI acceleration, technical skills don’t stay fresh for long, and keeping up suddenly feels urgent.
This is not a time‑management lecture or a learning‑path walkthrough. It’s a practical operating model for staying technical in a rapidly shifting industry. You’ll learn the 3C Framework—Consistent, Contextual, and Connected—and apply a 90‑day Learning Roadmap to uncover hidden time pockets, choose one high‑impact skill, and design a micro‑learning habit tied to real work. You’ll learn how to embed learning into everyday workflows, build credibility through steady curiosity, and let go of the do it all mindset.
Walk away with a personalized plan, a 30‑day commitment, and curated less than 20‑minute resources you can sustain.

sessions.title: Louder Isn't Better: Making Space for the Quietly Exceptional
sessions.abstract: In most workplaces, success is measured not just by what you accomplish, but by how loudly you show up. Assertiveness and constant visibility have become the unspoken prerequisites for promotion. This bias toward extroversion undervalues the many strengths introverts bring to the table and forces them to adopt extroverted qualities just to feel secure in their roles. This talk challenges the "extrovert ideal" that quietly shapes who gets ahead, who gets heard, and who gets left behind. Attendees will walk away with practical strategies to build inclusive environments where all employees can do their best work. Ultimately, you'll feel empowered to foster a workplace culture where every voice is valued, because the quietest people in the room may have the most to offer.

speakers.name: Sheila Oh
speakers.title: Teaching Professor and Director, Computer Science Fundamentals Certificate Program

sessions.title: Agent-Driven Development: Architecting Autonomous Workflows for the Modern SDLC
sessions.abstract:
AI has transformed how we write code but our operational overhead - manual Jira grooming, triaging security vulnerabilities, and regression testing - remains a bottleneck. To achieve maximum benefit,we must move beyond "chatbots (prompting) toward Agent-Driven Development (ADD): a framework for orchestrating autonomous, self-healing workflows across the SDLC.

In this session, we will deep-dive into the architecture of "Agentic Loops" that handle the heavy lifting of modern engineering. We will explore three real-world case studies:

The Project Pilot: Automating Jira backlog refinement and requirement mapping.

The Security Shield: Intelligent vulnerability triaging and automated remediation suggestions.

The Quality Loop: AI-driven Test Generation that evolves with your codebase.

Attendees will leave with a technical blueprint for selecting the right orchestration hooks, ensuring data privacy, and implementing "human-in-the-loop" checkpoints to scale AI-augmented operations with confidence

sessions.title: Find Roles Hidden in Your Skills using Graphs
sessions.abstract:
You have more career options than your job title suggests, and a graph can prove it. 

This hands-on workshop uses a career skills graph to answer the question: what roles could I move into based on what I already know how to do? Participants will explore a dataset connecting skills, job roles, and open positions, then personalize it with their own experience. 

Graphs are great at multi-hop traversal, revealing roles two or three connections away. We’ll enhance this with vector similarity to uncover semantically related skills, and an LLM layer to explain why a role fits and highlight skill gaps. 

You’ll leave with a visualized career graph and real queries to guide your next move. Who knows? You might discover an unexpected path.

sessions.title: Designing Execution: Product Thinking as a Leadership Discipline
sessions.abstract: Mid‑career technologists are increasingly asked to lead complex initiatives that span teams, constraints, and competing priorities. While executive direction is often clear, translating that direction into coordinated, sustainable execution is where leadership work happens. This session reframes product thinking as a leadership discipline for designing execution, not a role‑specific or technical practice. Drawing from enterprise‑scale initiatives at the Virginia Community College System, including legacy ERP to cloud transformation and AI governance strategy development, the session introduces a practical framework for turning intent into an execution system. Engagement is embedded throughout the presentation as attendees apply each part of the framework to an initiative they are currently leading or influencing. Participants leave with a clearer execution model they can refine and use immediately to lead delivery with greater clarity, alignment, and confidence.

sessions.title: Game On – Unconventional Strategies for Women Who Lead
sessions.abstract: What if the fastest path to becoming a strategic leader ran through a poker table, a chessboard, or a virtual escape room? This session explores how games — from poker and chess to Minecraft simulations and VR team challenges — teach women the strategic thinking, calculated risk-taking, and resilience that boardrooms demand. We'll spotlight real initiatives like Girls Who Game, GameChangeHERs, and the Women's HistoryPlunge card game, and show how these tools are closing the gender gap in tech leadership. Walk away with a personal game plan to level up your strategic edge — because the first answer will always be no, but the right strategy changes everything.

sessions.title: Manage Your Manager (and your career)
sessions.abstract:
This session is an Interactive workshop to turn common workplace dynamics into career leverage.
Most of us don’t get to choose our managers yet the quality of that relationship can strongly influence career growth, day-to-day effectiveness, and stress levels outside of work. This interactive workshop will help participants build practical skills to “manage up” with clarity and confidence. Through short exercises and guided reflection, the aim is to explore common management styles, employee working styles, and how to collaborate productively. Participants will leave with a simple toolkit for setting expectations, communicating needs, and building a healthier work rhythm including how to ask for help and receive support from a manager, a challenge many women experience.

sessions.title: Bridging Business and Technology as Early-Career Female Developers
sessions.abstract:
As early-career software engineers who began in Bank of America’s Global Technology Analyst Program, we quickly realized technical skill alone doesn’t create impact. The real challenge is translating business needs into scalable solutions while building confidence and credibility. In this session, we’ll share lessons on bridging business and technology early in our careers: asking strategic questions, identifying the core problem behind requests, and communicating clearly with nontechnical partners.

We’ll highlight common pitfalls, effective collaboration strategies, and practical ways early developers can influence decisions and grow professionally. We’ll also discuss how we use AI to strengthen problem-solving, improve efficiency, and accelerate learning. Finally, we’ll share leadership experiences beyond our core roles, mentorship, community involvement, and internal initiatives, that expanded our networks and shaped our long-term paths.

speakers.name: Siri Avula
speakers.title: Software Engineer II & Master's Student in Computer Science

speakers.name: Lahari Vavilala
speakers.title: Assistant Vice President; Software Engineer II

sessions.title: Analytics Data vs AI Data: Why your Architecture Must Evolve
sessions.abstract:
For years, data teams have optimized ETL and ELT pipelines to power dashboards, deliver trusted metrics, and drive executive decision-making. We’ve built reliable analytics foundations designed around aggregation, reporting, and customization.

But AI changes the equation.

Data built for dashboards is not the same as data built for AI-driven analytics. AI systems require richer context, stronger governance, tighter lineage, and greater reproducibility. Pipelines that work for BI often break silently when used to power models.

In this session, I’ll explore the architectural shift required to move from traditional analytics to AI-ready data platforms. I’ll share lessons from working with data leaders navigating this shift, along with practical frameworks for managing this transition and building AI systems that are not only powerful but also trustworthy.

sessions.title: A Gen X, a Gen Z, a Millennial, & a Boomer Walk Into a Tech Conference
