sessions.abstract: Ever wonder how the tech industry is experienced by women from different generations? We did! Come by to hear stories of our unique paths in tech and share your own.

sessions.title: 0 to AI Engineer in an Hour: Build Production-Level RAG Applications
sessions.abstract: Join Muskaan Goyal and Tisha Arora from Amazon, who have four years of experience building AI products and production-ready RAG applications, for a hands-on workshop that takes you from zero to practical AI engineering skills in just one hour. Participants will design prompts, integrate LLMs with vector databases, rank retrieved information, and generate structured outputs — all while building a mini RAG application. This interactive session emphasizes real-world, industry-ready AI engineering workflows, giving attendees a working prototype, reusable code templates, and direct experience with the tasks AI engineers do in production. Laptops with Python and an API key are required.

sessions.title: Can LLM Run On-Call? Inside LinkedIn’s Autonomous Network Agent
sessions.abstract:
On-call is unforgiving. Systems fail at 2AM, not in controlled demos. At LinkedIn, we’re building the Network On-Call Agent: an autonomous AI system that moves beyond triage to real incident remediation. The agent consumes live incident events, correlates signals across dozens of infrastructure systems, dynamically loads operational knowledge, and executes controlled remediation actions, all within strict safety guardrails and audit boundaries.

This session explores what it takes to safely let AI operate in critical production environments. 

We’ll dive into event-driven workflows, validation layers, staged autonomy, cost observability, rollback strategies, and human override mechanisms. If you’re building agentic systems that must diagnose, decide, and act, without compromising reliability, this talk will show what production-grade autonomy actually requires.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Build Your Own Table: How to Create Opportunities in College with Impact Projects
sessions.abstract:
Rejection is redirection, and every closed door is a chance to build your own. This session is for college women and non-binary students in tech who are ready to stop waiting for the right opportunity and start creating it.
Through personal story, practical strategy, and real examples, attendees will discover a concrete framework for building impact projects that open doors, strengthen their resume, and compound into a career they are proud of. The path forward is not always the one that was handed to you. Sometimes you get to design it yourself.
Whether you have faced rejection from an internship, a research program, or a competitive club, this session will remind you that your skills, creativity, and consistency are enough to build something meaningful right now, exactly where you are.

sessions.title: Stop Applying, Start Building: How Non-Technical PMs Use AI Side Projects to Get Hired
sessions.abstract:
The PM job market has changed. Hundreds of applicants per role, AI screening resumes, and hiring managers who can’t tell candidates apart. For non-technical PMs, the challenge is harder: how do you prove you can ship when your resume says “strategy” but not “code”?

This panel brings together PMs who stopped waiting and started building. Each panelist has used free AI tools to ship real side projects — from voice-to-task apps to automated workflows — without writing code. These projects became the differentiator that landed interviews and offers.

Attendees will walk away with: 
- A framework for turning daily annoyances into portfolio-worthy AI projects 
- Strategies for showcasing side projects in resumes, interviews, and LinkedIn
- Honest conversation about imposter syndrome and the mindset shift from “I’m not technical enough” to “I shipped this”
For every PM, career switcher, and woman in tech told she doesn’t have the right background, and ready to prove otherwise.

sessions.title: Cracking the SWE Career Journey: Resumes, Interviews & AI-Powered Job Search
sessions.abstract: Landing a software engineering internship or full-time role takes more than just technical skills—it takes strategy. In this practical, insight-packed session, you will learn how to navigate the entire job search process with confidence. We will cover how to find the right roles, craft standout resumes and cover letters, write effective cold emails and LinkedIn messages, and deliver a compelling 60-second elevator pitch. You will learn how to prepare for behavioral and technical interviews using frameworks like STAR, and how to approach LeetCode-style questions with clarity and confidence. We’ll also explore how to use AI tools to streamline your job search and tailor your applications. You will leave with actionable templates, sample answers, and a clear roadmap to help you land your next SWE role—whether it’s your first internship or a full-time offer.

sessions.title: The Inventor’s Edge: Building Executive Influence through Strategic Innovation
sessions.abstract:
For experienced technologists, the leap to visionary leader requires a shift in perspective. As an award-winning speaker, inventor, and best-selling author with 15 years industry experience, I have learned that leadership isn't just about solving today’s problems—it’s about protecting tomorrow’s ideas. In this session, we will explore how to identify innovation gaps within any complex system and transform those solutions into valuable intellectual property (IP).
Drawing on my journey as a multi-patent holder and WISE (Women in Science & Engineering) India ERG Leader, I will break down the strategic side of the patent process. You will learn to align technical breakthroughs with long-term business goals, overcome the imposter syndrome of inventing, and use your IP portfolio to build executive-level influence. You will leave with a "Leader’s Innovation Framework"—a strategy to turn everyday problem-solving into innovation that elevates your presence at the leadership table.

speakers.name: Richa Daga
speakers.title: Software Engineer and WISE India ERG leader

sessions.title: The Next 25 Years: Building Technology with Intention
sessions.abstract: As technologies like AI and quantum computing accelerate, the defining question of the next 25 years is not what we can build but who benefits, who participates, and whether innovation strengthens society or deepens inequality. This panel brings together leaders across frontier technology, economics, education, philanthropy, and public policy to explore how innovation can be designed with intention. Drawing lessons from history, current investments in emerging tech, and real-world examples of cross-sector collaboration, the discussion will challenge technologists to think beyond speed and scale toward responsibility, resilience, and shared prosperity. Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of the human, civic, and systems-level choices that shape the future and their role in making them.

speakers.name: Megan J. Smith
speakers.title: Entrepreneur, Engineer
speakers.company: Former U.S. Chief Technology Officer, Member National Academy of Engineering, CEO shift7

sessions.title: Beyond the Model: Crafting Human-Centered AI Experiences
sessions.abstract:
Explore the engineering and design principles behind integrating generative capabilities seamlessly across an entire operating system—from system-wide writing tools to playful visual creation like Genmoji and Image Playground. Attendees will gain insight into how deep collaboration between engineering and human domain experts (writers, designers, and artists) sets the benchmark for quality, privacy, and taste, turning raw models into intuitive, delightful everyday tools.

Key Takeaways for Attendees:
How to approach AI product development from a customer-experience-first perspective rather than tech-for-tech’s-sake.
The systems-engineering and API considerations required to weave intelligent tools natively across an entire platform.
Why human expertise, evaluation, and craftsmanship are essential to building trustworthy and expressive generative features.

sessions.title: Celebrating Latine Technologists
sessions.abstract: Vibrancy, collaboration, and community in action! Join us as we celebrate our vibrant Latine tech community and the cultural wealth we bring to the future of technology. Come connect with fellow changemakers, build meaningful professional bonds, and find inspiration in a welcoming, high-energy space dedicated to lifting up Latine voices, leadership, and success in tech.

sessions.title: The Operator's Edge: Why the Best Early-Stage Investors Understand the Product and the People Building It
sessions.abstract: As a former engineer turned early-stage investor, Ananya found that the best investors at the earliest stage can read both halves of a startup at once - the product and the people building it. She calls it the operator's edge. In this talk she breaks it into the technical read and the human read and shares how having built things herself shapes both.

sessions.title: The Portfolio Playbook: Building a Career That Rises Above AI
sessions.abstract: In an era of Agentic AI, the most resilient professional asset is multidimensional context. This context also empowers meaningful global, societal change. AI can execute tasks and synthesize information at remarkable scale, but it cannot replicate the judgment earned from launching products at Google, navigating product and policy at the White House and FTC, scaling impact through venture and non-profits at Mozilla, and going deep on hard questions in academia at Harvard. This session is a masterclass in building a Portfolio Career, turning cross-sector experience into perspective no model can reproduce, and the impact and professional leverage that comes with it.

sessions.title: AI and the 2026 Threatscape: Securing Innovation in the Age of Intelligent Adversaries
sessions.abstract:
As AI rapidly transforms the cybersecurity landscape, defenders are now facing intelligent adversaries capable of learning, adapting, and scaling attacks faster than traditional controls can respond. This session provides a technical, forward-looking exploration of the 2026 threatscape through real demonstrations, emerging research, and actionable frameworks.

We begin with a concise recap of 2025’s most significant attack trends from AI-generated phishing to identity-driven compromises before previewing the next wave of AI-powered reconnaissance, deepfake-enabled social engineering, and cloud-native exploitation. 

Participants will also see how AI can strengthen defense through behavior-based anomaly detection, data-centric security. 

We conclude with a practical four-step AI Security Readiness Roadmap Assess, Detect, Respond, Validate plus a resource toolkit enabling attendees to replicate the workflows in their own environments.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: First-Gen Career Branding: The Brand Blueprint for Students and Early-Career Professionals
sessions.abstract: This hands-on workshop helps first-gen students and early-career professionals build a personal brand that reflects their authentic story and career goals. Attendees will actively build their brand in real time—updating LinkedIn profiles, crafting an “About Me,” selecting a professional headshot, exploring banner templates, and learning what types of posts resonate for college students and early-career professionals. At the end, participants will complete the “Make Yourself Visible” LinkedIn Challenge by creating a post with a session photo, one insight learned, a new connection tagged, and a goal they’re committing to. Participants leave with strategies to amplify their voice, showcase their skills, and confidently pursue opportunities, turning their unique background into their greatest professional asset.

speakers.name: Zawadi Pilipili
speakers.title: Founder | Speaker | Gen-Z Student Leader & Advocate

sessions.title: From Paycheck to Portfolio: Your Career Wealth Strategy
sessions.abstract:
The technology sector offers competitive compensation, yet many professionals struggle to translate high salaries into lasting wealth. Without structured guidance, knowledge gaps around equity compensation, investment strategies, and financial planning limit economic security, reduce negotiation leverage, and delay major life decisions—with significant impacts on women and underrepresented professionals.
Participants will discover actionable frameworks to create investment plans, analyze equity compensation, and reverse-engineer financial goals through interactive exercises and real-world scenarios. The session incorporates risk tolerance assessments, equity tax calculations, and goal mapping techniques.

Through concrete demonstrations and implementation strategies, attendees will acquire practical methods to incorporate wealth-building practices into everyday workflows, fostering both personal financial empowerment and professional advancement.

sessions.title: Quantum Unbound: Defeating 'Harvest Now, Decrypt Later' with Post-Quantum Cryptography
sessions.abstract:
The "Quantum Threat" is a present-day risk requiring an unbound approach to cybersecurity. Adversaries currently use "Harvest Now, Decrypt Later" (HNDL) tactics to steal encrypted data today for future decryption once quantum computers mature. We walk you through the technical transition from classical RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) to the new era of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC).

We demonstrate building "Quantum-Ready" infrastructure using the latest NIST-standardized algorithms. We teach you to implement "Crypto-Agility"—the ability to switch cryptographic standards without replacing hardware or causing downtime. We provide a technical migration blueprint for unpatchable legacy systems and brittle firmware. Join us to learn how to future-proof your organization so that your technology remains resilient against the most powerful computers ever built.

sessions.title: The Visibility Gap: Why Talent Alone Won’t Get You Promoted
sessions.abstract:
You can be exceptional at what you do and still be overlooked.

In high-growth organizations, advancement is not determined by output alone. It is shaped by visibility, narrative control, and perceived influence. The professionals who rise fastest are not always the most technically capable; they are the most clearly positioned.

At senior levels, excellence is assumed, but influence must be demonstrated.

Through candid storytelling and tactical examples drawn from both corporate leadership and the creator economy, this session will unpack why visibility is a strategic leadership skill and how to intentionally build it. Attendees will leave with practical tools to clarify their personal brand, communicate impact in high-noise environments, and position themselves for executive advancement.

If you aren’t proactively shaping your narrative, someone else will.

sessions.title: Breaking Barriers: Thriving as the Only Woman in the Room
sessions.abstract:
For much of my life, I’ve often been the only woman in the room — in classrooms, boardrooms, and countless meetings. Over time, it became so familiar that I barely noticed it. But through conversations with other women, I realized that this experience can feel intimidating, isolating, and even discouraging. Too many talented women hesitate to chase opportunities simply to avoid standing out alone.
In this session, I’ll share a personal perspective on why being the only woman in the room doesn’t have to hold us back — and how it can become a source of strength. We’ll explore practical ways to reframe the experience, step into visibility with confidence, and create space for more women to join us in every room we enter.

sessions.title: AI for Career Transitions: A Reverse Prompting Framework
sessions.abstract:
Many mid-career professionals reach a point where a transition feels necessary—but the direction is unclear. Is the next step a new company, a new role, or a new industry? How does existing experience translate into realistic market opportunities?
This session introduces a practical reverse prompting framework for career transitions. Instead of using generative AI to rewrite resumes, participants will learn how to reverse-engineer role expectations, simulate hiring perspectives, identify adjacent career paths, and evaluate skill gaps against real job requirements.
Through live examples, attendees will see how tailored prompts can transform AI into a structured decision-support tool—reducing emotional bias and increasing strategic clarity. Participants will leave with a repeatable reverse prompting approach they can immediately apply to design their next career move.

sessions.title: 5 Career Moves That Accelerate Your Journey from Engineer to Technical Leader
sessions.abstract:
Promotions are rarely accidental — they follow recognizable patterns.

This session outlines five strategic career moves that accelerate leadership growth: owning ambiguous problems, influencing cross-functional teams, communicating measurable impact, mentoring intentionally, and thinking architecturally.

Attendees will leave with a clear roadmap to grow intentionally in the AI-driven tech landscape.

sessions.title: Beyond Status Updates: Making the Most of Your 1:1s with Your Manager
sessions.abstract: 1:1s with your manager can easily become status updates you dread or rush through. This session is about turning them into a space where you get real feedback, stay aligned on goals, and build the trust that makes hard conversations possible. We'll cover warning signs that your 1:1s aren't working - only project updates, avoiding tough topics, wanting to reschedule, or worrying about what will end up in your review - and how to build trust step by step, including the role of emotion in honest conversations. You'll get a practical structure for a high-impact 1:1: highlighting 2-3 wins, giving and asking for feedback tied to your goals, discussing team dynamics, and having career conversations. You'll leave with a framework and concrete prompts to use in your next 1:1.

sessions.title: Lattices, Not Ladders: Redefining Success and Navigating the Strategic Career Pivot
sessions.abstract:
As technical roles evolve and AI shifts the required skillsets, the most resilient employees are those who treat their careers as a lattice—moving laterally to gain diverse expertise and not just accepting the standard definition of success as "moving up" the career ladder. This also allows an opportunity to ensure fulfillment in your work even if it doesn’t fit the typical career path.

In this session, I will discuss how women in tech can navigate career changes as "strategic migrations" to better-aligned roles, which is something I recently went through myself when switching to a Chief of Staff role in a product organization after 18+ years in tech roles. I will challenge the audience to move away from the stigma of career changes and build their own definition of success around prioritizing fulfillment, skill acquisition, and values-based development.

sessions.title: Influence Without Authority: How Product Analysts Drive Strategy Through Metrics
sessions.abstract: Product analysts often sit at the center of critical decisions — without owning an actual product roadmap. This workshop focuses on how to use metrics as a lever for influence at both the executive and team level, and how to show up as a strategic partner rather than just a reporting function. Drawing on real experience leading cross-functional initiatives — from major strategic programs anchored in one or two critical metrics to building unified, reliable data foundations — I’ll share practical techniques for framing analyses in terms leaders care about, designing metrics that clarify trade-offs, and turning “data requests” into strategic proposals. The session will include guided exercises where attendees reframe a vague ask, outline a metrics narrative for a high-stakes decision, and map the stakeholders for their next project. We’ll also talk about influencing executive stakeholders, managing interrupts versus long-term programs, and protecting time for high-impact work. Attendees will leave with concrete scripts, templates, and confidence to lead through data and operate as a strategic partner in any role.

sessions.title: Human-in-the-Loop: A Cross-Generational Approach to Responsible Health AI
sessions.abstract:
17 years ago, at GHC2009 in Tucson, when I presented Network Security research, leveraging early ML to secure networks, my toddler daughter was in the conference childcare. Today, she is a medical student at UNISR(Milan), navigating a healthcare landscape reshaped by Large Language Models (LLMs). We return to GHC to show that the bridge between code and care is built by those who understand both the algorithm and the anatomy.This session bridges two generations to address the "Translation Gap" between algorithmic output and clinical safety.

Utilizing Kahoot and Mentimeter for interactive exercises, we analyze three high-stakes ethical pitfalls, which are hallucinated histories, encoded bias, and oversight erosion. 
By merging technical rigor with clinical intuition, we propose a "Responsible AI" framework that prioritizes the patient over the prompt.

Attendees will learn to design Human-in-the-Loop systems, ensuring AI remains a clinical assistant, not a liability.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

speakers.name: Dr Jyotsna Sharma
speakers.title: Adjunct Faculty
speakers.company: Demont Institute of Management and Technology, DUBAI

sessions.title: Designing Career Mobility Like a Product: The Reverse Mentorship Playbook
sessions.abstract: Career moves rarely fail because of skill - they fail because opportunity is invisible. In Microsoft's Azure Compute organization, we co-led a reverse mentorship pilot where a diverse group of early-career mentors coached senior leaders (mentees) by tackling real, high-level organizational challenges the leaders brought in. That flipped mentorship model became a repeatable "career mobility engine": it rapidly builds mentors' networks and turns their fresh perspectives into credibility, while delivering tangible outcomes that hiring managers recognize and value. In this talk, we share the exact operating model we used: how we designed the program like a product, and how any individual can leverage it to gain visibility, craft a stronger career narrative, and accelerate their own career transitions.

sessions.title: Infrastructure as a Catalyst: Building a 40%+ Female Engineering Team
sessions.abstract:
Hardware is often one of the most male-dominated areas in tech. So how did we intentionally build and sustain a 40%+ female engineering team in this space?

In this high-energy conversation, a manager–IC duo from NVIDIA’s Hardware Infrastructure team unpacks the real strategies behind the numbers. We’ll explore how bias shows up in hiring loops, what research says about women-led teams driving diversity, and how leadership development in niche technical domains changes pipeline outcomes. We’ll also share how principles like “the mission is the boss” and “one team” have shaped decision making and hiring strategies at scale, ensuring alignment with NVIDIA’s broader goal of building technology that delivers meaningful impact.

This session blends research, tactical hiring shifts, and honest lessons learned. Attendees will leave with actionable frameworks to influence hiring decisions, cultivate sponsorship, and build diverse teams, even in traditionally underrepresented technical fields.

sessions.title: Leaving Isn’t Failing: When Walking Away Is an Act of Leadership
sessions.abstract:
Leaving a job—especially one that is difficult or toxic—is often framed as quitting or personal failure. This panel reframes career exits as informed, values‑driven leadership decisions.
Drawing on lived experience across technology, security, and organizational leadership, panelists explore how to recognize when a role is no longer serving you, how to walk away with integrity (without burning bridges or confidence), and how to transition without shame. Attendees will gain practical tools to evaluate misalignment, reclaim agency, and tell their career story with clarity and confidence.

sessions.title: Beyond the Script: Architecting the Interview from the Inside
sessions.abstract:
The technical interview is often viewed as a high-stakes test, but for the interviewer, it is a data-collection exercise. How can you ensure the data you provide is "high-signal"? This session pulls back the curtain on the interviewer’s rubric to reveal what happens on the other side of the whiteboard.
We will move beyond the "coding grind" to explore the architectural principles of a successful interview. Attendees will learn how to transition from a reactive "task-solver" to a proactive "system architect" by mastering the art of the technical narrative. We’ll discuss how to navigate ambiguity, communicate trade-offs, and handle the dreaded "I don't know" with senior-level composure. Whether you are navigating your first technical loop or aiming for a Staff-level role, this talk provides a blueprint for turning an intimidating interrogation into a high-level technical collaboration.

sessions.title: Reinvent, Rebuild, Rise - A Playbook for Mid‑Career Technologists Leading the AI Shift
sessions.abstract: Reinvent, Rebuild, Rise is a session for mid-career and senior technologists shaping how AI is adopted, governed, and scaled across organizations. It reframes AI from a replacement risk to a transition that technologists must steward—bringing architectural judgment, enterprise context, and responsible decision-making. The talk introduces three AI-era archetypes: the Defender, the User, and the Architect of Intelligence, and argues that growth comes from adopting the Architect mindset: designing AI-enabled systems that are scalable, trustworthy, and aligned to business outcomes. Participants learn how to move from writing code to orchestrating intelligence by strengthening data foundations, setting guardrails, and engaging early in AI governance. Practical guidance covers increasing leverage, influencing technical direction, mentoring future architects, and advancing ethical, resilient, sustainable AI adoption—so technologists don’t just adapt to the shift, but lead it.

sessions.title: Bridging Bytes and Biology: Automating 3D Anthropological Topography
sessions.abstract: In physical anthropology and evolutionary biology, researchers rely on tedious, manual methods to measure tooth wear, leading to imperfect data and massive time sinks. Other times, they rely on expensive, fancy software. To solve this industry bottleneck, our team of four computer scientists developed "Topo Tooth," a production-ready web application that automates complex 3D topographical measurements. Built with Svelte and Threlte, this tool transforms raw CSV point clouds into interactive 3D meshes using Delaunay triangulation. By implementing radius-based spatial search algorithms, the software automatically identifies anatomical extrema (cusps and fossae) and calculates precise vectors, heights, and wear slopes. In this session, we will explore the architecture behind Topo Tooth, detail how we translated spatial mathematics into an interactive 3D UI, and share strategies for modernizing traditional scientific research.

sessions.title: Objection! The Algorithm Is Biased: The Woman-in-the-Loop Imperative
sessions.abstract:
The AI got it wrong. A woman in the room caught it. That's not a coincidence.
AI systems are making decisions that affect hiring, healthcare, safety, and opportunity and most of them were built, tested, and validated without women in the room. The result isn't always intentional bias. It's invisible bias. And the people most likely to catch it are the ones it affects. This panel is about one thing: women need to be in the room when AI decisions get made. Not as an afterthought. Not as a diversity checkbox. As the essential voice that determines whether an AI system is fair, contextual, and trustworthy. We'll hear from women who've been that voice, who've changed what systems did, who it served,. They'll challenge the idea that "human-in-the-loop" is a technical safeguard. It's a leadership role. And it demands exactly the skills imposter syndrome has been quietly convincing women they don't have: empathy, context, ethics, and the courage to say "wait, is this right?"

speakers.name: Amanda MacDonald
speakers.title: Area Leader, Strategic Industries Energy & HCLS, Support

speakers.name: Cindy Dea
speakers.title: Sr. Enterprise Support Manager for Frontier AI

sessions.title: The Full-Stack Portfolio: AI Investing and Private Deal Access
sessions.abstract:
While the world is obsessed with the latest LLM release, the real wealth in the AI era is being built in the basement. To truly capitalize on the AI revolution, investors must look beyond the models to the entire value chain: the power grids, the liquid cooling systems that make AI possible across 3 fundamental pillars: market opportunities, internal investment framework, and access. 

In this session, a trio of AI investors share their framework for identifying winners and losers in the AI cycle. We will move from the upstream (energy, ASICs, and SSDs) to the downstream (agentic workflows and industry-specific disruptors), focusing on how to narrow in on your own investment ethos.

In addition, we will address the insider gap and how to gain access to early stage to growth stage/pre-IPO rounds in AI companies. Focusing on strategies women can use to access deals through secondary platforms and syndicates, providing a roadmap for building a diversified AI portfolio.

speakers.name: Maryam Farooq
speakers.title: Founder of New York Artificial Intelligence (NYAI)

speakers.name: Melissa Barr
speakers.title: Staff Technical Program Manager - Machine Learning

speakers.name: Catherine Yin
speakers.title: Head of Practice, Business and Corporate

sessions.title: From Survival Mode to Sandbox Mode: Playful Career Experiments for Thriving in AI Era
sessions.abstract:
AI just rewrote your role. Multiple reorgs. Leadership churn. Many of us in tech are operating in survival mode, reactively. In this 60‑minute interactive workshop for emerging leaders, mid‑career, and managers, we’ll trade survival for Sandbox Mode: a playful, research‑backed tool to lead yourself and your team to thrive through AI pivots and reorgs. 

Using guided scenario sprints (no laptop needed), you’ll learn to spot survival reflexes, design small, safe experiments, and reframe chaos as a creative sandbox. You’ll design a 30‑day micro‑quest to stay visible and protect your promotion path, leaving with one concrete next step you can put on your calendar immediately. Because if the rules keep changing, it’s time to design your own sandbox. 

Bonus: Workshop participants will also be entered into a giveaway to win one of three seats to a popular AI x Prototyping course.

speakers.name: Natashia Tjandra
speakers.title: Director of AI Product Design & Research

sessions.title: The "Stay" Strategy: Rewriting Our Careers From the Inside
sessions.abstract:
The trend in the last few years has been "move out to move up", but what if you stayed?
This panel brings together a product manager and four engineers from different technical fields who spent 5 to 12+ years at single companies and made their boldest career moves from the inside: switching from technical IC to Engineering Manager, relocating from India to the US, pivoting from a developer role to a PM role, switching fields from disaster recovery to datacenter networking, and building AI-driven data platforms from streaming infrastructure. We'll debate the real questions mid-career technologists face: IC track vs. Management? How do you avoid being pigeonholed? How do you negotiate compensation internally? How do you pivot from being a developer to a PM role?
You'll leave with concrete playbooks: how to use tenure as a trust signal for high-risk roles, how to make your reputation portable across teams, and how to turn institutional knowledge into a career superpower and not a cage.

sessions.title: Building in Public: How Visibility and Impact Creates Opportunity in Tech
sessions.abstract:
In today’s tech landscape, opportunity is driven not only by technical skill, but by visibility and impact. Many students and early-career technologists do meaningful work that remains unseen. This interactive session explores how building in public turns invisible effort into visible signals that create career momentum.

Building in public is not self-promotion or sharing perfect outcomes—it is documenting the journey. As AI lowers the barrier to building software, what differentiates developers is their process, problem-solving, and growth. Participants will learn why mass applying to jobs makes candidates blend in, and how a strong digital presence attracts opportunities instead.

The session introduces the BUILD framework—Begin where you are, Unpack your work, Invite conversation, Leverage the right platforms, and Design for sustainability. Attendees leave with a clear visibility strategy and concrete next steps to share work authentically - focusing on progress, not perfection.

sessions.title: From Detours to Direction: Mapping Your Career Story
sessions.abstract: Career paths are rarely linear. This interactive workshop is designed for students and early-career technologists who feel unsure how to articulate their experience or explain pivots with confidence. Participants will learn how to identify transferable skills from coursework, internships, jobs, and transitions, even when those experiences seem unrelated, using a mapping exercise. This is paired with skill stacking, a practical approach to naming the combinations of technical, analytical, and human skills that differentiate candidates in interviews.

sessions.title: How to Do a Successful Career Pivot in the Age of AI — A Practical Framework
sessions.abstract: Career pivoting in an AI-driven world is bold, risky, and necessary, but most advice skips the hard parts. Two practitioners who have successfully pivoted careers in one of the most brutal job markets in recent history share their unfiltered stories and introduce the BRICK Framework: a battle-tested playbook for navigating career transitions. We cover the real cost of pivoting, the brutal challenges nobody warns you about, and a step-by-step approach to building credibility in a new domain with AI as your ally, not your threat.

sessions.title: Fear, Courage and Resilience in the Age of AI
sessions.abstract: Five careers. Multiple disciplines. Countless moments of doubt. Clara Popescu Brooks moderates a conversation with professionals who've built products, led teams, launched companies, and navigated technological upheaval firsthand. Their fields span software engineering, product management, cybersecurity, AI/ML, UX design, entrepreneurship, M&As, and agentic workflows, but the thread connecting them is simpler: they kept going when things got hard. This is that conversation: honest perspectives on uncertainty, reinvention, and resilience in the age of AI.

speakers.name: Shelly Arora
speakers.title: AI Strategy and Operations | Merger & Acquisition Integration | Wharton EMBA

speakers.name: Tony Carraballo
speakers.title: Founder at The Caraballo Group | Founder & CTO at June

sessions.title: No Single Road to Software: The Evolution of Nontraditional Career Paths
sessions.abstract:
There has never been one “right” way to start a career in tech, and today the journeys are more varied than ever. Engineers and technical leaders increasingly are finding their pathway into the field through different industries, bootcamps, vibe coding, or career transitions. 

In this conversation, Jess Lee, co-founder of dev.to is going to be exploring how the nontraditional path into technology has evolved. Our panelists each offer a unique perspective both in and out of traditional computer science programs and will discuss how the landscape is changing.

sessions.title: Forging the Future: Limitless Ambition in the Digital Age
sessions.abstract: A panel session led by USAA female executives, bringing together visionary IT leaders to explore the boundless possibilities that arise when ambition knows no limits. In an era defined by rapid digital transformation, these executives will delve into how audacious goals and forward-thinking strategies are not just aspirational but are actively shaping the technological landscape. The discussion will illuminate the "art of the possible," showcasing how a mindset of limitless ambition empowers organizations to overcome challenges, drive unprecedented innovation, and redefine what's achievable in IT. A key focus of the session will be the transformative role of women in technology. The panelists will share insights on how diverse perspectives, particularly those brought by female leaders, are crucial in not only fostering a more inclusive tech industry but also in redefining its future trajectory. They will discuss how women are actively breaking down traditional barriers, challenging the status quo, and bringing unique approaches to leadership and innovation that are essential for navigating the complexities of the digital age and creating a more equitable and dynamic technological future.

sessions.title: Decisions, Not Diagrams: How Senior Engineers Shape System Architecture
sessions.abstract:
Architecture discussions often center on diagrams, frameworks, and patterns—but the systems that endure are shaped by the decisions engineers make long before any diagram is finalized.

This session explores how senior engineers navigate high-stakes architecture decisions in real-world systems—where requirements evolve, constraints shift, and there is rarely a single “correct” answer. Instead of focusing on idealized architectures, we’ll dive into the decision-making process itself: how experienced engineers frame ambiguous problems, evaluate tradeoffs, prioritize short-term needs against long-term impact, and recognize when to revisit earlier choices.

Drawing from experience building and evolving large-scale consumer systems, this session highlights decisions that scaled successfully as well as those that required course correction—and why.

Attendees will leave with practical mental models they can apply across technology stacks to make better architecture decisions when clarity is limited and the stakes are high.

sessions.title: Leading Beyond the Build: How Volunteering and Tech Strategy Accelerate Mid-Career Growth
sessions.abstract: As technologists reach mid-career, growth increasingly depends on not just what they build, but on how they make decisions - often without direct ownership of implementation. This session explores how strategic technology and AI advisory work, combined with volunteering and social entrepreneurship, can accelerate leadership growth, while advancing inclusive innovation in STEM. Drawing on first-hand experiences with an education nonprofit in Paraguay and a First Nations social enterprise in Canada, the talk explores how assessing and recommending technology solutions within real-world constraints becomes a powerful learning experience - one that builds strategic judgment, cultural awareness, and ethical decision-making. By working in social-impact contexts beyond Silicon Valley, the talk highlights how to create meaningful impact across communities, while equipping mid-career technologists with leadership skills that translate back to enterprise and global industry settings.

sessions.title: The Human Element - Why LLMs need your Intuition
sessions.abstract:
When LLMs took the tech world by storm, many experienced developers felt a sudden, sharp sense of obsolescence. If a machine can write the code, what is left for the engineer? This session is a journey from imposter syndrome to empowerment. Through the lens of a mobile developer, I followed my natural instinct: first tinker, then dig into the roots.
By building a female-centric, cycle-synced productivity app for myself, I discovered that the most critical part of 'Prompt Engineering' isn't the mechanics—it's the human thought process behind it. Once the app was built, I went deeper into why it worked, uncovering the probabilistic nature of LLMs and how they differ from the traditional instruction sets we know. Attendees will learn how to leverage their own lived experience and foundational knowledge to steer AI outputs, moving from being a passive code-generator to an active 'Architect of Intent.'
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: AI Is Rewriting Product & Program Leadership: What Leaders Must Do Differently in 2026
sessions.abstract:
The AI era is fundamentally reshaping how products are built, scaled, and governed. Traditional roadmaps, prioritization models, and execution frameworks are no longer sufficient in a world powered by LLM , and autonomous agents. 

This session explores how product and program leaders must evolve to operate in AI-native environments. Drawing from enterprise AI transformation experience, it outlines a modern operating model for AI-powered products centered on evaluation-first development, cross-functional governance, lifecycle orchestration for agents, and risk-aware scaling. 

Key Topics:

Shifting product strategy from feature-led to capability-led design

Replacing traditional QA with structured AI evaluation frameworks

Preventing agent sprawl and fragmented experimentation

Future-proofing product leadership in AI-first enterprises
Attendees will learn how to transition from traditional models to leading intelligent, adaptive systems with clarity and strategic impact.

sessions.title: From Resume to Offer: Leveraging AI Responsibly for Career Advancement
sessions.abstract:
In 2025, AI transformed career prep—but interviewers can spot AI-assisted answers in seconds. How do you harness AI’s power without losing the authenticity that wins offers in 2026?

After interviewing hundreds of candidates at Amazon, we’ve learned this: technical skills open the door, but storytelling gets you hired. AI makes that storytelling easier—and riskier. This interactive workshop shows you how to use AI for resume optimization, interview practice, and STAR stories—while staying within ethical boundaries.

As certified interviewers, we’ve seen candidates fail by reciting AI scripts—and others succeed by using AI strategically. We’ll share insider insights and red flags that reveal inauthentic responses.

Designed for women in tech, this session tackles bias, self-advocacy, and articulating achievements with confidence. You’ll leave with practical AI tools, authentic strategies, and a 30-day action plan.

sessions.title: From Tech to Climate: The Talent Gap & Your Transition Strategy
sessions.abstract:
Climate is no longer a niche sector — it is one of the fastest-growing areas of the global economy, with demand for green talent projected to outpace supply in the coming decade. At the same time, women remain underrepresented in climate leadership and technical roles.

In this data-driven session, women in tech will examine why the climate talent gap represents a strategic career opportunity — not only a values-driven choice. Drawing on U.S. labor market research, industry reports, and lived experience transitioning into climate tech startups, this talk will highlight where demand is growing, which skills are most sought after, and how to strategically approach the transition.

Attendees will leave with:
 • A clear understanding of climate as a viable career pathway
 • A practical framework to map transferable skills to climate roles
 • Concrete next steps to begin exploring the sector with confidence

sessions.title: Unlocking Big Tech: The Complete Interview Playbook for Engineers, SDMs & PMs
sessions.abstract:
Landing a role at top tech companies today requires more than technical competence — it demands strategic preparation and the ability to leverage AI effectively.

We will break down the three core pillars of Big Tech interviews — Data Structures & Algorithms, System Design, and Behavioral Excellence - clarifying what interviewers actually evaluate and how expectations vary across roles. We will then extend this foundation into the modern hiring landscape, where AI has become a powerful preparation partner. You will learn how to effectively use generative AI to sharpen your technical readiness, refine your narratives, and build a repeatable interview preparation workflow.

sessions.title: From Internship to Career: Maximizing Opportunities at Grace Hopper
sessions.abstract: Grace Hopper is an unparalleled platform for career growth, networking, and job opportunities. But making the most of it requires more than just attending sessions. In this talk, I’ll share firsthand insights on how to leverage GHC to land internships, secure full-time offers, and build long-term connections. Drawing from my personal experience of using GHC to secure an internship and ultimately land a full-time position at Bank of America, I’ll provide actionable advice on effective networking, crafting a strong personal brand, and translating conference experiences into real-world opportunities. From engaging with recruiters to leveraging mentorship, this session will cover the crucial steps to turn Grace Hopper into a career-launching experience.

sessions.title: The Future of Job Applications: Build Your Avatar
sessions.abstract:
Recruiters review resumes in seconds, turning rich experience into static PDFs that can’t answer real questions. Hiring deserves conversation.

In this hands‑on workshop, participants build a professional conversational AI avatar that represents them in real time. Using RAG, voice synthesis, and personality modelling, attendees transform their experience into an interactive digital presence.

Participants leave with a working AI avatar and practical skills for building conversational AI applications.

sessions.title: Beyond the Vibe Check: Evaluating Reliable AI Assistants in Production
sessions.abstract:
AI systems rarely fail with visible errors. They fail with confidence. 

A RAG assistant that worked yesterday can quietly degrade after a prompt edit, embedding update, or tool configuration change. It continues generating fluent answers. It simply stops being reliable. Without structured evaluation, these regressions are often discovered by users rather than engineers. 

Most conversations about AI evaluation focus on model benchmarks. This session focuses on production systems. We will examine how to evaluate retrieval quality, groundedness, tool-calling behavior, and regression risk in real deployments. If you are building copilots, assistants, or AI-powered features, this talk offers a systematic approach to measuring reliability before failures reach your customers.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Beyond Models: The 3 Pillars of Data Science
sessions.abstract:
When we think Data Science, we picture crunching numbers, digging into massive datasets, and building models. But to truly steer a company toward being data-driven, you need someone who can speak for the data, bring an analytical lens to every conversation, and hold the line between what the data shows and what the room wants it to show. It's about influencing decisions before a model is ever built, designing metrics that actually measure what matters, and making your findings land with stakeholders who never asked for them.

The session covers three pillars most Data Scientists learn the hard way: Leadership, Strategy, and Communication. Getting into the right conversations, measuring the right things, and turning analysis into decisions. Grounded entirely in personal experience, sharing what worked, what did not, and what I would do differently.

If any of this sounds familiar, this talk is for you!

sessions.title: Architecting Autonomy: How Mentorship Can Multiply Your Impact
sessions.abstract:
Mentorship shapes careers in two directions. As a mentor, you get to support someone's growth and help shape their career. As a mentee, you get to leverage someone else's experience to learn and chart your own path toward independence. Mentorship can be so powerful, but is often treated as a secondary priority instead of something built with intention. In this session, we'll explore a three phase approach to mentorship: from building trust and providing hands-on guidance, to fostering independent judgment, to creating opportunities for visibility and leadership. We'll discuss: As a mentor:

How do you support growth without creating dependency?

How do you know when advocacy accelerates growth versus undermines ownership?

How do you build a healthy support system for your mentee while juggling multiple priorities?

As a mentee:

How do you frame questions when you don't know what you don't know?

How do you decide when to ask for help versus figure it out yourself?

How do you turn feedback into action instead of just acknowledging it and moving on?

Join me as we learn what it means to architect autonomy, by supporting someone today to prepare them to thrive independently tomorrow.

sessions.title: Giving Girls Their Hidden History: The Great Women Portrait Project
sessions.abstract:
The presentation focuses on the effect that creative projects can have on the gender gap in STEM.

Specifically, the focus will be on the creation, and evolution of The Great Women Portrait Project, which uses art, history and technology to reveal STEM’s historic female pioneers. 
Highlights include:
• how Anita Borg was a catalyst for the creation of The Project;
• how The Project is moving beyond boardrooms, into classrooms, using AI with Art
• how companies like Lockheed Martin, Sanofi, AstraZeneca and others are embracing the Project 
• how a growing ‘constellation’ of contemporary STEM leaders and pioneers - including first woman in Mission Control for NASA, AstraZeneca’s global CFO Aradhana Sarin, and the late mathematician Gladys West, whose work helped enable the creation of GPS – have been helping to shape interest and engagement in The Great Women Portrait Project, and 
• demo of AI Great Woman Portrait

speakers.name: Jo Napier
speakers.title: Executive Producer, Great Women Portrait Project

sessions.title: From Chicago to Tokyo: Standing Out Through Communication Gave Us a Competitive Advantage in Tech
sessions.abstract: Communication and initiative can turn unlikely ideas into real opportunities. This session explores how communication and initiative create opportunities beyond technical skills through two “firsts” of a Fortune 500 company. One presenter became the first U.S. intern placed in the company’s Japan office after advocating at age 19 for an opportunity that had never existed. The other, the company’s Chief Communications Officer, built a path to becoming an expat in Japan through executive leadership and global strategy. Despite differences in seniority, both journeys were driven by proactively communicating ambition, aligning it with organizational value, and advocating for opportunities until they became reality. Together, this session shows that while technical skills may open doors, clear communication and strategic visibility create new ones.

speakers.name: Atmikha Jeeju
speakers.title: Former IT Intern, Hitachi (HIES)
speakers.company: MSIS Student, Kelley School of Business, Indiana University Bloomington

sessions.title: Software Engineering to Outcome Engineering: Coding Is Dead. Engineering Isn't.
sessions.abstract: In the era of agentic programming, what does it mean to be a software engineer? Software engineering was never just about writing code, but we spent so long typing that we forgot. This session will go over how the role of a software engineer is becoming more outcome-centric. This talk introduces Outcome Engineering: why the role is shifting from producing code to defining outcomes, and how we should make that shift deliberately. We will cover why this matters now with the 99% trap (agent code that looks done but hides production-breaking flaws) and models that keep getting better at the easy part while the hard part stays human. Attendees will leave with a concrete 5 step workflow: (1) defining outcomes before touching an agent, (2) context engineering, (3) defining intent and roles, (4) doubling down on testing and risk assessment, and (5) mastering the new debugging loop. We will do some live demos, audience polling, and go over frameworks anyone can apply daily.

sessions.title: The Transferable Skills Matrix: Pivot Your Way into Tech
sessions.abstract: Many people define themselves by their industry - for example: "I am a non-profit researcher." They often struggle to translate their industry-specific skills into career changing opportunities. This can be limiting if one’s goal is to move into a different industry or attempt a career change laterally. This workshop is geared towards teaching how to redefine professional skills by functions (rather than industries) in order to enable lateral career moves into the Tech industry. The specific goal of this workshop is to empower folks to redefine their own career journeys and take practical steps in shaping their CV or resume for the Tech world via drafting their own Transferable Skills Matrix. We will review specific prompts for AI tooling to help the audience members in articulating their own Tech-specific superpowers. The audience will receive their own Transferable Skills Matrix worksheet that will enable them to build out their Tech-first CV outline.

sessions.title: Actually Tho: Tech - Decoding the Buzzwords
sessions.abstract:
In an industry overflowing with jargon, “Decoding the Buzzwords” is a conference track dedicated to cutting
through the noise and getting to the truth behind today’s most overused technology terms. Too often, words
like AInative, platform, digital transformation, or zero trust become catchall phrases that lose meaning through
repetition. This track breaks each concept down to its essentials—what it actually is, what problem it solves, and
what it doesn’t do despite vendor hype. Sessions focus on clarity and practical understanding, translating
complex terminology into real-world implications for architects, delivery leads, and business stakeholders.
Whether it’s distinguishing automation from intelligence, understanding the difference between cloudenabled
and cloudoptimized, or unpacking what “modernization” really requires, attendees walk away with grounded
definitions, shared language, and a toolkit for more precise conversations. Ultimately, this track empowers

sessions.title: AI Adoption Without Chaos: Turning Manual Work into Scalable Intelligence
sessions.abstract:
AI adoption is stalling inside most organizations, not because the technology is immature, but because the AI adoption model is not designed for the everyday employee. Teams are overloaded with manual work, and redundant processes, while leaders push tools without changing how work actually flows.
This session introduces the a practical approach and framework for deploying AI as a digital workforce that reduces manual effort, eliminates task duplication, and accelerates execution across teams.
You will learn how organizations can map real workflows, define clear AI handoffs, and install AI solutions that handle repeatable work in any department. We will cover current industry trends in agentic AI, research-backed productivity gains, and a step-by-step strategy for reducing staff dependencies without mass layoffs or burnout.
Attendees will leave with a clear model for enterprise-ready AI adoption that drives efficiency, speed, and measurable business outcomes.

sessions.title: Scaling Mindsets: A Reset for Growing or Stuck Cross-Functional Teams
sessions.abstract:
Even strong teams hit phases where things feel off. Priorities blur. Ownership gets fuzzy. Cross functional work becomes heavier than it should be. Leaders feel the friction, and ICs feel the lack of direction.

As cross functional tech leaders supporting large enterprise partnerships, we’ve seen this pattern repeat across launch environments, mature businesses, and community organizations alike. Traditional exercises often create discussion but rarely yield results.

In this hands on workshop, we’ll introduce “Lean Action Workout,” a framework designed to help teams surface root friction, align on a shared future state, and translate that alignment into a prioritized, executable roadmap in a single session.

This approach is especially powerful for women and underrepresented leaders, who are often expected to absorb friction and “just make it work”. Rather than carrying invisible labor, this provides a structured way to create clarity that is shared, visible, and sustainable.

sessions.title: Women in Advanced Compute: Breaking Barriers in HPC & Quantum
sessions.abstract: Advanced computing fields remain heavily male-dominated, yet women are driving breakthrough innovations in HPC, quantum computing, and AI infrastructure. This panel features women leaders sharing their journeys, discussing barriers they've overcome, and offering strategies for building inclusive teams in highly technical domains. Explore mentorship approaches, advocacy tactics, and organizational changes needed to create equitable opportunities in the future of computing.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

speakers.name: Vanessa Hernandez Mateos
speakers.title: AWS Senior Solutions Architect for Public Sector

sessions.title: Trailblazers Show Us the Way: Women Belong in Technology
sessions.abstract: Women have led the creation of technology from the very earliest days. With women trailblazers from Ada Lovelace to Fei Fei Li and everyone in between, we can see and be inspired by their creativity and their determination to make a difference. For decades the stories of women's achievements in technology were hidden, but today there's a groundwell of effort to bring their stories to light. We draw strength from their achievements: not only are women capable of achieving innovation and discovery, but also our presence is essential, and truly the future depends on us. The right role models take us beyond showing us how to live, thru their example the principles we know in our heads take root in our hearts. With the stories of these trailblazers, we can really believe in our hearts that we belong here!

speakers.name: Jane Mack-Crane
speakers.title: Computer Science Technologist and Sales; Co-President Vision 1948

sessions.title: Architect Your Influence: How Senior ICs Drive Change Without Authority
sessions.abstract:
As a senior IC, you are responsible for outcomes across teams you don't manage, in organizations you don't control. Your power comes from influence, not authority, and that requires a completely different playbook.
Most senior ICs learn this the hard way. You write the perfect architecture proposal. You present the data. You are clearly right. And nothing happens. Because being right is not the same as being effective.
This session unpacks how senior ICs actually drive change at scale: building architectural authority, navigating cross-org politics without a title, and the counterintuitive strategies that turn "just an IC" into the person leadership turns to when direction is unclear.
You will leave with a practical influence toolkit: frameworks for RFC-driven consensus, stakeholder mapping strategies, and techniques for making your impact visible. This is not theory. This is fieldcraft.

sessions.title: AI + Human Collaboration: Redefining Roles in the AI Era
sessions.abstract:
Every generation has feared the machine. Every generation has adapted. This one is no different — except the stakes are higher, the pace is faster, and the opportunity is bigger than ever.

AI isn't coming for your job. It's coming for the parts of your job you never loved — the repetitive, the predictable, the draining. What remains is the work only you can do: the judgment calls, the ethical guardrails, the creative leaps, the human connections that no model can replicate. But thriving in this new reality isn't accidental. It requires intention.

In this session, we cut through the hype and get practical. Drawing on real-world examples across engineering, healthcare, and business operations, we'll map exactly where AI augments human capability — and where human expertise remains non-negotiable. You'll walk away with concrete frameworks for identifying where you add irreplaceable value, building the skills that matter in an AI-assisted world, and designing workflows where you direct AI rather than compete with it. Whether you're an engineer, analyst, product manager, or quality assurance professional — this session is your strategic playbook for the AI era. Not survival. Mastery.

sessions.title: Low-Code Enterprise AI with Copilot Studio & Power Automate
sessions.abstract: Enterprise AI is evolving from chatbots to autonomous agents that execute workflows across business systems. However, many technologists lack a clear framework for designing and scaling these agents responsibly. This session demonstrates how to build production-ready AI agents using Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Automate, combining LLM reasoning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), OCR, and automation workflows. Presented by an AI/ML engineer and a Power Platform automation specialist, Attendees will learn to design low-code agents, connect enterprise data, orchestrate actions, and deploy safely. Through architecture walkthroughs and a live demo, we show how AI agents enable document intelligence, decision support, and workflow automation. Participants leave with practical patterns, integration strategies, and guidance for enterprise adoption.

speakers.name: Aditi Singh
speakers.title: Research Lead / Assistant College Lecturer
speakers.company: Women in AI / Cleveland State University

sessions.title: The Open-Source Edge: When Sharing Your Code Becomes Your Startup Moat
sessions.abstract: Open source is not a feel-good choice, it can be a deliberate business strategy. This talk offers a decision framework for founders and builders to choose what to open, what to keep proprietary, and how to turn transparency into trust, adoption, and distribution. We will cover licensing basics, community building loops, product boundaries (core vs extensions), monetization paths (hosted, support, enterprise, services), and the real risks: maintenance load, competition, and security. You will leave with a playbook to evaluate if open source is your competitive advantage and how to execute it without losing your edge.

sessions.title: Building Regional Economic Futures Through Tech: The Power and Practice of Public Private Partnerships
sessions.abstract:
Regions are increasingly competing on their ability to align business, government, higher education, and philanthropy around tech-driven growth. And yet the toughest barriers—talent, infrastructure, equity, and coordination—can’t be solved by any single sector.

In this panel, leaders from P33 Chicago and a Joint Venture Silicon Valley share how they design public–private partnerships (PPPs) that deliver durable regional outcomes. The conversation moves beyond success stories into the practical work: governance, accountability, data, funding, and execution, plus the tradeoffs required to move with speed without losing legitimacy.

Attendees will leave with a transferable playbook for building and governing cross-sector coalitions, concrete questions to diagnose when PPPs help (or hinder), and examples of how regions translate shared strategy into programs, talent pipelines, and investments.

speakers.name: Megan J. Smith
speakers.title: Entrepreneur, Engineer
speakers.company: Former U.S. Chief Technology Officer, Member National Academy of Engineering, CEO shift7

sessions.title: Building Tech with Purpose
sessions.abstract:
What does it mean to build technology that truly matters? At Abbott, innovation goes beyond code, systems, or devices—it’s about improving lives around the world.
In this panel, you’ll hear from professionals across Abbott who are shaping meaningful careers at the intersection of technology, healthcare, and global impact. From digital platforms and data analytics to medical devices and life-saving diagnostics, our panelists will share how their work directly contributes to advancing patient care, expanding access, and driving better outcomes worldwide.
Whether you’re early in your career or looking to pivot toward purpose-driven work, this discussion will offer insight into the diverse career paths within Abbott, the skills that matter, and how you can make a tangible difference through technology.
Join us to explore how building tech with purpose isn’t just a mission—it’s a career.

speakers.name: Alex Mandl
speakers.title: IT Director, Data, Analytics and AI Solutions

sessions.title: Hands on Banking
sessions.abstract: Hands on Banking® is an interactive financial education program designed to help attendees build practical money management skills. Through a realistic budgeting simulation, participants take on an assigned profile with a unique salary and financial situation, then make monthly spending and saving decisions. The experience challenges attendees to balance competing financial priorities, navigate unexpected expenses, and understand the impact of everyday financial choices on their overall financial well-being.

sessions.title: Stop Waiting for Opportunities: Learn How to Ask for What You Want at Work
sessions.abstract:
In this talk, Chaitali Narla, Managing Vice President in Card Technology at Capital One, shares the skills she’s learned to help female technologists advance in their careers by asking for what they want at work. Chaitali grew up in a “guess culture” in India where asking for something is often avoided unless a "yes" is likely, as it's considered rude to force a "no." This contrasts sharply with corporate "ask culture," where not asking can mean missing out on opportunities. Chaitali will share learnable skills to ask for needs across several dimensions: professional development, leadership opportunities, strategic career moves, technical upskilling, project and resource management, and work-life balance. Participants will leave with a concrete framework and a "flip-book" of asking scripts for various work situations.

Learn more about this topic in Chaitali’s article “Asking as a Skill.”

sessions.title: Personal Growth Through Positivity, PIE, and Purpose: A Framework for Empowering Technical Women
sessions.abstract:
Abstract:
Personal and professional growth is deeply influenced by how we frame challenges, communicate, show up, and create impact. This session explores how positivity, cognitive reframing, and the PIE model (Performance, Image, Exposure) can be used by women in technology to develop confidence, expand influence, and accelerate career growth. Drawing from behavioral science, leadership concepts, and real-world applications, the talk provides actionable techniques such as positive priming, feed-forward, reframing, personal brand development, and strategic exposure that help attendees unlock their potential. Participants will leave with a practical, repeatable framework to strengthen self-awareness, improve communication, and build a career strategy aligned with purpose and impact.

speakers.name: Shawn McCarthy
speakers.title: Vice President, Architecture, Global Wealth and Asset Management Technology

sessions.title: Leadership Is Being Rewritten and Women Get to Write the Next Chapter
sessions.abstract: Leadership is evolving faster than most organizations are prepared for. AI is reshaping how work gets done, hierarchies are flattening, trust is strained, and burnout is real. The leadership models many of us were taught no longer match the reality we are leading in today. This session reframes leadership for the moment we are in. Grounded in executive experience, current research, and a human-centered approach, this talk explores why traditional leadership approaches are breaking down and what is emerging in their place. It highlights why women are uniquely positioned to lead in this next era by fully owning the strengths they already bring. Participants will leave with clarity on how leadership is being rewritten, practical language to articulate their leadership value with confidence, and a modern framework for leading with clarity, courage, and connection in an AI-driven world. This is not about fixing yourself. It is about stepping into leadership and shaping what comes next.

sessions.title: Why Is My Brain Wired Like This? Understanding Neurodivergence in Tech
sessions.abstract:
Traditional productivity advice assumes everyone’s brain works the same way and that willpower can overcome any challenge—but what happens when your brain doesn’t fit that mold? Mashal shares her personal journey navigating OCD-related symptoms and trichotillomania in tech to help attendees better understand how neurodivergent brains are wired differently, and why common approaches to focus and productivity often fail.
Grounded in neuroscience and real-world experience, this session introduces practical regulation strategies and frameworks for building sustainable workflows that work with your brain, not against it. Drawing on insights from Microsoft’s Neurodiversity Leadership team and examples of how neurodivergent users are shaping the use of AI tools like Copilot, Mashal shows how understanding cognitive differences not only supports individual sustainability—but is actively driving innovation in inclusive workplace technology.

sessions.title: ​Meet, Greet, Repeat. Networking Skills to Build Real Connections
sessions.abstract:
You could watch a training video in pajamas, so why show up in person? You want real connections that change your career. In a world where AI blurs reality, face-to-face interactions give you an edge no online course can.

Whether you're an introvert or extrovert, you're in the right place. We'll set your conference goal and make networking delightful. How do you keep conversations going? Escape chats going nowhere without being rude? Make connections that last beyond today?

We'll tackle these questions and more. You'll gain practical tips for engaging conversation, memorable connections, and navigating networking situations. This conference favorite helps people of all comfort levels with straightforward tactics. You won't just listen; you'll practice immediately in this interactive event. You might leave with your first new connection. Having structure will boost your confidence and help you maximize this and every event.

speakers.name: Annie Flippo
speakers.title: VP of AI and Data Science

sessions.title: Navigating from Operational to Strategic: Ops Hero to Strategy Star
sessions.abstract:
Women seeking to transition from operational to strategic roles must proactively build their strategic portfolios and overcome the internal and generic perceptions. 

This involves:
1. Seeking Diverse Experiences: Taking positions that build diverse but transferable skill sets, especially early in careers. Women should focus on roles that provide exposure to revenue generation, business development, and profit-and-loss responsibility. 

2. Strategic Career Planning: Developing a comprehensive strategy that includes clear objectives, timeline development, and risk assessment. This plan should specifically target strategic roles and the competencies required for them. Craft a "Pivot Plan" with timelines, risks, and AI-governance competencies.

3. Visibility and Recognition: Actively promoting achievements and contributions within the organization through presentations, speaking engagements, and leadership roles. must articulate their value proposition clearly and confidently.

sessions.title: Breaking Into Tech with a Liberal Arts Degree
sessions.abstract:
Every year, early-career professionals with liberal arts degrees are told the same thing: “If you want to work in tech, learn to code.” It’s incomplete advice — and often the wrong advice. After managing eight job families and conducting more than 350 interviews at Amazon, we’ve seen how hiring decisions are actually made. Technical pedigree is rarely the deciding factor. Clear evidence of impact, structured thinking, and business value are.

Liberal arts graduates are not underqualified. They are often mispositioned. This session is a tactical, no-fluff playbook for early-career professionals who want to break into tech without apologizing for their background or overcorrecting with unnecessary credentials.

You’ll leave knowing exactly:
• What hiring managers actually look for
• How to translate your degree into competitive positioning
• Which skills to build (and which you can ignore)
• How to establish credibility in your first technical role

speakers.name: Maria Dangles
speakers.title: Technical Advisor to the VP of WW Pricing and Promotions

sessions.title: UnderThinking
sessions.abstract:
Do you second-guess decisions, hesitate to speak up, or feel overwhelmed by constant mental chatter? Technologists are expected to think deeply while still moving work forward, but overthinking can slow progress and cloud judgment.

This session explores the habits and mindsets that keep you stuck and provides simple, practical tools to help you move forward. You'll learn how to identify your triggers, evaluate the trade-offs between action and safety, push past fear and perfectionism, take confident leaps, and build a strong support system.

Leave with greater self-awareness and actionable techniques to make decisions and take action with confidence. Whether overthinking is a frequent challenge or you simply want more clarity, you'll learn how to recognize common triggers and navigate uncertainty with greater confidence and ease.

sessions.title: Nutritious vs. Delicious: A Health Check for AI Model Content
sessions.abstract:
Our AI children are picking up lollipops off the floor, and this session is all about teaching you when and how to say "Don't lick that!" 

In more detail, this session is about work our team has done to identify when a website, or any tokenized dataset, may be polluted, or detrimental to the quality of popular open-weight LLMs. We begin with all the background you need to understand the problem, including how modern agentic LLM updating differs from traditional ML updates. We then will have an audience participation round, where we let the audience test whether or not they can easily identify pages that are helpful (Nutritious) or harmful (Delicious) for a model to train on. Next, we discuss our original research into three techniques to automatically determine the nutritiousness of a webpage before it is crawled. Finally, we conclude with a recap and takeaways, leaving the audience with a much better understanding of what AI model pollution is and how to fix it.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: AI Raised the Bar: Redefining Job-Readiness for Entry-Level Engineers
sessions.abstract:
AI is not lowering the bar for entry-level engineers. It is raising it.

In the past, junior engineers were expected to write boilerplate code, build CRUD APIs, and complete small feature tickets. Today, AI can generate much of that instantly. So what does “job-ready” mean now?

This session explores how AI is reshaping expectations for early-career engineers and why traditional definitions of entry-level work are rapidly changing. Instead of competing on syntax, engineers must differentiate through systems thinking: architecture decisions, data modeling, scalability, tradeoffs, and ownership.

Attendees will learn how to use AI as a development accelerator while building deeper engineering judgment and how to position themselves competitively in a shifting hiring landscape.

sessions.title: The Executive's Edge: Emotional Intelligence in a World of AI and Automation
sessions.abstract:
An interactive, hands-on workshop that helps senior leaders build practical emotional intelligence skills for navigating AI disruption. As organizations adopt LLMs and generative AI, teams face anxiety, disconnection, and pressure to prioritize technical skills over human capabilities. This session strengthens self-awareness, empathy, and emotional regulation—skills that are essential for sustainable performance.

Through four experiential activities, participants expand their emotional vocabulary, identify personal triggers and regulation strategies, practice cross-industry empathy, and learn how to create psychological safety on AI-era teams. Small, diverse breakouts encourage candid dialogue and meaningful peer connection.

Participants leave with actionable tools, including a trigger map, empathy assessment, and psychological safety action plan, plus a peer network to support talent retention and effective leadership in a tech-disrupted environment.

sessions.title: The Solo Explorer’s Guide to SRE: Navigating the Unknown with AI
sessions.abstract:
In the world of Site Reliability Engineering, an outage is often a journey into the unknown. This session introduces the Solo Explorer Mindset, a framework for navigating high-pressure system failures. We will explore how the transition from a "survival" mindset to a "wellness" mindset is powered by the Digital Compass: AI. Drawing from experience as a Senior SRE at Microsoft, the speaker will demonstrate how to build automation that identifies patterns between Error Codes and APIs, effectively filtering out system noise.

Key Technical Deep Dives:
The Explorer Mindset: How to cultivate the psychological resilience needed for solo incident response and ‘uncharted’ system debugging.

Building the Digital Compass: Practical strategies for integrating AI (LLMs/MCP servers) into alerting logic to identify ‘errorCode + API’ patterns.

From Survival to Wellness: Using AI-driven predictive reliability to move from reactive firefighting to proactive maintenance.

sessions.title: Leading with Both Sides: The Business-Creative Hyphenate
sessions.abstract:
More professionals than ever are combining business acumen with creative ambition, choosing careers that embrace both. This conversation explores what it takes to lead in corporate spaces and pursue creative passions with purpose. Hear from leaders who’ve scaled brands, launched movements, and built new narratives—without giving up parts of themselves to fit the mold.

Takeaways:
1. How to successfully navigate dual career paths across corporate and creative industries without "starting over"
2. Tactics to integrate creative identity into your professional brand and leadership style
3. How corporate-to-creative leaders are reshaping success, innovation, and the future of work
