sessions.title: Cachémon, I Choose You! Protecting the User Experience in Distributed Systems Under Stress
sessions.abstract:
Distributed systems can feel like a boss battle, so we teach them like one.

Step into the role of an on-call engineer keeping a large-scale platform alive during high-stake incidents. In this interactive workshop, your system is pushed to its limits through escalating gym battles inspired by real failure scenarios: from traffic surges to partial outages and retry storms.

Working in teams, you will assemble a lineup of Pokémon-inspired component cards to reconfigure your system and see how it responds. Earn badges for diagnosing failures and evolving system behavior under pressure.

You will leave with a practical framework for reasoning about distributed systems, along with component cards that capture key tradeoffs, failure modes, and system guarantees. You will be better equipped to ask the right questions, interpret system signals, and confidently explain architectural choices in interviews, on-call situations, and design discussions.

sessions.title: Value Based Leadership
sessions.abstract:
Value-Based Leadership explores how leadership becomes more authentic, effective, and sustainable when it is grounded in personal core values. While everyone has a set of values, many people have not taken the time to identify them clearly or examine how those values show up in everyday decisions. Strong leaders do more than understand their values, they learn how to communicate them, live them consistently, and use them to guide how they lead teams, navigate challenges, and build trust. This session will help attendees reflect on the connection between self-awareness and leadership, and show how values can become a practical foundation for leading with intention.

Attendees will be able to:

  - Discover personal core values

  - Check value alignment

  - Apply their set of values to their leadership

sessions.title: A Cross-Functional Conversation on AI, Collaboration, and the New Rules of Building Product
sessions.abstract:
Every team claims they’re “using AI.” But what does that actually look like when a product manager, a designer, and an engineer sit in the same room and try to ship a feature together?
At Rubrik, we build a cloud data security platform with a frontend serving hundreds of engineers. Over the past year, AI tools have reshaped not just how we write code, but how we write product specs, how we prototype designs, and how we hand off work between disciplines. Some of those changes were breakthroughs. Others created new friction we didn’t expect.
In this panel, three practitioners share what actually changed in their daily workflows — with honest before-and-after comparisons — and what surprised them about how AI shifted the dynamics between their roles.

sessions.title: The Mid-Career "Micro-Pivot": Upskilling in the Gaps of a Busy Life
sessions.abstract:
Research shows women executives are often AI-hesitant due to the 'Double Burden' of home and work, a time constraint that leaves no room for upskilling. This session cuts through the noise to offer The 15-Minute AI Executive: Upskilling in the Gaps of a Busy Life, a high-level roadmap for busy senior leaders. We reject the 'back-to-school' mentality and focus on practical strategies to achieve technical relevance, not just through professional advancement, but by creating the space and time for yourself to be more productive.
Our model centers on Micro-learning and leveraging professional Sponsorship (social capital) to gain crucial AI exposure without needing a second degree. This framework teaches you to strategically apply new skills in both your professional and personal life, enhancing overall productivity while protecting your personal time. Speakers will share their personal experiences and demonstrate exactly how they adopted this "Learning in the Flow of Work" guide

sessions.title: Scaling Cloud-Native Multi-Agent Systems for Investment Research on AWS
sessions.abstract:
The financial services industry is undergoing a transformation driven by AI — and investment research is at the center of it. This session explores how to design, build, and scale multi-agent systems on AWS to automate the investment research workflow for financial firms.

We walk through a cloud-native architecture orchestrating specialized AI agents — Market Intelligence, CRM, Stock Data, and Document agents — using Amazon Bedrock, Strands Agents, MCP and A2A protocols with Bedrock AgentCore. These agents collaborate to extract real-time market signals, query structured financial data using hybrid approaches, and generate intelligent investment reports.

In this session, we’ll break down the natural language query performance problem and reveal the specific blueprint used to achieve significant latency improvements. Discover how to implement hybrid retrieval architectures, schema pre-loading, and query validation patterns to deliver the near real-time responses required for scaling AI agents.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: The Trust Gap: Architecting Explainable AI to Bridge the Divide Between Black Box & High-Adoption AI
sessions.abstract:
The "Trust Gap" is the silent killer of enterprise AI. As we move toward a world of Agentic AI, we face "Algorithm Aversion" - a psychological barrier where one AI hallucination destroys more trust than a dozen human errors. For builders, "Ethical AI" is no longer a checkbox; it is the ultimate driver of user retention and ROI.
This session introduces the T.R.U.S.T. Framework (Transparency, Reliability, User-Agency, Safety, Traceability). We move beyond theory into the technical "how-to" of Explainable AI (XAI). We’ll deconstruct how to lead cross-functional "Red-Teaming" for bias, implement "Guardrail Layers" in your stack, and design human-in-the-loop orchestration that actually scales. Attendees will leave with a technical blueprint to transform "Black Box" models into production-ready ecosystems that users actually trust.

sessions.title: $1.3 Billion Spent, 3% Gained: Women Don't Need Inclusion in AI - They Need to Own It
sessions.abstract:
We've spent $1.3 billion over 20 years to increase women in tech and grown CS female graduates by just 3%. With AI reshaping every industry, women are the largest group at risk of being left behind, and the economic cost is staggering.
But the answer isn't more of the same. Research on minoritymajority dynamics shows that when underrepresented groups consolidate, lead with economic value, and drive innovation, they become impossible to ignore. Women must lead the AI revolution not just advocate for inclusion.
This panel brings together leaders across AI product development, workforce investment, and venture funding to share actionable strategies mid-career women can use now: driving AI adoption within their organizations, directing investment toward women-led AI ventures, and positioning themselves at the center of the AI buildout. Attendees will leave with a practical framework for shifting from representation to economic leadership -making women indispensable to the future of AI.

sessions.title: At the Helm: Own Your Brand, Voice, and Influence
sessions.abstract: Join us for an engaging panel discussion with women leaders across technical and managerial disciplines at Amazon. Drawing from diverse career journeys and cross-functional expertise , this session explores the strategic dimensions of leadership advancement—from intentionally building your professional brand to navigating unconscious bias as you progress to senior roles.

sessions.title: Beyond the "No": Scaling Resilience and Engineering a Gen AI Career
sessions.abstract:
In a hyper-competitive tech landscape, the bridge between a stunning AI prototype and a production-grade system is paved with continuous iteration. The exact same rule applies to our careers; a professional rejection is not a dead end, but vital training data.

As an industry leader, Cloud Research leverages advanced Generative AI to revolutionize data quality, automate complex research workflows, and scale high-fidelity behavioral insights. Representing their engineering front lines, this session delivers a battle-tested blueprint for breaking into and thriving in the Gen AI space. We will deconstruct the practical roadmap every aspiring practitioner needs—from mastering core LLM toolchains to establishing frameworks for rapid technical upskilling. Attendees will walk away knowing how to move from AI consumer to AI builder, transforming both industry setbacks and modern AI tools into platforms for massive career acceleration.

sessions.title: Thriving in the Messy Middle: A Playbook for Modernizing Products in the AI Era
sessions.abstract:
The tech industry often romanticizes "0 to 1" innovation, but the reality for most builders is stepping onto a moving train. We aren't working on blank canvases; we are inheriting existing products with established users, deep-rooted technical debt, and rigid infrastructures. This is the "Messy Middle" - the high-stakes challenge of evolving a product that is already in flight.
In the AI era, this challenge has intensified. How do you integrate probabilistic AI features into a deterministic legacy platform? How do you navigate the "mess" of iterating on a product you didn't start, while the technology itself is shifting beneath you? This session provides a survival guide for the "Builders" - the PMs, engineers, and designers who thrive in the complexity of 1 to N. We will explore a strategic playbook for mastering the iterative grind, managing stakeholder expectations in the face of ambiguity, and ensuring that AI becomes a tool for evolution rather than just more tech debt.

sessions.title: The Concurrency Crisis: Engineering a High-Stakes Career While Honoring Personal Life
sessions.abstract:
The generative AI boom has left the industry in an overdrive, creating "Double FOMO": the fear of missing the next breakthrough while personal milestones sit in a "Low Priority" backlog. We’re told to ship now and sleep eventually! As a Silicon Timing engineer at NVIDIA, I ensure GPU signals reach their destination at the exact picosecond required. But the hardest timing to close isn’t on silicon—it’s the gap between professional roadmaps and our actual lives. 
Forget the "work-life balance" cliché (which usually means answering Slack from a treadmill), this session introduces Concurrency Strategies: architectural practices for running career growth and personal milestones in parallel, not in serial conflict. We’ll explore identifying "Personal Critical Path," using "Micro-Learning" to stay relevant without burnout, and leveraging deep-tech expertise as a career safety net. Stop surviving the hype cycle and start architecting a career that respects both innovation and the human roadmap.

sessions.title: SWE interview Toolkit: A 45 Day Framework for FAANG Offers in the AI Era
sessions.abstract: Cracking software engineering interviews while working full time has never been harder as assessments evolve to include AI assisted coding and higher hiring bars. Research indicates that performance ratings can be up to 12% lower for women even when code quality is identical. This gap is often driven by subjective evaluations rather than technical ability. This session reveals a structured 45 day framework to secure FAANG offers without burnout. We focus on three pillars: Technical Strategy, Interviewer Signal, and Neuro Performance. Attendees will learn to navigate AI augmented rounds by using AI as a co-pilot while maintaining core problem solving signals. I will demonstrate a mock AI assisted interview and share a repeatable roadmap designed for a 9 to 5 schedule. Participants will leave with a definitive call to action and a high impact toolkit designed for immediate application in their interview preparation.

sessions.title: Across the Great Divide: Lessons Learned from Storage and GPU Engineering
sessions.abstract:
For most of my career in data infra at AWS Lakehouse, I understood how petabytes of enterprise data was stored and optimized. What I did not understand was what happened to it after it left my system. The GPUs consuming with it were a black box, and for a long time I did not think it mattered.

It turned out it DID matter.

When I moved to Crusoe to build GPU observability tooling, I began seeing training jobs from the other side. A pattern emerged: significant GPU idle time unexplained by model architecture or hardware. GPUs were waiting for data loaders to assign files at runtime. The hidden variable was the data pipeline! It remained invisible because storage engineers never saw usage traces, and compute engineers lacked the context to connect the dots.

This talk weaves two threads: a case study showing how metadata-aware loading eliminates this bottleneck and meaningfully reduces wasted compute, and a personal account of my career that spans both sides of the AI-training boundary.

sessions.title: Beyond Your Title: Influence Without Authority
sessions.abstract:
Are you a developer with great ideas but no seat at the table? This session unpacks a repeatable framework for scaling influence without authority—whether you're eyeing growth or already wear the title but want to expand your impact.
Master a four-pillar framework to scale technical impact while staying close to code: build credibility through consistent excellence, communicate like a leader while managing stakeholders, be proactive, and accelerate growth through continuous learning and community. Learn how to sustain momentum using the "Execution Flywheel."
Walk away with a 90-day influence roadmap, templates, and a playbook for leading without authority. Your role name doesn't define your impact—you can architect both systems and your career.

sessions.title: Modernizing IT to Transform Veteran Lives: Inside the VA’s Digital Transformation
sessions.abstract:
The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) has led one of the largest IT modernization efforts in the federal government, transforming its legacy systems into digital platforms that improve access to health care, benefits, and services for millions of veterans.
This panel brings together senior VA technology leaders to share candid stories from the frontlines of modernization. Beyond systems and architecture, we’ll explore what transformation looks like in real outcomes: faster benefit decisions, improved health data access, and more seamless service experiences for veterans and their families.
Attendees will gain practical lessons in large-scale modernization, human-centered design, and mission-driven technology leadership they can apply to their own work through powerful stories that demonstrate how transforming technology can meaningfully improve lives.

sessions.title: LinkedIn That Lands Offers: How to Build a Brand That Gets You Hired, with a LinkedIn Top Voice
sessions.abstract:
You don’t need more qualifications.

You need more visibility.

In today’s job market, talent alone isn’t enough. Recruiters Google you. Hiring managers check LinkedIn before interviews. The people who get hired fastest aren’t just qualified, they are discoverable.

In this hands-on workshop led by Morgan Young, a LinkedIn Top Voice, LinkedIn Learning Instructor on Personal Branding with 20K+ learners, and former Product Manager at Shopify & Disney, and Fatimah Hussain, a technical founder & content creator with over 200M+ views on social media, you will learn how to turn LinkedIn into an opportunity engine for your career.

We will cover:

• How to optimize your profile to attract recruiters

• How to write posts that demonstrate expertise without oversharing

• How to build a professional personal brand that feels authentic

• How to convert visibility into interviews, speaking opportunities, and promotions

You will leave with a stronger profile, a clear content framework, and a repeatable strategy to turn your online presence into a personal brand that gets you real opportunities.

sessions.title: Designing a Tech Hub with Intention: How Chicago Is Building an Inclusive Innovation Ecosystem
sessions.abstract: Becoming a global tech hub doesn’t happen by accident. Instead, it requires intentional ecosystem design. In this presentation, Brad Henderson, Founding CEO of P33 Chicago, shares how Chicago is aligning industry, academia, government, and philanthropy to build a competitive and inclusive innovation economy. Rather than focusing on individual companies or technologies, this session examines the systems that enable sustained growth: talent pipelines, stakeholder coordination, governance, and long-term investment strategies. Drawing from Chicago’s experience, attendees will learn how regions and organizations can move beyond fragmented efforts toward collaborative models that generate both economic impact and equitable access to opportunity.

sessions.title: Celebrating Systers
sessions.abstract: Honoring Our Roots, Shaping Our Future In 1987, Dr. Anita Borg and 12 computer scientists started one of the first and largest global email networks exclusively for women in computing. That single spark created Systers and ultimately inspired the creation of GHC itself. This reception is your chance to network across generations and experience the power of collective support. Come for the connection, stay for the community, and help us write the next chapter.

sessions.title: GHC POWER UP
sessions.abstract:
Morning Movement for Stronger Bodies, Sharper Minds & Better Days 

Before the sessions start, the meetings begin, and the ideas start flowing, take 45 minutes for you. 

GHC Power Up is a new morning movement series designed to help attendees start the day feeling energized, grounded, and ready to take on GHC. Across three mornings, attendees can choose from yoga, HIIT, and full-body fitness experiences led by dynamic wellness instructors Reina Dominguez and Paris Jackson. 

Because showing up as your best self isn't just about what you know. It's also about taking care of the body and mind that make everything else possible. 

Whether you want to stretch, sweat, reset, or simply make space for yourself before a full conference day, Power Up is your invitation to move.

Kick off GHC with energy. Join Coach P for a high-energy Cardio Dance workout combining upbeat music, rhythmic movement, and muscle-focused exercises for a full-body, feel-good fitness experience. 

Participants will dance, groove, and sweat through movements designed to elevate the heart rate and work the body from head to toe. No dance experience is required, and the class is designed for all fitness levels.

Turn up the energy before the conference day begins. This high-energy fitness experience is designed to get your heart pumping, challenge your body, and build strength while allowing participants to work at their own level.

Close out GHC with Flow State, a mindful yoga flow designed to improve mobility, release tension, and reconnect mind and body. 

Through intentional movement and breathwork, participants will build space, restore balance, and leave feeling grounded, energized, and ready for the day ahead.

sessions.title: Why Most GenAI Pilots Fail and How Leaders Make the Ones That Matter Succeed
sessions.abstract:
Organizations are launching Generative AI pilots at unprecedented speed, yet most fail to move beyond experimentation. The problem is rarely the technology & it’s how leaders decide what to prioritize, measure, and scale.

This session examines why most GenAI pilots stall or fail from a leadership and decision making perspective. Drawing on real enterprise experiences in regulated environments, it introduces a practical framework leaders use to evaluate GenAI ideas, align them to business outcomes, and decide when to stop, pivot, or scale.

Attendees will learn how successful leaders define meaningful success metrics, avoid common adoption traps, and build cross-functional alignment across product, engineering, risk, and operations. Participants will leave with actionable tools to move GenAI initiatives from pilots to sustained business impact.

sessions.title: AI Beyond English: Building Multi-Lingual AI Solutions
sessions.abstract: This talk addresses the core challenges technical teams face when dealing with non-English languages in building effective AI solutions, reinforced by real-life examples. We will outline the complexity of non-English data, from tackling non-Latin character sets and low-resource languages to the practical hurdles of transforming unstructured data (like images and audio) into usable text. We will also go into the options for different technical approaches, including topics such as the complexity of language detection and cross-language processing techniques. The session will also analyze the current role and limitations of LLMs across diverse languages. We will conclude with best practices for designing and deploying high-performance, multilingual NLP systems that deliver value for practical business use cases.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: AI Is Changing Skills — But Not Who Gets Heard
sessions.abstract:
AI is transforming how work gets done, how skills are measured, and how careers are built. Yet while technology is evolving rapidly, the systems that determine whose expertise is trusted and who advances into leadership often remain unchanged.
Drawing on international experience in SaaS and EdTech, alongside qualitative and quantitative research on workplace equity across Europe and the US, this session examines a growing disconnect in the future of work: AI may be changing what we value, but not who gets heard. Women and underrepresented professionals are frequently evaluated through outdated signals of confidence, authority, and “fit,” even as organizations claim to be future-ready.
This talk challenges audiences to rethink how leadership and talent are recognized in an AI-driven world. It offers a practical lens for redesigning evaluation, influence, and decision-making systems so that innovation reflects not just technological progress, but human progress as well.

sessions.title: Aspire to Inspire: Turning Rejection into Ripple Impact and Becoming the Leader You Once Needed
sessions.abstract: Breaking into tech isn’t just about landing the job, it’s about becoming someone who lifts others along the way. After facing countless rejections, final-round losses at top companies, and navigating the U.S. tech ecosystem as an international student, I stopped chasing “success” and started building something bigger: impact. From wearing multiple hats at a high-growth startup to mentoring students, leading Women in Tech initiatives, and helping women navigate internships and careers, I discovered a powerful truth: Career growth multiplies when you design it to serve others. In this session, I will introduce the "Aspire-Build-Give-Multiply" framework, a practical, repeatable approach that transforms setbacks into confidence, growth into leadership, and individual wins into community impact. Attendees won’t just leave inspired, they’ll leave with tools, habits, and systems. Because when one woman rises, she can bring ten more with her.

sessions.title: From Automation to Augmentation: The New Era of Human-AI Collaboration in Supply Chain Planning
sessions.abstract: As supply chains gets more complex, advanced technologies are transforming AI-Supply Planner interaction. This session explores the shift from automation to collaborative intelligence in supply chain planning domain. Learn how to create future-ready strategies, driving smarter decisions, greater agility and sustainable competitive advantage. Join us to explore actionable approaches for shaping the future of work and learn how to position your organization at the forefront of this evolution.

speakers.name: Monisha Athi Kesavan Premalatha
speakers.title: Lead AI PM - Supply Chain Operations Managements

sessions.title: Alone Together: Building Collective Courage in a Connected, Lonely Tech World
sessions.abstract:
In an era where technology connects us in unprecedented ways, the loneliness epidemic persists, especially in demanding tech cultures where leaders are expected to perform alone.

This session reframes that tension as a design and leadership problem, not a personal failure. Drawing on lessons from high‑stakes environments — extreme mountain expeditions and global legal systems — Anjali Mehta explores collective courage as a measurable leadership practice that leads to inclusive innovation and meaningful systems change.

We go through: actionable frameworks to build psychological safety and trust across teams; leadership practices that turn vulnerability into sustainable, innovative performance; strategies for embedding collective courage into team norms, increasing innovation and opportunity for systems change. 

Attendees will leave with tools they can apply immediately to strengthen connection, influence, and effectiveness as leaders in tech.

speakers.name: Anjali Mehta
speakers.title: Founder & Executive Director
speakers.company: What is the Power of We

sessions.title: Building Culture and Influence on Technical Teams: What I Wish I’d Known
sessions.abstract: Strong teams are shaped in small choices—how we listen, decide, and show up. This interactive session shares six lessons I wish I had learned sooner about building team culture in technical environments. Early in our careers, we’re taught to ship code and solve problems, but rarely how to intentionally shape the culture that makes those outcomes possible. Through practical, hard-earned takeaways, we’ll explore what builds trust, strengthens collaboration, and sustains performance. We’ll examine the invisible dynamics of decisions, feedback, conflict, and psychological safety. The session also highlights the often invisible work women in STEM carry, framing culture-building as leadership, not “extra” work, and empowering participants to strengthen teams while advancing their careers. Building culture isn’t accidental—it’s intentional, and it’s the leadership many of us wish we’d understood sooner.

sessions.title: Build a success mindset
sessions.abstract:
In our fast paced and constantly disruptive workplaces- especially in this age of AI, women in technology face many #internal and #external barriers on our journey to unlock our maximum success.

These barriers can deplete us of our energy and play tricks on our mind to make us believe we are not set up for long term and sustainable success.

Using the power of AI, and small group discussions, this interactive workshop will #equip, #empower and #energize to build a success mindset from inside-out so you can remain on track to unlock your maximum success- no matter what comes your way.

Drawing from our joint lived experiences (former VP at IBM, Founder and CEO and a best selling author,  former CTO at Microsoft/Podcast host and Software Engineer at ClickUp), we'll guide you through practical exercises and discussions to:

1. Intentionally Aim High

2. Craft your Personal Success Plan

3. Show your worth in every interaction.

4. Own your Power.

5. Reflect and Celebrate weekly to remain energized.

You will learn to move towards your success on a daily basis and pivot when necessary.

speakers.name: Shelmina Abji
speakers.title: CEO, ShowYourWorth.ai. Best selling author and former IBM Vice President

speakers.name: Lakecia Gunter
speakers.title: Tech Executive and Corporate Board Director

sessions.title: Align Your Work With What Executive Teams Actually Care About
sessions.abstract:
Do you ever question how your work impacts the bottom line? Do you wonder, how to best communicate your impact? Many professionals work hard, yet struggle to gain visibility with leadership. Understanding how to speak the language of the C-suite is essential.

In this session, Parul Lahoti Bhandari introduces a practical framework built around five core metrics that executive teams consistently use to evaluate priorities: growth, risk, customers, efficiency, and future position. Drawing on experience across technology, operations, and customer success, she demonstrates how professionals at any level can translate their work into language that resonates with decision-makers.

Key Takeaways
- The five metrics executive teams use to guide decisions and prioritize investments
- How to translate technical or functional work into business-relevant outcomes
- Practical techniques for communicating impact 
- Strategies to increase visibility and influence regardless of role or title

sessions.title: Growing Your Career While Working with Legacy Systems
sessions.abstract:
Legacy code is inevitable in long-standing and high-impact systems. Early-career engineers are often told to avoid legacy systems, as they’re frequently perceived as confusing, built on outdated practices, or detrimental to system reliability. However, they are missing a key opportunity for technical and professional growth, as working with legacy systems builds skills like deep product and domain expertise, effective stakeholder communication, and cross-functional collaboration.
In this workshop, participants will explore how all long-standing systems gradually become “legacy,” and how modern engineers can evolve legacy code without breaking what works. Through hands-on activities inspired by real-world financial systems, participants will practice evaluating trade-offs with stakeholders and be introduced to modern technologies.
By the end of this session, participants will look at legacy code as a source of learning and opportunity, rather than a liability.

sessions.title: Non-Target? No problem!
sessions.abstract:
Students from smaller or lesser-known universities often feel discouraged about breaking into big tech, but your school name does not determine your success. In this talk, I’ll walk you through practical strategies to help you stay competitive in today’s tech recruiting landscape.

I’ll share what actually works, from building strong projects and making the most of hackathons and internships, to networking with intention and preparing for both technical and behavioral interviews. My goal is for you to leave with a clear roadmap and the confidence to pursue opportunities at top tech companies, regardless of where you go to school.

sessions.title: AI Won’t Replace You — But Lazy Engineering Will
sessions.abstract:
AI coding tools are transforming how engineers build software. They can generate code, write tests, and suggest solutions in seconds. But are we becoming smarter engineers — or just faster ones?This session explores the difference between over-relying on AI and using it strategically. Through relatable examples, we’ll discuss how AI can either strengthen critical thinking or gradually weaken problem-solving skills.

Designed for engineers at all levels, this talk focuses on maintaining strong fundamentals, sound judgment, and technical confidence in an AI-driven world. Attendees will leave with practical strategies to use AI as a thinking partner — ensuring it amplifies their skills rather than replaces them.

sessions.title: From Great to Sought-After: The Strategic Shift Women in Tech Must Make
sessions.abstract:
Many of us in tech were taught that if we work hard, stay humble, and consistently deliver excellent results, we will rise. So we do it all. We raise our hands. We stay late. We become the reliable problem-solvers and steady force behind key initiatives. Yet despite our excellence, we often find ourselves overlooked for high-visibility opportunities, excluded from strategic conversations, or passed over for leadership roles.

With two decades at Microsoft and now coaching high-performing professionals, and as author of The Sought-After Leader (June 2026), Uma Subramanian has witnessed a difficult truth: greatness builds credibility, but it does not automatically create influence or demand.

This session explores the strategic shifts required to move from excellent to sought-after. Attendees will learn how to elevate their impact from execution to strategy, strengthen their influence in critical moments, and become leaders whose contributions are actively sought, valued, and rewarded.

sessions.title: Inner Workshop: Lead the Moment by Leading Yourself
sessions.abstract:
The higher you climb, the more you're asked to hold - complex decisions, evolving team dynamics, organizational pressure, and the constant calibration of how you show up. For experienced women in tech, the challenge of leadership is not simply capability. It is capacity. And how you lead yourself - your clarity, your presence, your ability to recover - directly shapes the team, culture and performance around you.

This workshop works directly with the internal mechanisms that govern how you think, respond, and replenish - drawing on the toolkit the TLEX Institute brings to executives at leading global organizations, including evidence-based breath work and meditation as precision instruments for cognitive performance and leadership presence.

We'll explore what it means to lead each moment from a place of genuine steadiness. When you are regulated, you think more clearly. When you are present, your team feels it. When you recover well, you lead with range. These are not soft outcomes. They are the conditions that make everything else in your leadership possible - the quality of your decisions, the trust you build, the connection you create.

This workshop is experiential and designed for inner growth that extends well beyond the room. You will leave with resources to cultivate your mind, sustain what you've built, and connect with a community navigating the same terrain.

sessions.title: Leading the Enterprise AI Shift: Redefining Tech Roles and Career Growth
sessions.abstract:
AI is no longer a future concept. It is actively reshaping how work happens inside world’s largest enterprises. As organizations scale AI, it’s not just technology that’s changing, but roles, responsibilities, and career paths.

This panel offers a behind-the-scenes look at how leaders across hyperscalers and enterprise platforms are navigating this shift. Panelists from engineering, product, technical program management, operations and consulting will share how their roles have evolved as AI moved from experimentation to business-critical infrastructure.

Together, they will explore how enterprises are adopting AI, which skills are becoming essential, and how professionals are redefining leadership and impact in an AI-native workplace. This session goes beyond hype to focus on how professionals are learning new technologies, managing uncertainty, and shaping AI adoption while delivering business value. Attendees will gain practical insights to help future-proof their careers by harnessing AI.

speakers.name: Mike Flynn
speakers.title: Principal - EY US Technology Sector Consulting Leader and EY – Rillet Global Alliance Leader

speakers.name: Alexandria (Lexi B) Butler
speakers.title: Principal Technical Program Manager, AI Safety and Security

sessions.title: Responsible AI at Global Scale: Governance, Compliance, and Contextualization
sessions.abstract:
An AI model ships globally overnight. It sounds fluent, but offends culturally in one market, breaks layout in another, misformats currency elsewhere, and violates a disclosure rule in a fourth. The model is accurate. The business is at risk.

This is the cost of scaling AI without scaling governance.

At PayPal, operating across hundreds of regulatory regimes has required building compliance, linguistic intelligence, and market validation directly into our platforms. In the AI era, reactive reviews are not enough. Regulatory fragmentation, design variability across languages, and market-specific financial laws demand governance-by-design.

In this session, I’ll share how to embed regulatory intelligence, locale-aware validation, and policy enforcement into AI architectures, separating model capability from compliance control. Responsible AI at global scale is not just about ethics; it is about operationalizing trust in real time.

speakers.name: Aarti Ashok
speakers.title: Director of Product, Globalization Technology & Services

sessions.title: Autonomous Incident Response with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract:
Cloud engineering teams are drowning in incidents. Manual troubleshooting, endless logs, and pressure to resolve issues quickly make incident response exhausting — driving talented people, disproportionately women, out of the field.

  Autonomous agents are changing that. By investigating incidents like an experienced DevOps engineer — correlating signals across your observability tools, runbooks, and code automatically — AWS DevOps Agent transforms operational response and makes cloud engineering sustainable.

  In this hands-on workshop, we walk you through creating and configuring Agent Spaces and investigating real incidents across EC2 and Lambda workloads. You'll see how autonomous agents detect failures, correlate signals, identify root causes, and deliver actionable mitigation plans — then help prevent future incidents — without starting from scratch at 2am.

  You'll leave with practical experience setting up and using autonomous agents for incident response, and an understanding of how this technology reduces operational burden and makes cloud engineering more accessible and sustainable.

Laptop required — this is a hands-on session, so please bring your own laptop.

sessions.title: Build Your Career Before You're Hired: Digital Presence in the AI Era
sessions.abstract:
Early-career professionals are entering a job market shaped by rapid technological change and increasing uncertainty. Traditional career paths are less predictable, and resumes alone are no longer enough to stand out. Today, digital presence plays a critical role in creating visibility, credibility, and opportunity.

In this session, Martina Matthews shares lessons from joining the founding team of Chegg immediately after college and building a career by saying yes to opportunities before feeling fully qualified. She will introduce a practical framework for building a strong digital presence using tools such as LinkedIn, AI assistants, and Canva.

Attendees will learn how to position themselves online, communicate their strengths clearly, and use AI to accelerate career growth. Participants will leave with a simple, actionable plan for building a professional presence that creates opportunity early in their careers.

sessions.title: Data Foundations for Agentic AI - Vision to Value
sessions.abstract:
Agentic AI marks a strategic shift—from tools to teammates that can reason, decide, and execute in pursuit of business outcomes. For executives, the question is no longer if agents will transform the enterprise, but how to build the right data foundation to unlock value—quickly and responsibly.

This session will present a forward-looking vision for the data foundations that enable enterprise-grade agentic AI to move from ambition to impact. We will explore how to federate data architectures for real-time, context-aware agents; establish governance models that balance speed with trust; and cultivate a data-driven culture and operating model that accelerates innovation rather than constrains it.

Leaders will leave with practical insights on compressing time-to-value, aligning data strategy with business outcomes, and organizing teams to responsibly scale AI agents as trusted digital teammates across the enterprise.

speakers.name: Kalpana Mahesh
speakers.title: Head of Data & Gen AI, Solution Architecture

sessions.title: Uncertainty is a Feature, Not a Bug: Thriving Through Motherhood, Mortgages and Career Plateaus
sessions.abstract:
Do you feel like your career algorithm is stuck in an infinite loop? We're told growth requires "hustle," but what happens when life throws exceptions you can’t catch—like visa renewal anxiety, a heavy mortgage, the identity shift of motherhood, or a career plateau?
In this session, we'll reframe these constraints not as system failures, but as features forcing clarity. Inspired by the "10x is easier than 2x" philosophy, we will explore how limitations help strip away the non-essential. When your bandwidth is capped by paperwork, finances, or a toddler, you lose the luxury of "busy work." You're forced to identify the few high-impact actions that actually move the needle.
You'll leave with a framework for setting goals when the future feels foggy. We'll ditch rigid 5-year plans for a "micro-commit" strategy – taking small, non-threatening steps that compound into massive results. Stop waiting for perfect conditions and start shaping your path forward, right where you are

sessions.title: Human-AI Collaboration in Hiring: From Ghosted to Offer-Ready
sessions.abstract:
In 2026, competitive advantage belongs to professionals who collaborate with AI intentionally. The job market is AI-saturated.Candidates use generative tools, while hiring managers see rising generic, misaligned applications. The real differentiator isn't whether you use AI, but how. This interactive workshop introduces a human-in-the-loop, agentic AI career workflow. Participants will learn a structured Draft → Evaluate → Revise loop grounded in real hiring decision systems. Through live demo & guided breakouts, participants will learn how to:
• Extract hiring signals from job descriptions
• Build a compelling, role-aligned "why you" narrative
• Generate ATS-safe, interview-defensible resume
• Score & intentionally revise AI outputs
• Create an interview readiness & networking plan 
Using structured prompt packs & HR recruiter-informed rubrics, attendees gain a repeatable workflow & take-home Tech Pack to apply independently.

sessions.title: Why the Future of Tech Leadership Isn’t Technical — It’s Relational
sessions.abstract:
AI can write code, review pull requests, and accelerate delivery faster than ever. So where does that leave you as a technology leader?

The leaders who will thrive in the age of AI aren’t the most technical. Instead, they’re the ones who build relationships that enable trust, align stakeholders, and shape culture. As execution becomes automated, your ability to build relationships becomes your greatest differentiator. 

In this session, two senior tech leaders share practical strategies to expand your influence in ways that match your natural style. Whether you’re energized by broad networks or prefer a few deep, trusted partnerships, you’ll learn how to scale your impact without pretending to be someone you’re not.

sessions.title: Uprooted & Unstoppable: Breaking In Without a Blueprint, A First‑Gen Tech Story
sessions.abstract:
What happens when you're the first in your family to go to college, intern in tech, or navigate life as a child of immigrants in an unfamiliar country? You figure it out anyway. And once you're in, the journey is just beginning. 

This panel brings together five first‑generation Latinas from immigrant households, all former tech interns and now professionals at Microsoft: two software engineers, two product managers, and a product marketing manager. Each broke barriers their families never imagined, whether becoming the first to attend college, enter tech, or work in the U.S. 

This is a safe, honest space to talk about the real cost of being the first: what it takes to break into tech, imposter syndrome, cultural pressure, financial responsibility, and the moments of doubt behind every “yes” and every offer. If you’ve ever wondered whether you belong in tech, this session shows you how to build your own seat, and hold the door open for those coming after you.

sessions.title: From ETL to AI: A Data Engineer's Honest Journey into AI/ML
sessions.abstract: Most AI/ML Engineers did not start there and that is the point. This session tells the honest story of how a Data Engineer with two years of pipeline building, PySpark, and ETL automation became an AI/ML Engineer building production ML systems and AI agents. This is not a pivot story. It is a depth story covering advanced algorithms, neural networks, Women in AI global research, LLM fine tuning, and agentic AI, all built while the field evolved at breakneck speed. Today that journey lives in production at Pile Dynamics Inc.,USA, where decades of geotechnical foundation testing data used in 100+ countries is being transformed into intelligent ML systems and cloud deployed AI agents. Presenter: Dinky Mishra, is an AI/ML Engineer at Pile Dynamics Inc.,USA. and a Research Assistant at Women in AI, whose work spans ML architecture, AI agent deployment, and global research on LLMs. If you are a data professional wondering whether your skills are enough to make this leap, they are.

sessions.title: Agentic Public Health Copilots: Reduce Noise, Speed Response, Add Guardrails in Disease Surveillance
sessions.abstract: Public health exists to prevent harm before it becomes a crisis, and disease surveillance is the early warning system for detecting outbreaks and trends. Today, ML and DL workflows already help surveillance teams manage volume and complexity, including text classification for triage, NLP extraction of key fields from narratives, clustering to group similar reports, anomaly detection to flag unusual patterns, and summarization to speed situational awareness. This virtual session shows students and early career technologists how to combine these capabilities with Generative AI and LLMs into an agentic surveillance copilot that runs a safe workflow: triage inputs, extract structured data, retrieve evidence from approved guidance, generate grounded summaries, and escalate uncertain cases to humans. Attendees will learn the end to end blueprint, evaluation basics, and practical guardrails to reduce hallucinations and build trust.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: The Blueprint: Masterclass on Navigating the Tech Ecosystem as Black Women
sessions.abstract: For Black women in tech, building a high-impact career requires a clear strategy to navigate today’s complex tech ecosystem. As a group of engineers and PMs from Google DeepMind, Uber, Capital One, SeatGeek, and Snap, we are coming together to decode the unwritten rules of the industry. From breaking into AI and product to navigating the cultural shifts between "Big Tech" giants and the high-velocity world of startups and entrepreneurship, we offer a 360-degree view of the modern tech landscape. We share the tactical maneuvers that fueled our journeys through "Big Tech", McKinsey, Twitter, Harvard, and the founder experience.

sessions.title: AI Trust Architecture: Scaling Autonomous Multi-Agent workflows with Human-on-the-loop Governance
sessions.abstract:
As we pivot from simple chatbots to autonomous Agentic Workflows, the engineering challenge moves beyond "one-shot" prompting toward iterative reasoning loops. For a system to be effective, it must master four core design patterns: Reflection, Tool Use, Planning, and Multi-Agent Collaboration. However, in production-grade systems, autonomy without accountability is a liability, prompting the need for a new Trust Architecture. 
This panel draws on firsthand experience building production-grade multi-agent orchestration systems at Adobe and Intuit and explores building this architecture by combining standardized protocols like the MCP for secure tool use with Constitutional AI for ethical self-correction. We will debate the challenges of managing Human-on-the-loop systems and the disciplined evaluation processes required to ensure agents remain aligned in unpredictable environments. Attendees will leave with a strategic blueprint for scaling agentic systems that are "Trusted by Default"

sessions.title: International Women in US Tech: Navigating Career, Identity, and Optionality
sessions.abstract: International women in tech often navigate multiple layers of complexity: cultural adjustment, confidence challenges, immigration uncertainty, and career pressure. This session shares practical frameworks for building optionality and resilience while growing in US tech environments. We’ll cover how to build a strong professional narrative across cultures, communicate confidently in interviews and on teams, and design a career path that remains flexible under uncertainty. The goal is empowerment through strategy: skills that compound, relationships that support you, and choices that expand freedom over time—so you can keep progressing even when the environment changes. You’ll leave with practical scripts for self-intros, boundary-setting, and asking for opportunities without sounding aggressive. Key takeaways: an optionality framework, cross-cultural communication tactics, and a plan for non-linear growth while staying competitive.

sessions.title: AI Roadshow Experience
sessions.abstract: Get hands-on with the future of AI! The AI Roadshow Experience features five interactive stations where you'll rotate through cutting-edge demos and workshops. Perfect for all skill levels—discover how AI is transforming technology and learn practical skills you can apply immediately.

sessions.title: Leading Through Change: A Career Built on Curiosity and Continuous Learning
sessions.abstract: As industries, technologies, and business priorities evolve, the ability to adapt becomes one of the most important career skills. Join Jess Quagliaroli as she reflects on key moments that shaped her career, including developing confidence as a leader, challenging conventional thinking, embracing emerging technologies, and helping guide AI transformation through both grassroots engagement and leadership-driven change.

sessions.title: Designing with Accessibility in Mind
sessions.abstract: Both digital experiences and physical environments should be accessible to all, regardless of abilities or disabilities. In this session, Apple designer Lisa Mirth and Apple TV accessibility lead Tatiana Lee will discuss how accessibility can create more inclusive spaces for all. Attendees will walk away with knowledge of design best practices, terminology and built-in features to support accessible exp

sessions.title: Celebrating LGBTQIA+
sessions.abstract: Proud, powerful, and changing the face of tech! Join us as we celebrate our incredible LGBTQIA+ community and the diverse voices driving innovation forward. Come connect with fellow changemakers, share your story, and be part of a welcoming, inclusive space where authenticity meets leadership and tech excellence thrives.

sessions.title: Staying Relevant When the Ground Won’t Stop Moving
sessions.abstract:
Twelve months ago, we were building elaborate agent frameworks, complex RAG stacks, and orchestration layers to compensate for model limitations. Today, frontier models are quietly absorbing much of that scaffolding. Larger context windows, stronger reasoning, and native tool use are collapsing layers of glue we once believed were essential.

The half-life of AI best practices is shrinking.

In this keynote, I reflect on what it means to lead and build in a world where last year’s architecture becomes today’s technical debt. Drawing from enterprise-scale AI deployments, I will explore the shift from heavy scaffolding to starting simple—and from building glue to designing domain-driven evaluation.

As models improve, durable advantage moves away from elaborate orchestration and toward judgment: knowing what “good” looks like, building feedback loops that sustain quality, and architecting systems that expect replacement. The system hasn’t disappeared—it has moved upward, into governance, observability, cost discipline, and human alignment.

But this is also a personal story. What does it feel like to watch carefully engineered best practices age in months? How do we maintain confidence and clarity when the technology redefines itself faster than our roadmaps? And how do we help the next generation build careers that endure beyond any single stack?

In a world where models eat the glue, the most important skill is not mastering today’s infrastructure—it is learning how to evolve with it.

sessions.title: Behind the Magic: GitLab Disaster Recovery
sessions.abstract:
In Imagineering, guests only see the magic—but behind the curtain, reliability keeps the show running. GitLab plays a critical backstage role, housing years of source code, pipelines, and creative work. When outages, breaches, or cloud failures strike, hope is not a strategy—design is.

This session shares how the WDI SRE Core Team engineered a production-ready disaster recovery strategy for GitLab, protecting over 2TB of critical data across hundreds of users and thousands of pipelines. Attendees will learn how immutable AWS Backup Vaults, automated backup plans, layered monitoring, and repeatable DR testing work together to ensure GitLab can be restored quickly when the unexpected happens.

Using real-world examples and live-tested recovery workflows, this talk reframes disaster recovery as part of the show design itself—because when systems fail, the magic doesn’t stop, and the curtain never has to fall.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Breaking Barriers: The Female Journey from Manager to Director in Health Tech
sessions.abstract:
Transitioning from Technical Product Manager to Director of Enterprise Data in healthcare technology presents unique challenges for women leaders. This session highlights the hurdles I faced and explores the effective pathways I took to become successful. 

My personal journey included feeling overwhelmed and isolated; however, emphasizing essential leadership qualities like empathy, adaptability, and decisiveness led me to success. I will discuss with you how the critical role of mentorship and community helped me overcome obstacles. 

We will engage in interactive discussions to uncover strategies that empower women to break glass ceilings and foster inclusive workplaces. Together, we can inspire the next generation of female leaders driving change in the health technology industry. 

Join me in this engaging session to explore how we can collectively build a more inclusive future in health technology!

sessions.title: Brilliant, Exhausted, and Overthinking Everything
sessions.abstract:
You've been "thinking about it" for months. Maybe years. The promotion. The pivot. The leap. You tell yourself you need more clarity, more data, more certainty.

But what if the thing keeping you stuck isn't information — it's courage?

High performers are trained to analyze, optimize, and prepare. But that same instinct becomes a trap when the decision that matters most requires trust, not data.

This session is for women in tech who know something needs to change but keep waiting for the "right time." You'll learn to recognize when research becomes avoidance, how to break the cycle of analysis paralysis, and what it actually takes to move forward without certainty.

Lilah Jones spent 9 years at Google on the founding team that scaled Google Cloud from $0 to $106B. Now she coaches high-performing women through the career transitions they've been avoiding — helping them stop overthinking and start moving.

sessions.title: 2 Hours in Transit, 2 Hours for Growth: Turning Lost Time into Your Time
sessions.abstract:
Return-to-office mandates have added 10+ hours of commute time weekly for many tech workers. Rather than viewing this as lost time, this session shares strategies for transforming commute hours into opportunities for technical growth, relationship maintenance, and mental well-being.
Drawing from personal experience commuting to work, I'll share what actually works: technical podcasts that build skills, strategic phone calls that maintain relationships sacrificed to busy schedules, language learning apps for career development, and mindfulness practices that prevent commute stress.
You'll learn how to choose learning content that matches your commute type (driving vs. public transit), build sustainable commute routines to protect personal time despite longer days, and leverage commute time for professional development without sacrificing family connections.
This session is about sustainable strategies for navigating the new reality of office returns while maintaining career growth.

sessions.title: Cultivating Resilience: Engineering Agriculture with Graphs and Spatial AI
sessions.abstract:
Global agriculture is no longer a collection of isolated data points—it is a connected system shaped by climate, geography, and rapidly changing conditions. Yet most data platforms still treat these dimensions independently, limiting our ability to make reliable, AI-driven decisions.

In this session, we explore how a hybrid approach—combining ontologies, knowledge graphs, and spatial intelligence—enables context-rich, decision-ready data. Through a real-world agricultural logistics scenario, we demonstrate how semantic models (RDF) establish meaning, property graphs enable high-speed connected data retrieval, and spatial analytics adds critical location awareness.

You’ll see how this “brain + muscle” architecture powers context-augmented AI, where the system performs reasoning and data retrieval before invoking the LLM—reducing hallucination and improving reliability. We’ll walk through an end-to-end workflow that transforms a complex question into a grounded, explainable recommendation.

Whether you’re designing data platforms or building AI-driven solutions, this session provides a practical blueprint for turning disconnected agricultural data into intelligent, actionable insight.

sessions.title: Rebuilding Without a Reset Button
sessions.abstract: The majority of us don't plan our major life or career transitions; instead, life presents them to us. There's no reset button. You rebuild while things are still falling apart — new country, new domain, new technology, new identity, all at once. This talk is that story, and the hard-won lessons from it. Anyone who has had to rebuild without a clear plan and wants to return stronger, smarter, and more self-assured should listen to this talk.

sessions.title: From Hospitals to Phones: The Shift Toward Patient-Owned Health Data
sessions.abstract: Personal health records are no longer locked inside hospital systems—they are now accessible on phones, patient portals, and consumer health platforms. This shift toward patient-owned health data is transforming how individuals engage with their health, how technology is built, and how data is used across healthcare, AI, and digital products. This session explores how interoperability standards, APIs, and consumer health platforms are reshaping personal health records (PHRs). Attendees will learn what data is actually included in a health record, how it flows across systems, and what “data ownership” truly means in practice. Using a health informatics lens, the session will unpack the opportunities this shift creates for greater transparency, patient empowerment, and innovation—alongside the risks, including data fragmentation, privacy concerns, and inequitable access.

sessions.title: Agent Architecture Patterns: Building Blocks for Intelligent AI Systems in Production
sessions.abstract:
Large Language Models have evolved from simple chatbots to sophisticated agentic systems capable of complex reasoning, tool use, and multi-step problem-solving. But how do you architect intelligent agents for production?
This technical session breaks down proven patterns: ReAct (Reasoning + Acting), Chain-of-Thought, Tree-of-Thoughts, and Reflection. Learn when to use each pattern, how to compose them for complex workflows, and critical production considerations.
Drawing from enterprise experience in financial services, we'll explore multi-agent collaboration, memory systems, error handling, and evaluation frameworks. Demonstrations use LangGraph and LangChain, but architectural principles apply universally.
Whether building customer service agents, data analysis workflows, or autonomous systems, you'll gain practical patterns applicable across any stack—with code examples, architecture diagrams, and a decision framework for pattern selection.

sessions.title: The Fast-Track Blueprint: How to Go from Entry Level to Senior Engineer in Under 5 Years
sessions.abstract:
Landing your first role is just the beginning. The real challenge is navigating the leap to Senior Engineer in a competitive workforce. Join five Senior Engineers from Capital One, representing Mobile, Backend, Web, Full-Stack, and ML/AI Engineering, who successfully fast-tracked this transition in under five years. This panel pulls back the curtain on the hidden curriculum of growth: mastering technical performance, navigating large organizational structures, and strategically navigating the performance management process.

We will discuss the tactical shifts required to level up, including how we each leverage AI to accelerate our careers and increase our daily impact. We’ll dive deep into the mechanics of performance reviews: how to document results, align with business goals, and turn feedback into a promotion roadmap. Whether you’re a student or an early-career associate, you’ll gain a blueprint for rapid growth and the political literacy needed to achieve seniority well ahead of schedule.

sessions.title: From Invisible to Influential: 3 Signals That Turn Work into Recognition and Promotions
sessions.abstract:
Many women in tech consistently deliver high-quality work yet struggle to gain recognition or secure promotions. Often, the issue is not caliber but how impact is perceived, communicated, and connected to leadership signals.
In technical roles, early promotion gaps compound over time. McKinsey’s 2022 analysis found that for every 100 men promoted to manager in tech, only 52 women were promoted. Research on performance evaluations (2021–2023) shows women are more likely to receive personality-coded feedback than impact-focused language, shaping how leadership potential is assessed.
This session introduces the 3 Signals of Influence, a practical framework to counter these dynamics by making impact measurable and ownership visible.
Participants will gain a repeatable strategy to translate strong work into recognized influence and promotion momentum, even in environments shaped by bias.

sessions.title: STORYHabits: From Self-Doubt to Strategic Influence
sessions.abstract:
Strategic influence is built—or eroded—through daily behavior. In 2024, STORYHabits debuted at Grace Hopper and filled to capacity. The method resonated deeply.

Over the past two years, we followed up with attendees and gathered real-world data from technologists who applied the framework. We learned what shifted executive presence, what strengthened boundaries, what reduced self-doubt—and where habits failed to stick.

Those insights shaped the evolution of STORYHabits.

In this updated session, you’ll see community outcomes and the refined system born from them. Attendees will also receive exclusive access to STORYHabitsGPT—an AI tool built from these insights—to refine their own habit identity live during the session.

You’ll leave with a values-anchored habit design, a repeatable refinement method, and a clearer path from self-doubt to sustained strategic influence.

sessions.title: Irresponsible AI - 10 things you shouldn’t do if you want to develop AI safely
sessions.abstract: This satirical but serious tech-talk focuses on common mistakes and disastrous pitfalls throughout the AI lifecycle. Instead of focusing on what you should do, this talk presents responsible AI core dimensions in their opposite form: irresponsible AI practices to ensure your AI model is completely unhinged. This talk covers scholarly research and current events in the rapidly evolving AI landscape, touching on various ways that AI can (and will!) go wrong without responsible AI considerations. From fully autonomous AI agents to pushing to production without any evaluation, this talk is a recipe for AI disaster. Come ready to laugh, learn, and think critically about how we all can do better when it comes to responsible AI.

sessions.title: Your Voice, Amplified: Using AI to Launch Your Career
sessions.abstract:
Early-career professionals are entering a job market where AI can accelerate every step of the application process—while also making candidates sound indistinguishable from one another. This session cuts through the noise and shows how to use AI as a thinking partner, not a shortcut.

Attendees will learn where AI meaningfully improves outcomes across career exploration, resumes, interviews, and networking—and where it can undermine authenticity and credibility. The session introduces a simple, repeatable framework to generate ideas, critically evaluate outputs, and translate them into a voice that is clear, differentiated, and personal.

Participants will also gain insight into how employers are adapting to AI-enabled candidates and what signals actually stand out in a highly assisted landscape. Attendees will leave with actionable strategies, effective prompts, and a clear approach they can apply immediately to navigate their job search with confidence and intention.

sessions.title: Staying Relevant in the Age of AI - Without Becoming an AI Expert
sessions.abstract:
As AI reshapes the technology landscape, many professionals feel pressure or anxiousness to reinvent themselves as AI experts. But long-term relevance does not require deep model-building expertise - it requires strategic AI integration.

This session explores how technologists can remain indispensable in the age of AI by shifting from technical specialization to systems thinking. Drawing from enterprise experience at Fortune 50 companies, the talk demonstrates how AI can be used as a leadership multiplier - enhancing decision-making, accelerating operational insights, and elevating strategic influence.

Attendees will leave with a clear framework for positioning themselves as AI-enabled leaders: professionals who understand how to integrate AI into systems, teams, and strategy, even if they are not building the models themselves.

speakers.name: Ashmita Srivastava
speakers.title: Associate Director of Technology- Engineering Operations

sessions.title: From Potential to Power: Mentorship and the Rise of Women Leaders in the Age of AI
sessions.abstract: In AI's fast-paced world, technical skills are only half the story; real power lies in building human connections. With 62% of Gen Z professionals wanting more guidance and 74% expecting AI to impact their work within a year, this workshop explores why intentional mentorship is now a strategic necessity. We will move past basic networking to discuss how high-impact alliances help women navigate AI era challenges. By focusing on the transition from mentorship to sponsorship, you will learn how to turn raw potential into leadership power that opens doors and changes careers. We will provide a clear roadmap to help you use your technical background as a foundation for leadership. You will learn to build a "Power Map" to find those who will champion your work in rooms you haven't entered yet. This is a call to action to stop waiting for permission and start using our collective strength to lead the AI revolution. Join us to claim your seat at the table and learn to lift others as you climb

sessions.title: What "Actually" Gets You to the Next Level
sessions.abstract:
Engineers at every level ask some version of the same question: how do I get to the next level? But the engineers who advance fastest aren’t the ones asking that question; they’re the ones making the answer obvious to the people around them.

This talk draws on firsthand experience inside calibration and promotion decisions to share what actually drives career growth: visible impact, operational reliability, and the ability to connect individual work to business outcomes. Attendees will leave with a practical, contrarian checklist they can apply immediately, regardless of their current level or company.

sessions.title: Why are we still talking about Imposter Syndrome in 2026?
sessions.abstract:
Women have been coached to overcome, overcompensate, and navigate the broken rung to leadership. We've talked at length about building confidence and power poses. How is it then that women and non-binary individuals can still fear that our success is accidental, our belonging conditional, and our real selves somehow disqualifying?

Come prepared to move beyond talk and focus on taking action to dismantle the conditions that allow imposter syndrome to take hold. Join in sharing stories and learning strategies to leverage community to tear down walls, build resilience, create and claim power, and identify when to walk away from environments setting you up to fail. We will unpack the psychological patterns that fuel imposter syndrome, the cultural pressures that reinforce it, and how to foster inclusive belonging. You will leave with concrete steps to break out of imposter syndrome barriers, tap into a community of support, and find conditions to let your authentic leadership shine.

sessions.title: Debugging Your Resume: Refactor, Optimize & Ship an Interview-Winning Version
sessions.abstract:
Is your resume stuck in legacy mode? Time for a system upgrade!
In today’s hyper-competitive tech market, strong technical skills aren’t enough. Candidates who land interviews learn to communicate impact with the same clarity they bring to building systems. 
In this hands-on workshop, you’ll treat your resume like a codebase and learn a practical “debugging” method to improve it. You’ll refactor its structure for clarity, eliminate vague statements, and rewrite bullet points as measurable, results-driven achievements. You’ll also learn a simple approach to “version control” that allows you to tailor your resume to different roles quickly and strategically.
During the workshop, you can choose to practice on a provided sample resume or on your own. Either way, you’ll leave with a practical framework you can use to continuously refine and adapt your resume to an interview-winning version as your career grows.

sessions.title: Returnships After the Boom: A Leadership Strategy for Unlocking Overlooked Talent
sessions.abstract:
A decade ago, returnships were a niche idea found mostly on Wall Street. In 2016, tech companies began exploring these programs to tackle gender imbalances and find talent in a tight labor job market. The model scaled rapidly and major companies invested. By 2022 hundreds of programs had launched and thousands of women were hired.

Then the market shifted, hiring contracted, and many companies pulled back on talent initiatives — including returnships. 
What does that mean for women trying to return to careers in tech? And for leaders trying to hire the talent needed for the next wave of tech innovation?

Drawing on a decade of data and frontline experience building programs with 100+ companies, this session examines why returnships grew, why some stalled, and what comes next. We’ll share workforce trends, insights from leaders in tech, and practical frameworks companies of any size can use to design sustainable pathways to ensure that mid-career women remain part of tech’s future.

sessions.title: The Partnership Playbook: Turn Corporate Education Investments Into Real STEM Talent Pipelines
sessions.abstract:
Your company spends six figures on education partnerships. You attend ribbon cuttings, take photos with students, and file them in the CSR report. Then your CEO asks what that investment did for your hiring numbers, and you change the subject.

This 60-minute hands-on workshop is for CSR directors, ERG leaders, and community impact professionals who are done with performative giving and ready to build education investments that connect directly to workforce diversity goals.

Using the Partnership Accelerator Process, a framework developed through $5M+ in secured funding and 50+ corporate-school partnerships, participants will audit their current investments, identify pipeline gaps, and leave with a 90-day action plan that justifies continued funding to leadership.

No theory. No slides you forget by Monday. Just frameworks you implement immediately, built by someone currently running the programs she teaches you to fund.

sessions.title: Don’t Get Fooled by the Bot: Red Flags, Real Signals, and Career Smart GenAI
sessions.abstract:
Generative AI can help you move fast or confidently lead you astray.

In this interactive session, we will use Microsoft AI tools to break down common GenAI red flags, such as hallucinations, false confidence, and vague or misleading answers, by having attendees evaluate real outputs, vote on what feels safe versus risky, and unpack why polished responses can still fail. We will then pivot to opportunity, showing how professionals can use GenAI effectively by structuring stronger prompts, validating assumptions, and communicating decisions with clarity to demonstrate senior level judgment.

Participants will leave with:
• A practical GenAI red flag checklist to identify risky outputs before they are acted on
• Reusable prompt patterns that surface assumptions, reasoning, risks, and recommendations
• A repeatable evaluation framework they can apply to product, architecture, and engineering decisions
• Techniques to communicate Gen AI supported recommendations with senior level clarity

sessions.title: Inside the algorithms: How AI is reshaping hiring - and how to position yourself to win
sessions.abstract: As AI quietly rewires how jobs are posted, discovered, and evaluated, many professionals—especially women navigating transitions—are unsure how to stay visible and competitive. This session reframes algorithmic matching not as a black box, but as infrastructure you can work with. We’ll unpack how modern hiring systems interpret skills, preferences, and behavior; how they filter and rank candidates; and which signals actually move people forward. Attendees will leave with a practical readiness framework, concrete ways to redesign their career narrative for AI-driven platforms, and a structured pathway to approach role changes, re-entry, advancement, or pivots with more agency and confidence.

speakers.name: Ruonan Ding
speakers.title: Senior Manager in Machine Learning Engineering

sessions.title: I Didn’t Have a Seat at the Table - So I Built My Own
sessions.abstract:
This session explores how to intentionally build influence, visibility, and career momentum. As a first‑generation professional, I learned early on that career growth is not accidental - it’s designed.

Drawing from my experience navigating large, complex organizations, I developed a deliberate approach to building trust, reputation, and sponsorship over time. In this session, I will teach the TABLE framework—a practical, repeatable model for building leadership capability through consistency, curiosity, and strategic relationship‑building.

Attendees will learn actionable strategies to build professional influence from scratch and increase visibility. The session shows how consistent execution and presence compound into influence, even in environments where expectations and rules are often implicit.

Attendees will leave with a clear framework and repeatable strategies they can apply immediately to start or accelerate their careers and build strong professional networks.

sessions.title: AI Workforce Strategy: Executive Strategies for Building Inclusive AI Talent Pipelines
sessions.abstract:
The AI talent gap is a board-level risk, and companies that fail to invest in early pipelines will face long-term competitive disadvantage. 

This executive panel is a strategic workforce planning discussion focused on early AI talent pipeline development. The session will explore how corporate leaders and workforce development organizations must align now to prepare the next generation of AI-ready talent before hiring pressure becomes a crisis. This conversation centers on what enterprise leaders must do differently today to secure tomorrow’s workforce.

Moderated by Joshua Cooper, Head of Culture at Uber, the session features Jessica Santana, Co-Founder and CEO of America On Tech and Erica Marie Dionne, SVP of Global Business Operations at NBCUniversal.

sessions.title: An Unhinged but Effective Guide to Scholarships and Fellowships
sessions.abstract: What do you do when your funding disappears — not once, but twice? You get creative. This session is part survival story, part playbook: a candid, practical guide to finding scholarships, fellowships, and other opportunities that most students never knew existed. Forget the usual advice. We're talking strategies that uncover opportunities buried in places you'd never think to look — and a system to make sure you're ready when they open. Whether you're actively searching or just want to get ahead of the game, you'll walk away with a completely different approach to finding funding that fits who you are.

sessions.title: Cracking the Early‑Career Job Hunt: Real Stories, Real Tactics, Smart AI
sessions.abstract: A practical, story driven playbook for landing your first tech job in a tough market by pairing proven job search tactics with AI as an ally. Through real examples: friends who rebounded after multiple layoffs, international students who upskilled to meet market and visa needs and mentees who turned chance conversations into offers. This session shows how to use AI to tailor resumes, strengthen portfolios, practice interviews, decode job descriptions, and network authentically. Attendees leave with clear, actionable steps and simple AI prompts they can apply immediately.

sessions.title: The Architecture of Inequality: Deconstructing Gender Bias in AI and the Power of Inclusive Tech
sessions.abstract:
The myth that Artificial Intelligence(AI) is inherently fair masks a dangerous reality: algorithms amplify historical gender biases. With women comprising just 12% of senior AI professionals , systems systematically default to a male-centric paradigm.

This presentation explores the profound impacts of this algorithmic patriarchy. We unpack staggering metrics: LLMs are 3 to 6 times more likely to default to rigid gender stereotypes , while computer vision systems have a 34% error rate for darker-skinned women. These biases drive systemic harm, from AI recruiters penalising older female candidates to economic models erasing women's unpaid labor.

Crucially, we reveal the massive socioeconomic dividend of fixing this architecture. Rectifying bias is a powerful lever for equity , capable of unlocking a projected 20% boost to global economic output and transforming AI from an engine of marginalization into a catalyst for true parity.

sessions.title: From Air Force to Algorithms: Unconventional Paths to Tech Leadership
sessions.abstract: It's about time we step into our power in tech—and this panel is here to show you how. This isn't your typical career advice session. Four exceptional women with radically different journeys are bringing real talk about building authentic careers, claiming your space in technology, and thriving on your own terms. Whether you're fresh out of college, pivoting from another industry, or ready to level up your career, this conversation delivers the strategies and confidence you need to succeed.
