Our panelists Deb, Lindsay, Anupama, and Michelle—have learned through decades of combined experience that showing up as your authentic self isn't just feel-good advice. It's a competitive advantage. No fluff, no corporate speak—just honest insights about navigating tech as women who refuse to compromise who they are.

sessions.title: Leading Through the Age of AI
sessions.abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming technology at an unprecedented pace, reshaping how we build products, solve problems, and interact with information. Yet while the technology itself is advancing rapidly, the organizations that succeed in the age of AI will not be defined by their models alone. They will be defined by their people, culture, adaptability, and leadership. As companies navigate one of the most significant technological shifts in decades, the challenge is no longer simply keeping up with innovation. It is building organizations that can continuously learn, evolve, and thrive amid constant change. How do leaders create environments where people embrace new technologies rather than fear them? How do teams balance speed with trust, innovation with resilience, and technical excellence with human judgment? And how do individuals build careers that remain meaningful and impactful as the nature of work evolves? Drawing on lessons from Bloomberg's own journey through multiple waves of technological transformation, this session will explore the human side of innovation—from fostering adaptable teams and inclusive cultures to empowering technologists to grow alongside the technologies they help create. We will discuss why diverse perspectives and strong leadership are essential to navigating uncertainty, and why the most successful organizations will be those that invest as deeply in people as they do in technology. For attendees at every stage of their careers, this conversation is an invitation to think beyond the tools themselves and focus on the qualities that endure. In the age of AI, lasting success will come not from technology alone, but from the people who shape what comes next.

speakers.name: Yunfei Xu
speakers.title: Global Head of Engineering, Enterprise Products at Bloomberg

sessions.title: Can Quantum Computers Solve Real-World Problems Yet?
sessions.abstract:
Quantum computing has the potential to reshape the world, but what can today's quantum machines actually do? This talk focuses on the problems most accessible to near-term quantum hardware, and examines where quantum approaches meaningfully apply today.

We'll explore how real-world optimization problems are mapped onto quantum systems, and take a look at current techniques such as quantum annealing, QAOA, and VQE algorithms. Using case studies across industries, we'll see how quantum optimization shows up in practice in areas like traffic routing, finance, and energy scheduling. Attendees will learn how to assess which problems fit today's quantum hardware, what the key technical limits are, and why most results rely on hybrid quantum-classical approaches.

This session is designed for technologists and strategy leaders who want a high-level understanding of what quantum computers can do in 2026, and how to make informed decisions about piloting it inside organizations.

sessions.title: From Skipping Every Opportunity to Building a Community I Wish I'd Had
sessions.abstract:
I was terrified of being a CS major. I didn't fit the typical tech stereotype, and instead of pushing through that discomfort, I let it shrink me.  I literally thought LeetCode was a programming language. I skipped opportunities, avoided putting myself out there, and stayed as invisible as possible. On paper I was in the program. In reality I was hiding.

Junior year, I decided it was time to change things for myself. I started showing up as the person I wanted to become, even before I felt ready. And slowly, everything started to shift.

After graduating, I started hosting monthly tech panels so others wouldn't feel that same isolation. But after 5+ events, I noticed a gap: students left inspired, then went right back to job searching alone. Inspiration wasn't enough. People needed structure, accountability, and someone in their corner.

That's when I built a recruiting buddy matching system from scratch, while working full time, with no team and no roadmap. What started as a workaround for a problem I personally lived became a 500-person community I wish had existed when I was starting out.

This session is for anyone who has ever felt too hidden to start.

You'll leave knowing:

- How to start showing up in rooms where you don't yet feel like you belong

- How to spot when you need accountability, not just inspiration

- How to find people who will actually help you follow through

- How to create structure that keeps you moving between the big moments

- How to build a support system without waiting for someone else to build it for you

sessions.title: Spatial Intelligence + AI: Closing the Gap Between Strategy and the Real World
sessions.abstract:
Most business decisions have a “where” component, yet that context is often missing from traditional analytics. When businesses incorporate location, proximity, and real-world constraints into their data, insights emerge faster and decisions become more actionable - enabling organizations to uncover unmet demand, optimize networks and coverage, reduce risk, and adapt more quickly to change.

Adoption of spatial intelligence follows a maturity curve - from no geospatial usage, to fragmented tools, to scalable platforms still limited to specialist teams. Today, AI is shifting that curve by embedding spatial context directly into decision workflows. Drawing on experience working with organizations across industries, this session explores why spatial intelligence is becoming a business essential and how AI is accelerating its impact in real-world decision-making.

sessions.title: Building Your B.R.A.N.D.: A Practical Framework for Career-Focused Personal Branding in Tech
sessions.abstract: In today’s tech-driven world, your digital presence often speaks before you do. Whether you are applying for jobs, changing directions, or building credibility, personal branding plays a bigger role in your career than you might expect. Building Your B.R.A.N.D. introduces a practical framework to help technologists be intentional about how they show up online. This session focuses on turning your skills, interests, and experiences into a digital presence that reflects who you are and where you want to go. Participants will explore areas like what they want to be known for, whether their online presence aligns with their goals, and how to share their work authentically. Participants will also be introduced to tools and resources for each part of the B.R.A.N.D. framework and leave with clear next steps to audit and refine their digital presence. So, join me in building YOUR brand and taking control of your professional story!

sessions.title: Build Your AI Chief of Staff: A Hands-On Workshop for Non-Technical Women
sessions.abstract:
Most AI workshops assume you're technical. This one assumes you're busy. And the best way to learn is to DO, while solving your pain points today.

In 60 minutes, you'll build a personalized "AI Chief of Staff" — a custom AI assistant trained on your role, your communication style, and your actual workflows. No code. No jargon. Just a working tool you can use before your next meeting.

We'll build an AI Chief of Staff to help you do three main things: prioritize your day, prep for any upcoming meetings or synthesize info, and draft communications in your voice. You'll leave with a working AI assistant and a repeatable framework for finding new uses every week.

This workshop is built on a proven curriculum from Women Defining AI, a nonprofit that has trained 1,500+ non-technical professional women through hands-on AI micro-learning programming. We focus on your workflows and use cases rather than the tech. And we get hands-on from the start!

sessions.title: Soft Skills That Scale: Emotional Intelligence, Influence, and the Power of Saying No
sessions.abstract:
Some of the toughest challenges we face in our careers are not just technical. They show up when we need to push back on senior stakeholders, reset unrealistic expectations, or decline work that could introduce risk. Yet saying "no" can feel risky, like we may be seen as difficult, not collaborative, or not ready for the next level.

As roles grow more complex, success depends not only on technical excellence but also on emotional intelligence, communication, and the ability to influence outcomes. 

This session explores why many technical professionals hesitate to speak up, how unspoken expectations shape decisions, and how defaulting to “yes” can quietly limit career growth and lead to burnout.

Through realistic scenarios, guided reflection, and repeatable techniques, attendees will gain practical tools to set expectations, say “no” without damaging trust, and communicate with confidence in high-stakes situations, strengthening relationships and supporting continued career growth.

sessions.title: From APIs to Agents: Translating Backend Architecture into Agent Workflows
sessions.abstract:
Agentic AI can feel like an entirely new discipline. When I transitioned from backend engineering into machine learning engineering, that is exactly how it felt. The breakthrough came from recognizing that production agents are still software systems. They ingest data through APIs, move through structured workflows, route decisions, call downstream services, and manage state under failure conditions.
In this session, I translate five core backend design patterns into their agentic equivalents. Using a vendor-agnostic email triage-and-action agent that ingests customer emails, classifies intent, triggers downstream services, and generates structured responses, I demonstrate how these familiar patterns evolve when an LLM becomes part of the workflow.
Attendees leave with a five-pattern mapping framework and a practical readiness rubric they can apply directly to systems they already build, allowing them to approach agent development with the skills they already possess.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Invisible to Influential: Owning Your Voice in High-Stakes Rooms
sessions.abstract:
In many high-stakes rooms, talented women and nonbinary technologists do the work, but their ideas land last—or not at all. This session equips attendees with a practical playbook to move from feeling invisible to becoming a trusted, influential voice when it matters most. Drawing on real stories from engineering and product decision rooms, we’ll unpack the subtle dynamics that mute voices and translate them into specific, doable power moves.

Participants will learn three core skills: (1) how to enter the conversation early and with clarity, (2) how to make ideas “stick” using strategic framing and cite-and-build techniques, and (3) how to project authority through body language, vocal choices, and concise language—even when you’re the only one in the room who looks like you. Attendees will leave with a repeatable toolkit to advocate for their ideas, amplify others, and create a ripple effect for more equitable, inclusive decision-making in their own organizations.

sessions.title: Unlocking Grants: How to Find, Apply, and Build with Non-Dilutive Capital
sessions.abstract:
Access to capital remains a critical barrier for many technologists, founders, and researchers—especially women and non-binary professionals. Grants offer a powerful yet often underutilized pathway to fund innovation without equity loss or repayment pressure.

This interactive workshop demystifies the grant landscape by breaking down what grants are, how they differ from funding and fellowships, and when to leverage them. Participants will explore examples of research, startup, and corporate grant programs, including cloud and infrastructure credits offered by major technology companies.

Through hands-on exercises, attendees will analyze sample grant applications, identify grants aligned with their goals, and map how grants can be used strategically to build products, conduct research, or scale impact—without the constraints of traditional funding. By the end of the session, participants will leave with an action plan and practical tools to pursue grants confidently and effectively.

sessions.title: The Conference Aftermath: Leveraging Follow-ups To Solidify Your Next Opportunity
sessions.abstract:
How I secured 56 client leads: The conference may have ended, but your journey is just beginning. True networking isn’t just about making connections, it’s about nurturing them into meaningful, lasting opportunities. Long after the buzz dies down and the recap posts fade, how do you ensure that a handshake or LinkedIn request evolves into a powerful professional relationship?

This dynamic session equips leaders with actionable strategies and tangible tools to transform their follow-ups into career-defining moments. Whether you're solidifying new partnerships, exploring career advancements, or expanding your influence, this session will help you turn every introduction into a next-level opportunity.

sessions.title: Start Anyway: How Unplanned Paths Lead to Cyber Careers
sessions.abstract:
Most people assume there is a clear path into cybersecurity. There is not. And that is actually good news.

This talk is for anyone who has ever felt behind, underqualified, or unsure what move to make next. It starts with a story: in high school, I was featured in the CodeGirl documentary for building an app that solved a real community problem. I had no idea that moment would eventually lead me to product security. The path from there was not straight. It went through computer science, embedded systems, and a few wrong turns before landing where I am now.

Security careers rarely follow a script. The field moves too fast, the roles are too varied, and the best practitioners usually came from somewhere unexpected. That is not a bug. That is how the industry works.

You will leave with frameworks for building skills with intent, growing influence without a title, and spotting your next move before someone hands it to you.

sessions.title: When You Don’t Own the Team but Own the Outcome: Building Trust and Influence Across Cultures
sessions.abstract: “What makes a leader when you must influence teams without having them on your org chart?” How do you lead, earn trust, and drive results - without caring about hierarchy or titles? In today’s global, matrixed tech world, many professionals face this challenge every day. Panelists from Microsoft, Siemens, Braze, and Hitachi Energy dive into real-world stories, frameworks, and strategies for leading across teams and cultures, navigating tough trade-offs, and aligning stakeholders when you don’t “own” the team. Through candid examples and myth-busting insights, attendees will leave with actionable tools to influence outcomes, spark collaboration, and deliver impact!

speakers.name: Rushal Sharma
speakers.title: Digital Innovation Strategist, Office of the CTO

sessions.title: Beyond Hiring: Non-technical Training and Job‑Fair Pairing That Accelerate Early Careers
sessions.abstract:
Most early‑career programs focus on technical onboarding, but Bloomberg’s Entry-Level Engineering Training Program goes far beyond that. In this session, attendees will learn how our seven‑week training program integrates essential non-technical development: networking, professionalism, communication, and philanthropy, to build confident, well‑rounded engineers. What makes our model unique is the general offer structure paired with a job fair, team shadowing, and a mutual matching process. 

This two‑sided approach empowers new engineers to explore roles thoughtfully, while also helping teams select candidates who are aligned with and motivated by their focus. By combining non-technical skill‑building with a human‑centered placement model, we accelerate early‑career success and create stronger long‑term matches for talent and teams.

sessions.title: Shift Left on Strategy: The "Shadow Board" Framework for Scaling IC Influence
sessions.abstract:
Why are critical technical insights often the last to reach leadership? In many organizations, a "Clarity Gap" exists between engineers writing code and leaders setting strategy, killing velocity.

Enter the Shadow Board: a strategic advisory body of Individual Contributors (ICs) bridging the divide. Using a framework that scaled from a 200-person pilot to a 650-person pillar at Workday, this session reveals how to "hack" corporate hierarchy to drive technical excellence. Discover how an IC-led board provided the "unfiltered" technical truth that drove a 50% reduction in code freezes and optimized incident response.

Whether you’re an IC seeking influence or a leader needing a competitive edge, you’ll leave with an Operational Blueprint to:
- Design the Board: Selection criteria, global scaling, and balancing.
- Execute the Pulse Check: A repeatable system turning sentiment into executive action.
- Architect the Pipeline: Cultivating strategic leaders through structured shadowing

sessions.title: 5 Techniques to Stop AI Agent Hallucinations
sessions.abstract:
AI agents hallucinate in four distinct ways: fabricating data from approximate search, picking wrong tools, ignoring business rules, and claiming success on failed operations.

In this workshop, you'll tackle all four failure modes with production-tested techniques. Starting with Graph-RAG to replace vector search with structured knowledge graphs for precise data retrieval, then semantic tool selection using FAISS to dynamically filter dozens of tools to the most relevant per query.

Next, neurosymbolic guardrails that enforce business rules through verifiable code the LLM cannot bypass. Then, runtime steering that allows the agent to self-correct instead of blocking when it violates operational rules. Finally, multi-agent validation where specialized agents cross-check each other's work through structured debate.

Using a travel booking agent as our running example, each technique builds on the previous one. You'll leave with five reusable patterns and a decision framework for choosing which techniques to apply based on your specific hallucination challenges. Laptop with Python 3.9+ required.

sessions.title: Accelerating LLMs on GPU: Techniques and Tools for Speed
sessions.abstract: Making LLMs like Gemma performant on GPUs is crucial for broader adoption. This session outlines a practical approach to optimizing LLM inference and training on GPUs using widely available tools and techniques. We, Google XLA:GPU engineers, will guide you through a complete optimization journey: from identifying bottlenecks using accessible profiling tools, through applying powerful optimization techniques like kernel fusion and quantization, debugging performance issues, and finally, validating improvements. Attendees will learn how to leverage these methods to achieve significant speedups and efficiency gains for their AI workloads on GPUs.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Designing at Scale: How to Stand Out in System Design Interviews
sessions.abstract:
System design interviews are not about reciting patterns -- they’re about demonstrating engineering judgment.
In this technical deep dive led by an Uber Engineering Manager and Senior Engineer, we explore what strong system design performance looks like today: structured decomposition, explicit trade-offs, scalability planning, and resilience under real-world constraints. Drawing from large-scale architectural patterns inspired by Uber’s production systems, we examine how to reason through consistency models, sharding strategies, fault tolerance, and event-driven architectures — and how to articulate those decisions clearly in high-stakes interviews. Attendees will leave with a practical framework for approaching complex system design problems with depth, clarity, and confidence. 

This builds upon the workshop we hosted at GHC 2024, where we helped participants navigate the system design interview at a higher level. In contrast, this offers a deep dive into the technical details.

sessions.title: A Bug's Life: Being the Engineer People Call at 2 AM
sessions.abstract: You know the engineer - the one people call when systems are down, alerts are firing, and the fix isn't obvious. Becoming that person is about judgment under pressure, clear communication, and building systems that are debuggable. This panel explores what it really means to be a trusted escalation point on modern engineering teams. Through real-world stories from on-call rotations, production incidents, and launches, panelists will unpack how engineers earn trust, debug effectively, and balance ownership with sustainability. The session will include interactive bug scenarios where attendees can reason through issues alongside the panel, followed by discussion of how experienced engineers approach diagnosis, decision-making, and resolution. Attendees will gain insight into both the technical and interpersonal skills required to handle high-pressure incidents so the "2 AM engineer" doesn't burn out.

sessions.title: Emotionally Intelligent Leadership in the Age of AI: Trust, Resilience, Human-Centered Innovation
sessions.abstract:
Generative AI is reshaping enterprise systems, workflows, and decision-making, and leadership must evolve with it. Technical expertise alone is no longer enough. Leaders need emotional intelligence to manage resistance, create psychological safety, and enable responsible AI adoption at scale.

Drawing from real-world enterprise transformations, this session presents a practical leadership framework built on four capabilities: empathy in change management, alignment between technical and business stakeholders, clarity in AI strategy communication, and strong cross-functional connection.

We will explore how emotionally intelligent leaders reduce adoption friction, accelerate buy-in, foster safety during automation-driven change, align AI initiatives with human-centered design, and balance data-driven decisions with trust-based leadership.

Attendees will gain actionable strategies to build high-performing, AI-enabled teams grounded in trust, inclusion, and innovation.

speakers.name: Tanvi Hungund
speakers.title: Senior Manager, Customer Solutions, Digital Native Business

sessions.title: Doing the Scary Thing First: How Engineers Can Grow at Every Level
sessions.abstract:
Regardless of where they are in their career, engineers often feel like they should wait for confidence and clarity before taking ownership. But in reality, high-impact work and growth opportunities don’t wait. These moments appear throughout an engineering career. From submitting your first PR to leading a cross-team effort, growth often shows up disguised as discomfort.
When engineers hold back instead of leaning into the unknown, they lose time, stall their career development, and miss chances to make meaningful impact.
In this workshop, attendees will reflect on their own success (of any size!) to pinpoint factors that made those wins possible. Using a third-person lens, they’ll practice coaching a friend through a tough scenario, then apply the same method to a real challenge they’re facing to map out concrete next steps. 
Attendees will leave with an actionable plan for a task they’ve been avoiding, as well as a repeatable approach for confidently taking ownership under pressure.

sessions.title: Ransomware Recovery Resilience: Building Tamper-Proof Backup Infrastructure with AWS
sessions.abstract: In an era of escalating cyber threats, recovery resilience is paramount. This session delivers actionable strategies for fortifying backup infrastructure aligned with NIST CSF 2.0, focusing on three critical pillars: immutability with isolation, integrity validation, and predictable availability. Attendees will discover how AWS Backup's Vault Lock creates tamper-proof backups, while restore testing ensures integrity assurance. Explore integration with partner solutions for enhanced forensic analysis and business continuity.Whether you're architecting resilient systems or responding to security events, you'll gain concrete techniques to enhance your recovery posture and maintain operational continuity in the face of sophisticated attacks.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Accessibility in practice: Designing Under Constraint with AI Support
sessions.abstract:
Accessibility in product development is rarely just about applying guidelines. It is shaped by timelines, technical debt, resource limits, and stakeholder negotiation. Designers are asked to advocate for inclusion while working within systems that prioritize speed and scale. This workshop recreates that tension. Participants audit familiar consumer apps using a four lens framework: vision, motor, cognitive, and automation. In cross-functional teams, they receive limited accessibility budgets and stakeholder roles. Apart from fixing everything, they must prioritize, justify tradeoffs and defend decisions using product language.
Midway, AI is introduced as a decision-support tool to surface blind spots and alternatives, while participants evaluate its limits. The session concludes with a facilitated critique, where teams defend their choices and reflect on how accessibility is negotiated in real organizations. Attendees leave with a repeatable framework and practical advocacy skills.

sessions.title: Mastering Production Readiness: A Capacity Planning Blueprint
sessions.abstract:
Launching a global digital platform housing over 25 years of research and more than one million reports requires infrastructure engineered for extreme scale and performance. In this session, we present a real world case study demonstrating how data driven capacity planning enabled a successful go live and delivered a significantly improved user experience worldwide.

We will examine the risks of under and over provisioning critical components and share a practical methodology that moves beyond guesswork. Attendees will learn how we sized diverse content types, analyzed historical access patterns, and translated empirical data into concrete infrastructure decisions, including strategic upgrades and post launch optimization.

Designed for engineers, architects, and operations professionals, this session offers actionable insights into proactive performance engineering and best practices for balancing performance, stability, and cost efficiency in high traffic system launches.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: AI-Powered SDLC: Faster, Smarter, and Inherently Resilient
sessions.abstract: In an era where speed is the new currency and software is the heartbeat of innovation, SDLC is being reimagined through AI. An AI driven SDLC integrates intelligent automation & machine learning across every phase - from requirements & design to coding, testing, deployment, & operations. This transformation increases velocity while improving software quality & developer experience, the ultimate self-optimizing delivery engine. This session explores how AI is reshaping modern SDLC workflows through AI-assisted analysis, code generation, autonomous testing, intelligent CI/CD pipelines, & predictive AIOps. Real world case studies highlight measurable outcomes, such as reduced cycle time, faster incident resolution & improved code quality. Attendees will gain practical guidance for scaling AI responsibly & fostering a culture where humans & AI collaborate as one engineering force, proving the future of software delivery is not just automated, but adaptive, anticipatory, & AI-empowered.

sessions.title: Owning the AI Economy: Turning Women's Expertise into Equity
sessions.abstract: Women have been told the AI economy is full of opportunity. What they haven't been told: their expertise, data, and labor are actively building that economy, and they're not getting equity in return. This session exposes the participation trap: the structural pattern where women contribute to AI systems as users, testers, and knowledge sources while the economic value flows elsewhere. Then it presents a working alternative. Empressa AI's royalty model pays women experts every time their knowledge powers the AI, turning contribution into ownership. Attendees will leave with a framework for auditing where their expertise is being extracted versus rewarded, and concrete strategies to position themselves as economic stakeholders in the AI systems they help build.

sessions.title: Resume Optimization for AI-Era Roles: How to Stand Out Without Overclaiming
sessions.abstract:
As AI transforms job descriptions and hiring expectations, many students and early career professionals struggle to position their skills effectively. Should you list AI tools? Highlight automation? Emphasize technical depth?

This session provides a practical framework for optimizing resumes for AI-era roles. Participants will learn how recruiters interpret AI-related experience, how to frame projects responsibly, how to demonstrate impact without inflating expertise, and how to avoid common AI-era resume mistakes. Attendees leave with a clear checklist to strengthen their resume immediately and increase interview conversion rates.

sessions.title: Interviewing for 2027: Master the "Thinker" Mindset to Clear the AI-Native Bar
sessions.abstract: By 2027, the "coding interview" will be extinct and be replaced by the "thinking interview." As AI handles the syntax and rote coordination, companies are raising the bar for architectural intent, programmatic orchestration, and strategic oversight. This workshop provides a hands-on playbook for both entry-level and mid-level SWEs, Data Scientists, and TPMs to master the AI-Native Bar. Participants will learn to move from being "builders" to "orchestrators," demonstrating the high-level reasoning and human-in-the-loop ethics that no LLM can replicate.

speakers.name: Diana Zhang
speakers.title: Director, Technical Program Management/Chief of Staff

sessions.title: Bootstrapped, Not Broken: How to Build and Scale Tech Companies Without Venture Capital
sessions.abstract:
Venture capital is often treated as the default path to building a successful tech startup but it is only one form of capital, and not always the most accessible or strategic, especially in the early stages. 

This session shares a practical, experience-driven playbook for building and scaling tech companies without relying on VC, by designing for capital efficiency, resilience, and early profitability from day one.

Drawing from real-world founder experience, the talk introduces five levers of capital-efficient startup building: 
- assembling aligned teams through equity, 
- leveraging global talent, 
- unlocking customer-funded growth through partnerships and early revenue, 
- fine-tuning business models for profitability, and 
- prioritizing founder sustainability - including paying yourself.

Attendees will leave with concrete frameworks and decision tools to move from idea to product-market fit and scale on their own terms.

sessions.title: The Insider's Guide for Women in Tech: Navigating Today's Job Market with Confidence
sessions.abstract:
In today’s rapidly evolving job market, women in tech are navigating both unprecedented opportunity and increasing complexity. From shifting hiring expectations to evolving technical skill demands, standing out requires more than a strong resume: it requires strategy, confidence, and connection.
Led by Nicole Kaiser, this session will provide practical, real-world guidance to help attendees successfully position themselves for career growth in today’s competitive landscape. Drawing from direct experience supporting hiring and talent strategy, Nicole will share actionable insights on how candidates can align their skills with market demand, effectively tell their career story, and build meaningful connections that translate into opportunity.

speakers.name: Nicole Kaiser
speakers.title: Executive Search Partner & Senior Talent Scout

sessions.title: Celebrating Black Technologists
sessions.abstract: Excellence, innovation, and community in action! Join us for an inspiring celebration dedicated to elevating Black technologists who are shaping the future of the industry. This is your space to connect with brilliant minds, exchange ideas, and build the meaningful networks and leadership opportunities that move our community forward.

sessions.title: Building Influence Without Losing Yourself
sessions.abstract: This empowering workshop helps women in tech understand how power and influence work beyond job titles, and how to build credibility without compromising their values or authenticity. Participants will learn practical strategies for relationship-building, gaining buy-in for technical ideas, and confidently being heard in meetings—equipping them to increase visibility, shape decisions, and lead with impact in complex workplace environments.

sessions.title: Agentic AI for Breast Cancer Detection Using Wavelet Multi-View Learning and Spatial Transcriptomics
sessions.abstract: This presentation introduces an agentic AI framework for histopathological breast cancer detection that integrates wavelet-enhanced deep learning with spatial transcriptomic analysis. The session demonstrates how multi-scale features are extracted from whole-slide histopathology images using wavelet-enhanced convolutional neural networks, while high-dimensional gene expression data are analyzed through interpretable linear algebra techniques including Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), and Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (NMF). An agentic decision module autonomously evaluates reconstruction error, variance preservation, and numerical stability to select optimal representations across modalities. The presentation emphasizes mathematical rigor, interpretability, and clinical relevance, illustrating how applied linear algebra and agentic reasoning can improve diagnostic precision and transparency in healthcare AI systems.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Elevate Your Leadership Presence: Using Public Speaking to Command the Room
sessions.abstract: In today’s fast-moving business world, the ability to communicate effectively is a cornerstone of successful leadership. This program provides actionable strategies to help leaders improve their public speaking skills and build a confident, commanding presence. Designed to equip participants with the tools to confidently engage any audience, share compelling stories, and elevate their leadership presence. It will help improve skills needed to communicate confidently, lead with impact, and engage with their teams and stakeholders in a powerful way.

sessions.title: AI-Driven Mobile Apps in 2026: Patterns, Practices, and Practical Insights
sessions.abstract:
Mobile apps are evolving into intelligent, AI-powered experiences. But moving from an "AI wrapper" to a production-ready feature takes more than calling a model — it requires managing on-device inference, non-deterministic behavior, and a model that now ships with the OS itself. In this session, Divya Ravi, Senior iOS Engineer, breaks down the architecture of AI-driven iOS applications in the post-WWDC26 landscape.

We'll cover the on-device Foundation Models framework and Core ML, the real trade-offs between on-device, private-cloud, and third-party models, and the discipline that separates demos from shipping products: evaluating non-deterministic systems and securing agentic features against new risks like prompt injection. Whether you're a mid-level or senior engineer, you'll leave with a practical blueprint for building scalable, maintainable, and trustworthy AI features.

Beyond the code, Divya will share how mastering these emerging technologies can accelerate your career and position you as a technical leader in the AI era.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Breaking into Tech: The Missing Puzzle Piece
sessions.abstract:
Breaking into tech isn’t just about having a degree or maintaining a GPA. Degrees don’t differentiate candidates. Strategy does. We learned that through trial and error. As recent graduates, we’ve navigated this process firsthand, spent our undergraduate years figuring out what actually matters, and we’re not gatekeeping any of it.

This career-focused session is a one-stop guide for early-career professionals. We’ll walk through how to set yourself up for success by building transferable skills, taking leadership in academic projects, and turning experiences like hackathons, internships, and research roles into real career momentum. You’ll learn what actually opens doors, how to intentionally network, and why genuine connections and referrals beat automated applications every time.

You’ll hear from recent graduates who were in your shoes not long ago and have successfully navigated this path, and leave with actionable strategies to turn undergrad into a launchpad for tech careers.

sessions.title: From PM to Strategic Leader: Making the Shift from Delivery to Decision-Making
sessions.abstract: Strategic leadership is not defined by titles. It shows up in how decisions are made every day. This session helps experienced PMs see what separates delivery-focused work from strategic leadership: improving decision quality, thinking in second-order effects, and balancing near-term execution with long-term vision. You will leave with a practical way to audit your own decisions and start operating at the next level before the title arrives.

sessions.title: From Coworkers to Copilots: The New Team Dynamic in Tech
sessions.abstract: AI is reshaping engineering culture in real time. The question is no longer whether we will work with AI, but how and what we are willing to preserve. This session puts culture at the center, about how AI is changing the way we collaborate, build trust, and grow as engineers, and what can bring balance to a hybrid future of working with both AI and humans.

sessions.title: What can AI mean for my Professional Development & career?
sessions.abstract:
With rapid growth in Artificial Intelligence the type of career roles in technology are rapidly changing. Almost all domains can likely adopt AI driven processes in the future making the professional impact of this AI boom widespread. This gives rise to a need to understand how AI may affect your field, the new kind of professional tracks emerging due to AI and how one can best leverage their existing skills to adapt to the new professional development needed. This session would provide a "live-from-the-battle-field" point-of-view of this redesign in professional careers (in Technology) instead of the point-of-view of higher-leadership. Whether you are a senior professional trying to leverage AI for strategic improvement of your company's product or a early-in-career individual trying to circumvent the loss of coding jobs due to AI tools.
The session will also provide some actionable steps that can be adopted to hone skills that might be needed in this new emergent AI driven field.

sessions.title: "But Are You Actually Technical?" Navigating Career Identity in Tech
sessions.abstract:
Here's an uncomfortable question shaping tech careers: Are marketing, product marketing, and GTM professionals "technical people"? We translate DevSecOps concepts, position AI capabilities, enable sales on complex architectures—yet we're often excluded from the "technical" label. This isn't philosophical, it directly impacts positioning, compensation, and career progression.

This session tackles tech's false binary between "technical" and "non-technical" roles. We'll explore how technical credibility affects mobility and promotions, positioning for technical leadership without engineering titles, and building authentic career narratives. This isn't about proving you're technical enough—it's equipping you with language and frameworks to advance in an industry that undervalues technical skills outside engineering.

sessions.title: If You Can't Measure It, You Can't Trust It : AI Quality in Practice
sessions.abstract:
AI is everywhere in enterprise products - answering questions, generating recommendations, and acting on its own. Teams ship fast. The result? Hallucinations reach users, quality silently degrades, and bias by gender, race, or age goes undetected until it's too late.

I share how quality engineering and data science partnered to build an AI quality program from scratch - evolving from evaluation into red-teaming, safety guardrails, and now Disparate Impact Analysis.

I'll walk you through three layers: (1) a reproducible evaluation pipeline measuring whether AI outputs are accurate, context-grounded, and relevant; (2) adversarial red-teaming and guardrails that stress-test AI agents before release; and (3) Disparate Impact Analysis, in progress, comparing outputs across demographic groups to make fairness a permanent quality gate.

Whether you're a QA engineer, data scientist, or leader building AI accountability, you'll leave with practical templates you can use.

sessions.title: Accelerate Without Limits: Unleashing Next-Gen Model Scaling Across JAX and PyTorch with Keras
sessions.abstract:
How do industry leaders train models with billions of parameters that physically cannot fit on a single GPU? Simple distribution is no longer enough in this era of LLMs; the world’s most advanced AI relies on something more powerful: multi-dimensional sharding.

This session pulls back the curtain on the "Next-Gen" of distributed training. You will discover how to orchestrate massive scale training across JAX and PyTorch using a single, unified codebase. We will move beyond basic parallelism techniques to explore the magic of Tensor Parallelism and automated sharding.

Learn to transform a cluster of accelerators into one logical super machine using a Device Mesh. Whether you are looking to speed up training or architect models that are too big to train, this talk provides the blueprint for scaling without framework lock-in. Leave with the skills to implement autosharding and hybrid parallelism, ensuring your AI infrastructure is future-proof and ready for the billion-parameter era.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: From Web Pages to Research Pipelines: Building Ethical Data Collection Systems
sessions.abstract:
Modern research, AI systems, and data-driven products all depend on one thing: data. But where does that data come from—and who is responsible for collecting it ethically? This session introduces web scraping as a rigorous data collection method and demonstrates how professionals can build reproducible, responsible data pipelines directly from the web. Drawing from a university course on ethical web data collection, we explore how to navigate HTML structure, automate browsers, and design scalable scraping workflows while addressing privacy, bias, and data stewardship.
This session is especially relevant for data scientists, ML engineers, software engineers, UX researchers, and responsible AI professionals who want to move beyond consuming datasets to building them responsibly. Attendees will gain a practical framework for deciding when and how to collect web data ethically, transforming raw online information into research-ready datasets while minimizing risk and maximizing integrity.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Creating Shared Space: How Young Women Build Belonging in Tech
sessions.abstract: Young women in tech often learn that success depends not only on skill, but on finding spaces where they feel seen and supported. This youth-centered panel features current and former STEM Next Flight Crew members sharing what helped them build confidence, belonging, and momentum early in their tech career pathways. Through an open conversation moderated by a seasoned leader in tech, panelists will reflect on what supported them, what got in their way, and how they created spaces where they could see themselves thrive. Students will hear relatable stories about navigating gendered spaces in STEM and sustaining early interests into college and beyond. Attendees will leave with practical insights and encouragement for building community, finding support, and continuing their own journeys in technology.

sessions.title: Strategic Revenue Leadership: Leveraging AI and Technical Expertise to Pivot into Cloud Sales
sessions.abstract:
As AI automates routine tasks in customer-facing technical roles such as Technical Account Managers, Customer Success Managers, Solutions Architects, Technical Success Engineers, and Cloud Success positions across cloud and SaaS this creates strategic openings in consultative sales, where technical depth drives revenue ownership and leadership. Drawing from experience as an AWS TAM supporting startups/enterprises and contributing to Sales Accelerator premium support upsells, this session shows how women can strategically pivot into high-impact sales roles.
Tech sales is a powerful career accelerator delivering 20%+ revenue uplift from diverse teams, uncapped earnings, and executive paths in AI/cloud ecosystems. It addresses women’s hesitations (male-dominated cultures, confidence gaps, bias in promotions, rejection fears, aggressive stereotypes) by reframing sales as empowering: leverage existing technical/customer-facing skills + AI tools overcome barriers, and drive equitable growth.

sessions.title: From the Ground Up: Engineers Leading Inclusive Programs Without Formal Authority
sessions.abstract:
Mentorship, career development, and inclusion programs are most effective when built by the engineers they are meant to support. Yet, those who experience these gaps most acutely are often individual contributors without the authority, resources, or roadmap to drive change. How can early-career engineers take action and advocate for what they need without formal power?
In this panel, four engineers will share how a grassroots, engineer-led inclusion effort grew into a department-level program focused on mentorship, career growth, and community. We’ll discuss how first-hand experience surfaced real needs, how leadership emerged organically, and how structure and strategy helped these initiatives scale.
Through candid lessons on turning intent into impact, navigating leadership without authority, and avoiding burnout, this session aims to equip attendees with the tools and confidence to drive the cultural change they want to see.

sessions.title: Reclaiming Power and Resilience in the AI-Driven 'Efficiency Era’
sessions.abstract: The technology sector is undergoing a structural "Efficiency Era," with over 600,000 jobs lost in January alone and AI cited as a primary driver. For mid-career women (8–15 years), this creates a unique "double-bind": statistically more vulnerable to layoffs (1.6x more likely) while juggling disproportionate "sandwich generation" caregiving and a "broken rung" in executive advancement. This panel moves beyond "survival" to offer a proactive Recession-Proof Toolkit. Attendees will learn how to audit their role's AI-vulnerability, build financial sovereignty through "Portfolio Careers," and leverage complex human leadership as their most un-automatable asset. The discussion will deliver actionable strategies for professional fortification, focused on skills, financial prudence, and radical self-nurturing.

sessions.title: Both Sides of the Table: Cracking Tech Interviews in the AI Era
sessions.abstract:
Everyone walks into technical interviews more prepared than ever. AI-generated solutions. Polished answers. Clean code. And yet — more candidates are getting rejected.
Because companies didn't lower the bar. They shifted it.
The coding round looks familiar. The scoring doesn't. What earns a hire decision today is reasoning out loud, defending your choices under follow-up, and navigating ambiguity in real time. These are exactly the things AI cannot do for you in
the room.
Two engineers — with 20+ years of combined experience and hundreds of interviews from both sides of the table — break down what has actually changed, what hasn't, and what a strong candidate looks like right now.
Across coding, system design, AI/ML design, and behavioral rounds, you'll learn exactly what separates a hire from a no-hire in the AI era — and leave with a concrete framework to prepare for each one.
You have AI. Now learn what to do with it.

sessions.title: Build Resilient Systems at Scale: Hands-On Workflow Orchestration with Cadence
sessions.abstract:
What if you could develop a backend service that never forgets it's state, is resilient to failures, and scales to billions of executions, without building retry logic, state machines, or recovery systems yourself?

In this hands-on workshop, we’ll introduce Cadence, Uber’s Open-Source workflow Orchestration Engine powering 1000+ services and 12B+ executions monthly. It's a proven, battle-tested robust system trusted by some of the world’s most demanding distributed architectures. You will build a real workflow using native code and experience how durability, retries and fault tolerance come built-in.

Whether you're a backend engineer, distributed systems enthusiast, or reliability-focused developer, this session will demystify workflow orchestration and show how to design stateful, scalable systems you can rely on. Gain hands-on experience building production-grade, resilient services.

speakers.name: Satya Chandana Snehal Mattaparti
speakers.title: CS Graduate | Software Engineer | Open to Full-Time Opportunities

sessions.title: A11y All Week: Daily Practices for Developers
sessions.abstract: Web accessibility is not a one-time fix; it is a daily practice that directly shapes how users experience the digital world. With one in four U.S. adults living with a disability, developers have a meaningful opportunity to improve usability through small, consistent choices. This lecture introduces a simple weekly framework designed to make accessibility skills easier to build and maintain. Seven practical techniques, each immediately applicable, will be demonstrated to provide a repeatable routine that helps accessibility become a natural part of the development process. Participants will learn how decisions like semantic code structure, thoughtful color selection, and effective navigation patterns contribute to more inclusive user experiences. By strengthening these foundational skills, attendees will be better equipped to create digital products that are reliable, user friendly, and accessible to all.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: AI Didn't Give Me Answers. It Gave Me Standing.
sessions.abstract:
Earlier this year my father broke his hip. At his age and with his complications, he was facing a 50% mortality rate. I took two months of leave and moved back to Oregon to care for him.

I am a data scientist, not a clinician, and I did not understand a single line of his medical records when I started reading them. By the end of those two months I had found a diagnosis that had been sitting in his chart for two years, reversed the malnutrition that was slowly starving him, gotten him hearing aids he had refused for years, moved him somewhere better, and more than doubled his income through a VA claim that 70% of applicants lose.

AI did not make me smarter. It made me credible enough to keep asking after his doctor told me no three times.

I will walk through what I did, where it got things wrong, and how to build that fluency now, before you are the one sitting in the hospital chair.

sessions.title: Her Tech, Her Time!!
sessions.abstract: Modern digital transformation demands more than new technology - it requires rethinking architecture, delivery, and leadership. This session presents a real-world case study of evolving a large-scale digital ordering platform from legacy constraints to a modern, modular architecture using Orders 2.0 and GMA 8. Attendees will explore backend-driven design, platform orchestration, governance models, and pilot-driven risk reduction, while learning how a team of women led critical technical and operational decisions. The talk blends deep technical insight with leadership lessons, showing how women are driving scalable, resilient digital platforms used by millions.

sessions.title: Don't Panic! Your First On-Call Survival Guide
sessions.abstract:
RING RING RING
It’s 2:07 AM. Your phone is buzzing. Production is on fire. Dashboards are red. Customers are impacted. You’re on-call.
For many new engineers, on-call is the first time you truly own a real-time production issue — one that affects real users, real money, and real business outcomes. It’s exciting…but honestly a little terrifying.
While many teams provide technical onboarding, new engineers still often feel unprepared for the real-world pressures they’re going to face. In this workshop, we’ll introduce what actually happens during on-call, explore how to respond when alerts fire, and give tips on writing clear post-mortems. Afterwards, you’ll get a chance to practice these skills in an engaging, interactive incident simulation where you will face realistic incidents, make decisions, and learn that there are no perfect answers, only thoughtful trade-offs.
Join us for this workshop to build confidence as you practice triaging issues and communicating clearly under pressure.

sessions.title: Sazón & Strategy: A Latina’s Recipe for Thriving in Tech, Motherhood, and Remote Work
sessions.abstract:
Tech success is often defined without considering the realities Latina women face while balancing culture, caregiving, and remote work. In this interactive workshop, Melissa Delgado blends lived experience with practical strategy to help attendees design careers that are both ambitious and sustainable. 

Using the metaphor of sazón, the personal flavor shaped by culture, values, and life stage, participants will explore how to lead with authenticity, set boundaries without guilt, and navigate remote work without becoming invisible.

Attendees will leave with actionable tools to season their careers with intention, align success with their realities, and build a definition of growth that supports both professional impact and personal well-being. Exploring how to season their careers with authenticity.

sessions.title: Back at The Table: Engineering Your Influence After a Career Reset in Today’s Tech Landscape
sessions.abstract:
Re-entering the tech workforce after a career gap is a complex challenge requiring recalibrating both technical “hard” skills and strategic “soft” power. Join two alumni from the Morgan Stanley Return to Work program as we share our experiences navigating a successful return to today's evolving tech landscape.
We’ll walk through the journey of returning to tech, from refreshing technical skills, to navigating team dynamics and making the first months back productive and confident. Through honest stories, practical advice, and lessons learned along the way, we’ll explore how past experiences can become a strength when stepping back into tech.
Attendees will leave with a clearer sense of how to close skill gaps, regain momentum, and approach the first months back with intention. Whether you’re getting hands-on, moving into delivery or project management, or figuring out where you fit in today’s industry, this session offers a real-world perspective on making a successful return.

sessions.title: Stand Out in the Stack: Writing Technical Achievements That Sell Your Skills
sessions.abstract: You've built the skills, but is your job search strategy working as hard as you are? Landing a tech role takes more than technical ability; it demands a compelling resume, a strategic LinkedIn presence, and a focused search plan. Yet many students and early-career professional struggle: generic resumes get filtered out by applicant tracking systems, LinkedIn profiles sit dormant, and searches feel aimless. In this workshop we tackle all three. We start with resume fundamentals: structuring a technical resume that passes ATS screening, quantifying impact with strong bullet points, and tailoring to target roles. Next, LinkedIn strategy: optimizing your headline, summary, and skills for recruiter visibility, building presence, and leveraging connections. Then participants bring their resume for a live peer review using a structured rubric. Attendees leave with a polished resume, an actionable LinkedIn optimization checklist, and a focused 30-day job search action plan.

sessions.title: Build Your First AI Agent: A Hands-On Workshop for Women in Tech
sessions.abstract: This hands-on workshop demystifies agentic AI by guiding participants through building a real, working AI agent from scratch. Using open source frameworks and cloud-based tools, attendees will construct an intelligent agent capable of reasoning through multi-step problems and producing actionable outputs — all within a realistic healthcare compliance scenario. No prior AI experience is required, just basic Python familiarity and a laptop. Participants leave with working code they can adapt, a clear mental model of agentic AI architecture, and the practical skills to start building intelligent automation in their own organizations. This session is designed to empower more women technologists to be builders, not just consumers, of AI.

speakers.name: Eva Donaldson
speakers.title: Technical Account Manager -- Healthcare / Life Sciences

sessions.title: From College to Career: The Blueprint for Engineering Excellence
sessions.abstract: This session guides students and interns through the journey from early experiences to real-world career impact. Drawing on my high-engagement student background, defined by extensive involvement in competitions, research, internships, and leadership, I’ll share the exact strategies I used to turn these proactive efforts into actionable experience and accelerated career results. I will reveal how to strategically shift your focus from academic exercises to solving real-world, meaningful problems. Students will learn what to do now to build a competitive, career-ready profile and secure that first role. Interns will learn how to leverage their internship to exceed expectations, contribute meaningfully, and accelerate growth. Participants will walk away with an actionable framework to prepare effectively, perform confidently, and make an accelerated impact early in their tech careers.

sessions.title: The Path to Chief Data & AI Officer
sessions.abstract:
The Chief Data and AI Officer role is evolving rapidly as organizations move from experimentation to enterprise-scale AI. We need to empower more women to step into these leadership roles, especially when only an estimated 15% of AI leadership positions are held by women.

This session provides a first-hand look at stepping into a CDAIO role in a rapidly changing AI landscape. Attendees will explore real experiences, the pressures of leading through constant change, and the skill sets needed to move from technologist to enterprise AI executive.

Participants will leave with a clearer understanding of what it takes to lead at the executive level in AI, including the leadership skills, decision-making mindset, and strategic influence required to move beyond technical expertise and into enterprise leadership.

sessions.title: Built for Billions: Engineering Financial Inclusion at Scale
sessions.abstract:
For most of the world, international payments are riddled with friction. For the teams building those systems, the complexity is just as real: regulatory environments that actively conflict across borders, fragmented API standards, and infrastructure constraints that no single architecture solves cleanly.

PayPal is tackling this head -on by building a global platform connecting the largest countries, billions of users, and merchants worldwide. Mudita Tiwari, Global Head of Product Management, will walk through the real tradeoffs: how to architect interoperable systems that connect markets, bring complex partner ecosystems together, navigate conflicting regulations, and deploy AI responsibly while currency moves across the world in real time. 

She'll share her path from developer to consultant to fintech product leader, and what it taught her about building for global scale without losing sight of the person on the other end of the transaction.

speakers.name: Mudita Tiwari
speakers.title: Global Head of PayPal World Product Management

sessions.title: Data Is the Model: Rethinking How We Build AI Systems
sessions.abstract:
As AI systems become more powerful, the spotlight often lands on flashy models and new tools, while data is treated as a prerequisite rather than a defining component. In reality, AI systems behave the way they do because of the data they are trained on, not just the algorithms behind them.
This session takes a data-first look at how AI systems are really built, drawing on real-world datasets, applied machine learning projects, and classroom experience. Attendees will see how data quality, representation, imbalance, and context directly shape AI performance, reliability, and trust. Using concrete examples, the talk surfaces common data pitfalls that often go unnoticed and shows how they can derail even the most sophisticated models.
By shifting the focus from “Which model should I use?” to “What data is shaping this system?”, participants will leave with a more practical, responsible, and sustainable approach to building AI.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: From HR to Tech: A Playbook for Non-Traditional Talent Entering Technical Roles
sessions.abstract: As technology continues to disrupt all aspects of the business function, HR and operations professionals increasingly find themselves working alongside product, data, and engineering teams. However, many of them often face difficulties in breaking into the technical role of the organization due to a lack of understanding of the process and the requirements. This session will provide a framework for breaking into a technical role within an organization without starting over. Based on the speaker's real-world experience in leading HR technology, analytics, and platform initiatives, the speaker will share the tools and mindset required for breaking into a technical role within an organization.

sessions.title: Building Fast, Intentional MVPs: A Framework for Strategic Execution
sessions.abstract:
Senior engineering leaders face a critical tension when building MVPs: move fast or build it right? This session delivers a framework for making strategic technical decisions while empowering your teams to execute quickly without creating unmaintainable systems.
Through a case study where my team built end-to-end video capabilities in 16 weeks, achieving double-digit engagement increases and becoming the foundation for multiple company-wide features, you'll learn systematic approaches for evaluating "hack vs invest" trade-offs, choosing which organizational dependencies to bypass, and aligning teams around a technical vision that accelerates delivery.
This is a reusable methodology you can teach your teams and apply across domains: video platforms, ML systems, payment infrastructure, or any 0-to-1 initiative. You'll leave with practical decision tools, strategies for navigating organizational complexity, and leadership practices for maintaining team alignment under tight timelines.

sessions.title: Making Presentations Land: Structure, Slides, and Social Styles
sessions.abstract:
Most presentations fail not because the ideas are weak, but because they’re poorly structured, overstuffed, or misaligned to the audience. This interactive workshop tackles why smart work so often doesn’t land and how to design presentations that do.

Led by data and AI executives Vivien Wong and Abimbola Anifowoshe, the session focuses on practical fundamentals like clarifying purpose, designing narrative flow, and using slides to reduce cognitive load rather than add it. Participants will also explore the social styles framework, expressive, driver, analytical, and amiable to understand how different audiences interpret information and persuasion.

Through guided hands-on exercises, attendees will adapt real presentations for different audiences and styles. The goal is not polish, but impact: clearer thinking, stronger signal, and presentations that move decisions forward.

speakers.name: Vivien Wong
speakers.title: AVP, AI & Data Portfolio - Global Ops, Tech & Marketing

sessions.title: From Self-Care to Squad-Care: Elevating Women’s Wellbeing in the Workplace
sessions.abstract:
Women in tech don’t lack ambition, talent, or drive. They operate inside systems that ask them to carry more while offering less in return. From invisible labor and pay gaps to burnout and barriers to advancement, these challenges rarely respond to individual effort alone. Yet much of the advice women receive still centers on self-optimization instead of structural support.

This workshop reframes wellbeing as a collective practice. Through the lens of five dimensions of workplace wellness—career, financial, community, emotional, and physical—participants will explore how connection, not just resilience, drives sustainable success. Together, we will identify the patterns that hold women back and shift toward “squad care” as a strategy for shared growth, advocacy, and advancement. Attendees will leave with practical tools to support one another, navigate workplace realities with greater clarity, and build networks that move from connection to action. Because the path forward doesn’t rely on doing more alone. It depends on how effectively we show up for each other.

sessions.title: Adaptive Access: How AI is Transforming IAM Security
sessions.abstract:
Organizations increasingly rely on identity as the security perimeter, but static IAM fails against modern attacks like MFA fatigue, credential stuffing, and insider threats. This session demonstrates how AI-driven adaptive access evaluates User → Device → Location → Behavior → Risk Score → Policy Decision in real time, enabling context-aware, risk-based access. 

Attendees will explore real-world breaches, practical frameworks for implementing adaptive IAM, and learn how AI strengthens Zero Trust, reduces false positives, and transforms identity security from reactive to proactive. 

Key takeaway: Adaptive IAM continuously validates trust.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Shared Responsibility: Building Leadership Approaches for Stronger Teams
sessions.abstract:
Strong teams don’t happen by accident. Beyond vision setting, they are shaped by the everyday choices leaders make--a shared responsibility for how teams are built, supported, and sustained. This panel brings together senior leaders from venture, enterprise, cloud and AI transformation, and social impact to explore how leadership behaviors, decision making frameworks, and operational practices shape team effectiveness, define allyship, and long term outcomes. 

Panelists will discuss how leaders move from intent to execution by embedding accountability, trust, and opportunity into daily leadership practices. Through real world examples, the conversation will examine how executives influence culture across functions and organizations, balance performance with people outcomes, and create environments where teams can thrive amid rapid change. Attendees will leave with practical ways to lead with shared responsibility and build strong teams at scale across complex, modern organizations.

speakers.name: Shawn McCarthy
speakers.title: Vice President, Architecture, Global Wealth and Asset Management Technology

sessions.title: Interview Prep Strategies
sessions.abstract: I have gotten interviews from Google, Amazon, Bloomberg, Microsoft, PwC, and eBay, and received a Research Assistant offer from Columbia University. Over the past year, I applied to 40 positions. As a first-generation, low-income student from Queens College, I understand the struggles many students face, and would like to share what has worked for me and other students I have mentored. This summer, I am joining Google as a technical program manager Intern in the security team.

sessions.title: Inclusive Leadership without a title
sessions.abstract:
Leadership does not begin with a title, a team, or organizational authority. It begins with how we help the people around us contribute, learn, and succeed.

Drawing from experiences leading teams across the United States, Japan, and India, this session explores how individuals at every career stage can practice inclusive leadership. Attendees will learn how to share context instead of hoarding knowledge, create space for questions and different communication styles, support colleagues across time zones and cultures, and turn even overlooked assignments into opportunities to build trust and multiply the capabilities of others.

The session will also examine how AI can reduce language and information barriers through translation, accessible presentations, clearer communication, and personalized learning—while recognizing that technology cannot replace curiosity, cultural understanding, empathy, or accountability.

Through personal stories and practical examples, attendees will leave with behaviors they can apply immediately: approaching their work with ownership, asking the question others may be afraid to ask, bringing colleagues into the learning journey, and leaving every team more capable than they found it. Because inclusive leadership is not about being at the center—it is about making the room larger and bringing others with you.

sessions.title: Building Agentic AI Systems That Don’t Break: From Data Pipelines to Product Decisions
sessions.abstract:
Agentic AI is rapidly moving from experimentation into production, powering workflows, decision engines, and automation. Yet many systems fail not because of weak models, but because teams underestimate the hidden work across product design, data readiness, and system reliability.

In this session, a Product Manager, Data Engineer, and AI Engineer share how agentic systems are built end-to-end — from defining user problems and preparing retrieval-ready data to orchestrating tools, evaluation, guardrails, and monitoring in production. Drawing on real industry lessons, we highlight where agent pipelines most often break and how cross-functional teams can prevent these failures.

Attendees will learn a practical framework for aligning product, data, and AI roles, designing reliable agent workflows, and deploying AI systems that remain trustworthy, measurable, and useful over time.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Beyond the Buzzwords: Early-Career Engineers Building Real Impact with AI
sessions.abstract:
What does it really mean to build with AI as an early-career engineer? In this session, we’ll share our experiences navigating the transforming landscape of Software Engineering (SWE) and Machine Learning Engineering (MLE) across various tech companies, including Google, Microsoft, and Nike.
First, we will compare and contrast our experiences with our roles and companies. We’ll begin by clarifying how these roles differ and where they increasingly overlap as AI evolves. We’ll explore how AI is reshaping day-to-day work, from accelerating development to enabling entirely new capabilities, while also unpacking where it falls short. Between model hallucinations and reliability concerns, and the real costs of deploying AI systems compared to traditional automation, we’ll examine the trade-offs engineers must consider. Finally, we’ll discuss how companies evaluate AI usage and measure impact across a range of business goals.

sessions.title: From One-Pager to Impact: The Follow-the-Flavor Story
sessions.abstract:
Big impact in tech doesn’t always start with a massive roadmap. Sometimes it starts with a clear one-pager and the drive to build. In this panel, an Uber engineering manager and a Gen Z new grad engineer share the story of “GenZ: Follow the Flavor”, an intern idea that sparked cross-team interest, became a working demo at Uber’s AI-a-thon, and won both “Best Product” and “People’s Choice” from the CTO and CPO.
You’ll learn how to pitch early ideas to earn trust, align stakeholders, and build momentum inside a large tech company. We’ll cover practical tactics for crafting a compelling narrative, securing sponsorship, and turning a simple concept into real execution. Hear both the IC perspective that created the idea and the EM perspective that championed it across the org.

sessions.title: Beyond Burnout: Create Sustainable Success Through Resilient Leadership
sessions.abstract: Mid- and senior-career women in tech face increasing complexity, pressure, and invisible load. This interactive session introduces the 3C Resilience Model—Care, Connect, Create—to help leaders prevent burnout, regulate emotions under pressure, and design sustainable success aligned with purpose, influence, and long-term career growth.

sessions.title: Plot Twist: Career Strategy, Confidence & the Power of Networking
sessions.abstract: Early-career professionals are often told to "stay in their lane," yet strategic pivots accelerate growth when done intentionally — and with confidence in what you already bring. This session provides a practical blueprint for bold career moves early in tech while reducing risk. We reframe common fears — feeling too junior, losing credibility, not being ready — because your skills and perspective are more transferable than you think. We introduce the Early Career Pivot Triangle (Skill Depth, Business Impact, Relationship Capital) and a 4-step framework: clarify what energizes you, translate existing skills, prototype before switching, and build relationship capital early. Presenters share real journeys from distinct backgrounds — honest, not aspirational. We also share tactical LinkedIn networking strategies that go beyond the job board, helping you build the right relationships before roles are even posted. Attendees leave with a structured decision model, a downloadable Career Pivot Action Sheet, and the confidence to pursue stretch opportunities on their own terms.

sessions.title: Alignment before Optimization: 7 Skills to Navigate Uncertainty in Today's Evolving Tech Careers
sessions.abstract:
For decades, career advancement in technology was driven by optimization: improving performance, gaining experience, and progressing along predictable paths. As AI and structural shifts reshape technical work, optimization alone is no longer sufficient. Alignment—the ability to detect change early and calibrate your trajectory accordingly—has become a critical career skill.

This talk translates insights from navigating product lead roles at Microsoft, Snap, and Amazon, and a nonlinear career sabbatical, into 7 concrete skills attendees can apply immediately. Attendees will leave with practical tools to navigate uncertainty and build resilient, future-aligned careers.

sessions.title: 10 Strategies for Using AI to Improve Your Thinking
sessions.abstract:
You'll leave with a new way of working — one where AI makes you more you, not less. AI is no longer just a tool — it's a thinking partner. 

Use AI to ask better questions, not just get faster answers ·  Identify blind spots, assumptions, and trade‑offs using AI prompts ·  Apply AI to structured thinking (planning, evaluation, decision reviews) ·  Maintain human accountability, judgment, and agency in AI‑assisted work ·  Evaluate when AI adds value—and when it does not

The real gap isn't access to AI; it's knowing how to think with it. This talk challenges the idea that AI replaces work and reframes it: AI should sharpen your thinking, not outsource it. The focus isn't prompts or tools — it's developing the mindset to lead, decide, and create with AI while holding onto human accountability and agency.

In this session, an AI Product Manager shares what it actually looks like to think with AI in high-stakes, technical environments — not as a shortcut, but as a force multiplier for judgment. Drawing from real experience building and deploying AI systems, this talk offers a practical framework for using AI to surface what you're missing, stress-test what you believe, and move forward with more clarity and confidence.

sessions.title: The Digital Resume 2.0: Building Your Personal Brand with Claude
sessions.abstract: In 2026, a PDF resume gets you through the door, but a live, interactive presence closes the deal. While a static document lists your history, a personal website provides a multidimensional look at your unique problem-solving process and personality. This workshop introduces Vibe Coding: a philosophy where you focus on intent and high-level direction while directing AI agents like Claude to handle the technical syntax. We will bridge the gap between a one-page summary and a powerhouse digital brand. Using Claude as a lead developer, participants will bypass the hurdles of HTML/CSS to "will" responsive UI into existence. Don’t just list your skills—launch them!

sessions.title: Power Up Your Release Day Confidence: A Hands-On Bug Blitz
sessions.abstract: Save the day! Join a hands-on, high-energy "War Room" simulation to master debugging, AI-prompting, and cross-team communication. Gain the superpowers needed to contribute to your next production release with confidence. In this interactive workshop, join a squad to navigate a live, buggy application and practice the vital skill of diving into an unfamiliar codebase. Together, we'll hunt down a range of issues, determine their severity, and fix code-breaking bugs. What you’ll achieve: - The Problem-Solving Toolkit: Build a structured framework to approach tech challenges with precision. - Unlock AI Sidekicks: Learn to prompt AI agents to uncover root causes while validating their suggestions. - Advocate with Intent: You won’t just fix bugs. Practice justifying technical decisions and driving team priorities. Whether you’re squashing your first bug or your thousandth, you’ll leave with new skills, new connections, and a toolkit to rock your next launch day. Ready to join the War Room?

sessions.title: 3×Faster Delivery: A PM–Design–Engineering Operating Model with Visual Development Tools
sessions.abstract: Visual development tools can unlock major speed gains, but without the right operating model they can create inconsistent UX, governance gaps, accessibility regressions, and “shadow changes” outside engineering controls. This presentation shares a leadership-ready approach to achieve 3× delivery velocity for Product–Design–Engineering teams using visual development tools while maintaining quality, security, brand consistency, and operational excellence.
