You’ll learn what work should be design-led vs engineering-led, how to set guardrails (design system constraints, permissions, review/approval flows, content rules), when to use human-in-the-loop oversight, and how to measure impact with a scorecard (cycle time, rework rate, defect escape, accessibility compliance, experiment throughput). We’ll cover a rollout strategy (pilot → scale) for strategic transformation, and leave you with a repeatable framework and checklist to ship faster without losing trust or control.

sessions.title: Beyond Scale: How Data Engineering Shapes Foundation Model Performance at Spotify
sessions.abstract:
Foundation models are only as strong as the datasets they're trained on but scale alone isn't enough. At Spotify, we learned that how you design your data matters as much as how much of it you have. As a technical lead and product manager on Spotify's AI Foundation team, we'll share our journey building the data foundation for LPM, Spotify's large personalization model powering personalization across Spotify's global user base. We'll explore the technical and product decisions behind data representation, signal selection, and dataset composition and what it takes to get those decisions right when a single model serves multiple products simultaneously.

Attendees will learn:

- How data design decisions - representation, sampling, and composition shape what a foundation model can and can't do

- How to build feedback loops between data changes and model outcomes when your evaluation framework is still maturing

- The product and technical trade-offs of owning a shared data foundation that multiple teams depend on in production
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: 600 Billion Requests and Counting: Engineering Feature Flags at Massive Scale
sessions.abstract:
Wayfair’s global commerce platform serves 22M+ active customers and operates at massive scale. At this level, feature flags are not just deployment tools—they sit directly on the critical request path.

This session presents the architecture behind a high-throughput feature flag platform processing 17–18K requests per second at baseline and scaling beyond 100K RPS while maintaining sub-10ms tail latency. In a single year, the system served 6+ billion requests, supporting 400+ projects and thousands of active production flags.

We will walk through the evolution from a monolith-bound solution to a distributed Unleash-based architecture with regional clusters, Edge proxy layers, Redis-backed caching, autoscaling, and service mesh integration. The focus is on managing P99 and P99.9 latency at scale, reducing network hops, and building fail-safe systems that remain resilient under sustained high traffic.

sessions.title: Empathy as a Design Principle: Building Human-Centered Robots
sessions.abstract: In robotics, performance metrics often overshadow the human experience. This session argues that empathy—grounded in usability testing, iterative design, and user trust—should be treated as a core engineering principle. I will share experiences from my journey designing an adaptive audio navigation system for visually impaired users and developing a leg bag disposal (LBD) system at Level The Curve. The presentation emphasizes practical strategies for embedding empathy into the robotics design process without compromising technical rigor.

sessions.title: Silence Isn't Humble. It's Expensive: A Workshop on Negotiating Your Worth
sessions.abstract: Before this workshop ends, you will calculate exactly how much your self-doubt has cost you. Not metaphorically — in dollars. Every time imposter syndrome stopped you from negotiating your salary, asking for a promotion, or advocating for your worth, there was a real number attached to that silence. This workshop connects the dots between self-doubt and lifetime financial outcomes, revealing the compounding cost of undervaluing yourself early in your career. Using live calculations, we'll show how missing one $10K salary negotiation in your twenties can cost you $300,000+ over a career. Through table discussions, pair practice, and real negotiation scripts, you'll leave with your personal negotiation gap calculated, three scripts ready to use in your next financial conversation, and an accountability partner to make sure you actually use them. Imposter syndrome will tell you that you don't deserve more. The market data disagrees.

sessions.title: Leaders Don't Wait for Titles: Building Your Web of Influence
sessions.abstract:
You work hard every single day. You have the ambition, the potential, and the drive to make an impact. But maybe the opportunities pass you by, or you find yourself pushed in a direction that doesn't reflect who you are. You know you’re meant for greater things, yet you don't know where to start or how to get there.

I've been there, and this is how I moved forward.

In this session, I share how I went from a new graduate to a recognized leader at work (and beyond) by serving my community of women in tech. What started as a desire to connect early career professionals with senior leaders who had been through the women in tech journey, quickly grew into something bigger. I built informal authority without a formal leadership title, allowing me to expand my network and influence. Through that journey, I recognized the importance of the 3Cs: Clarity, Communication, and Courage. These are three principles I now apply to every major decision in my life and career.

Explore how to apply the 3Cs to your current role and expand outward to build a network of relationships and experiences that creates opportunities for growth. This session gives you a reframed perspective on what you can do with what you already have and to set yourself up for the opportunities you are looking for.

Growth has never been linear. It's all about branching out, showing up genuinely, and building a web that lets opportunities find you.

sessions.title: Beyond Prompting: Fine-Tune Your Domain-Specific Language Model
sessions.abstract:
Prompt engineering is powerful, but it has limits. As AI systems move into real-world applications, domain adaptation becomes essential. Fine-tuning allows you to adapt a general purpose language model into a specialized model that performs more reliably on tasks in your domain.

In this hands-on workshop, participants will learn how to fine-tune a language model using parameter-efficient techniques (LoRA). We will walk through preparing data, running a lightweight training job, and evaluating measurable performance improvements.

Participants will leave with a working fine-tuning template, practical evaluation skills, and a reusable process they can apply to any domain, whether building AI tools, internal automation systems, or production-grade applications.

sessions.title: They don't teach this in CS: Demystifying the Customer Engineer role
sessions.abstract:
The role of a software professional is evolving beyond implementation. This session pulls back the curtain on the Customer Engineer (CE) and Solutions Architect (SA) path — one of the industry's most strategic and underrated career tracks. As a Customer Engineer at Google Cloud, I  bridge the gap between cutting-edge technology and tangible business outcomes, operating at the speed of innovation. 

If you are looking for a career track that combines deep technical expertise with business strategy and real human impact — look no further. One day I'm working with a healthcare startup, next day a cybersecurity firm- building cross-industry experience few career paths can match. We will explore how this role functions as a technical partnership, requiring a unique blend of architectural depth and consultative skill — and the kind of problems you  get to solve everyday. Whether you are an early-career engineer or an aspiring architect, you'll walk away with a concrete understanding of this path, what makes it different, and what it takes to pursue it.

sessions.title: Your Work Makes Sense. But Does Its Story Translate?
sessions.abstract:
We talk about storytelling as something we do intentionally. But in tech, most stories are told unintentionally. 

Unintentionally through a narrow lens of 'Requirements, Design, Build, Test, Deploy.'

This shows up in how we explain our work, how we introduce ourselves, what we choose to share, and what we leave unsaid. Over time and from listening to hundreds of stories, I closely saw strong technical work lose meaning when it isn’t made legible to others. Back to basics, communication is especially crucial now - With extensive channels of communication made possible into 2026, comes the compromise of diluting context through the very systems that carry it. 

How then, do we envision beyond the industry's default playbook for ways to craft and communicate work?

To redress, I didn't have to look far - In my sophomore year, as I walked into my algorithms class in the morning and Data Sciences class in the afternoon, I caught myself at Philosophy, Physics, and Math lectures in the evening. While some labeled this as 'lacking clarity' in what I want to pursue, I did it anyway. As this developed into way of flipping open my career cards one at a time, I realized something. All these fields of study weren't separate - They were loosely connected through patterns I hadn’t learned to name yet.

In fact, all areas of study described the same concept, just in different languages. That was my 'Aha' moment. 

I knew there was something special to understanding the basics that founded an area of study. Once I understood the underlying patterns in one, I could translate them across others. 

And without trying to, that way of thinking began to show up:

- In how I explained systems. 

- In the way I learned large concepts in emerging Tech. 

- And in the way I applied science to practically executing my vision. 

Ever since, one of my passions outside of the many hats I'm gradually wearing, is one that reframes the art of simple language to explain complex solutions that run the world around us. In very simple language. But one that stands out for uniquely being 'YOUR' perspective. 

 This session will take a fresh attempt at exploring storytelling in Tech - Storytelling not as self-promotion. But rather a form of professional responsibility. As a way to shape trust and credibility through everyday moments and bringing your unique blend of expertise in areas within and outside of tech.  

Because whether you intend to or not, you are shaping how others understand your work and your judgment every day.

Attendees will leave with practical ways to:

1.  Communicate complex work with clarity and precision

2. Navigating multiple careers simultaneously.

3. Strategically position knowledge from different domains into your technical work. 

4. Most importantly, create a presence that reflects the quality of your judgement: Not just the output. 

Because while it's your technical skills that get you in the door, a muscle that pushes you beyond the finish line is the art of intentional, simple, and structured storytelling of your work - Within and outside of Tech

sessions.title: Building Human-Centered AI in Healthcare Customer Service with Abbott Diabetes Care
sessions.abstract:
Artificial Intelligence is transforming industries, but its greatest potential is realized when it empowers people to make a greater impact. In healthcare, that impact can extend far beyond technology, it can help improve the experience of people managing chronic health conditions every day.

In this session, discover how Abbott's Customer Service innovation was able to harness AI-powered agent assistance, intelligent customer intake, speech analytics, and automation to create faster, more personalized, and more meaningful customer interactions. What began as an ambitious digital transformation initiative has grown into a solution supporting thousands of specialized customer service agents while delivering measurable improvements in both operational performance and customer experience.

More than a technology story, this is a story of collaboration, innovation, and purpose. Attendees will gain an inside look at how teams across technology, business, quality, and customer service came together to design, deploy, and scale AI responsibly within a highly regulated healthcare environment. Through real-world lessons and practical insights, the session will explore how to build trust in AI, lead transformational change, measure business value, and balance innovation with compliance and patient-centered outcomes.

Whether you're a software engineer, architect, product leader, data professional, or aspiring technology innovator, you'll leave with a powerful example of how technology can solve meaningful problems at scale while keeping people at the center. Join us to learn how human-centered AI is shaping the future of healthcare, and what it takes to turn bold ideas into solutions that make a lasting difference.

sessions.title: Celebrating Technologists
sessions.abstract: To the innovators, problem-solvers, and future-builders! Join us for a vibrant celebration of our global community of technologists. Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just starting your journey, come mingle with peers, spark fresh collaborations, and celebrate the collective passion that powers the AnitaB.org community every single day.

sessions.title: Engineering the In-Between: Educating Artful Engineers for Complex Futures
sessions.abstract: Today's most pressing challenges (e.g., climate change, public health, social inequity, digital transformation) are not engineering problems alone. They are human problems that require different (i.e., more artful) design approaches. This session brings together a diverse panel of academics and practitioners from engineering, computer science, architecture, and design from across the globe. Each bridges disciplines, sectors, and ways of knowing to enact technological know-how with business acumen and human understanding, ensuring not only better design today but more well-equipped designers for tomorrow. Individually, they will share their unusual yet inspiring career trajectories, while reflecting on lessons learned and brainstorming thoughts on how best to design for complex futures. Together, they will advocate for multi/inter/transdisciplinary praxis, practice, and pedagogy--elevating the art and science behind design, balancing technical rigor with business strategy, and ensuring social valuation and creation. 'Engineering the In-Between' is geared toward learners and leaders across the Triple Helix of academia, industry, and government. The aim? To consider new ways of doing and learning, cultivate future multi/inter/transdisciplinarians who can conduct the creative and incisive work needed in the critical 'in-between,' and aim for transformative flourishing by design.

sessions.title: PETSEC NEXUS: Funding Cybersecurity Innovation from Idea to Global Scale
sessions.abstract: Cybersecurity startups face a dual challenge: proving technical excellence while securing sustainable funding in a competitive global market. PETSEC NEXUS explores how founders, executives, and innovation leaders can successfully move from concept to investment-ready ventures. This session examines real-world funding pathways, investor expectations, and growth strategies specific to security-focused companies operating in emerging and global ecosystems. Attendees will gain executive-level insights into structuring ventures for scalability, communicating value to investors, and building partnerships that unlock capital while maintaining technical credibility and trust.

sessions.title: Become a Stronger Software Engineer Interview Candidate
sessions.abstract: Unlock the secrets to excelling in technical interviews and becoming a standout candidate. This session will guide you through the process of translating your academic experience into interview success. Learn practical strategies to showcase your skills, tackle coding challenges, and confidently pursue offers from your dream companies.

sessions.title: Leading Through Relentless Transformation: Strategy, Sanity, and Selective Control
sessions.abstract:
We keep treating transformation like a phase. It’s not a phase — it’s the environment.

AI acceleration, workforce shifts, and global instability have permanently altered the terrain of technology leadership. Yet many organizations still operate with industrial-era assumptions: maximize utilization, plan extensively, and control tightly. Those systems were built for predictability. We no longer live there.

This session explores how leaders can redesign decision-making, funding, and ownership for constant change. Participants will learn how to anchor in clear strategic outcomes while enabling adaptive execution; make invisible work and bureaucratic friction visible; simplify ownership to accelerate momentum; and fund initiatives like a venture portfolio, not a factory pipeline.

In a world of relentless disruption, leaders must stabilize what matters most — trust, transparency, and direction — and release the illusion of control everywhere else.

sessions.title: Social Leverage - Why Bother?
sessions.abstract: You know the technical stuff — you can build anything with AI and your talents. But now what? How do you move UP and communicate YOUR value?

sessions.title: Next-Gen Leaders: Leadership Shifts for AI-Accelerated Engineering Teams
sessions.abstract:
As AI accelerates code generation, the challenge for engineering teams shifts from slow delivery to erosion of architectural ownership, decision quality, and critical context. When execution becomes abundant, leadership must evolve to effectively lead hybrid teams of humans and AI agents.

My transition from Senior Engineer to Team Lead revealed that leadership habits that once drove success can now create hidden risk in AI-accelerated teams. This session introduces a Leadership Playbook for the Age of AI – a modern framework built around five essential executive leadership shifts, such as moving from scaling execution to scaling judgment, from architectural control to decision guardrails, and from growing coders to growing decision-makers.

Through this talk, we will explore each principle and the mindset shifts behind them. Attendees will leave with a practical playbook that is designed to help them lead with clarity when speed is easy, but good decisions are not.

sessions.title: Leading Through Conflicting Feedback with Emotional Intelligence
sessions.abstract:
Women in tech are often expected to be decisive but not “too much,” confident but not “intimidating,” and visible but not “self‑promotional.” This contradictory feedback, often called double binds, can limit impact, visibility, leadership influence, and career growth.
This interactive workshop helps women leaders and aspiring leaders navigate these double binds using Emotional Intelligence (EI) and the principles of Whole Human Leadership. Participants identify common triggers, examine habits that hold them back, and practice emotionally intelligent responses through guided exercises and role‑play. The session blends evidence‑based EI insights with practical tools for mentorship, sponsorship, and high‑stakes workplace conversations, expanding leadership to address human, social, and systemic complexity.
Attendees leave with ready‑to‑use language, a mentorship conversation framework, and a 30‑day habit experiment they can apply immediately in meetings and feedback discussions.

sessions.title: The Power of Community: Lifting Each Other as We Rise
sessions.abstract:
Members of the Bloomberg Women in Technology (BWIT) community, leaders, allies, and technologists, come together to discuss how mentorship, sponsorship, and visible role modeling within the community provided support, confidence, and opportunity at pivotal moments in their careers. Panelists share personal career stories across four distinct paths: switching into technical roles, building deep technical expertise, stepping into formal leadership, and practicing meaningful allyship.

Attendees will leave with tangible ways to engage, lead, and pay it forward, regardless of role, tenure, or technical background. Designed for aspiring leaders and technologists at every stage, this session is open to all attendees and offers practical insight into how investing in community and building an inclusive culture accelerates individual growth while creating clear, accessible pathways for others, lifting each other as we rise.

sessions.title: Beyond the Hype: Real-World Strategies for Thriving in an AI-First Workplace
sessions.abstract:
Though AI is everywhere, most discussions about it seem abstract and unrelated to the realities of daily work. We keep hearing that AI will “change everything”, but few people explain how this will affect your projects, your skills, or your career path.
With useful tips for succeeding in an AI-first workplace, this session cuts through the hype. You’ll discover how to use AI as a partner rather than a threat by using simple framework of Augmentation, Agency, and Adaptability. We’ll explore how roles are shifting, which skills are becoming more valuable, and how to responsibly and successfully incorporate AI into your workflow.
This talk is for you if you’re prepared to go beyond buzzwords and gain actionable steps you can apply right away.

sessions.title: We are the 300,000+ "Resilience Through Healing and Policy" A Panel on Reinvention and Post-Job Loss
sessions.abstract: The impact of job loss on Black women presents a complex intersection of economic, social, and psychological challenges. As the workforce landscape evolves, many Black women face disproportionate job losses, exacerbating existing inequalities. The unemployment rate for Black women rose significantly from the start of 2025 to December. More than 300,000 Black Women lost their jobs, and that number is growing. This narrative extends beyond mere statistics: it embodies a profound journey of healing, resilience, reinvention, and policy reform. The emotional toll of job loss can lead to issues such as mental health struggles. Yet, amidst these challenges, Black women often emerge as powerful agents of change. This panel discussion hopes to foster a holistic dialogue that acknowledges the challenges and celebrates the resilience and ingenuity that women bring to the workforce. It will illuminate pathways to recovery and power, showcasing approaches to redefine careers in tech and beyond.

sessions.title: Connect Your Dots: Turn Your Experience into the Job You Want
sessions.abstract:
We’ve all heard the anecdote: women often apply to a role only when they meet 100% of a job description, while men will apply at 60% of criteria met. This session isn’t a pep talk to “just apply anyway” or to “shoot your shot”. Instead, this session is about helping you recognize that you are likely far more qualified than you think. You’re often much closer to meeting all that job criteria than you realize.

“Connecting Your Dots” is a strategy I’ve taught through internal talks within Electronic Arts and throughout the gaming industry. The goal is to show how experience that doesn’t match a job description word-for-word is often still highly relevant. Through your resume, cover letter, and interviews, the responsibility falls on you to connect that experience to what’s being sought after. This session equips you with practical skills to do exactly that, because no one else will connect those dots for you.

speakers.name: Julie Banta
speakers.title: Director of Build and Release - Apex Legends

sessions.title: Excellent at Everything… Except Relaxing: A Nervous System Upgrade for Women in Tech
sessions.abstract:
You can debug production issues at 2am, lead teams, mentor junior engineers, and navigate bias. All before lunch! But when it comes to relaxing, your nervous system didn’t get the memo. Every Slack ping feels like a five-alarm fire.

High-performing women in tech are running on adrenaline, cortisol, and sheer force of will. Tight chest, racing thoughts, sleep on backorder, and caffeine acting like critical infrastructure. We’ve normalized white-knuckling our way through the day, hoping ambition will sustain us.

This interactive session is your performance upgrade. Plot twist: calm is not weakness. It’s a competitive advantage. Backed by real science and built for real life, you’ll learn how 10 minutes a day of intentional nervous system regulation can level up your focus, stabilize energy, improve sleep, and strengthen emotional control without slowing you down.

Get a clear, practical understanding of stress physiology in high-demand environments and experience a live reset you can deploy in real time before a presentation, negotiation, or that meeting you’re already dreading.

Advancing women in tech isn’t only about access. It’s about longevity. You don’t need to quit tech or become a monk. You need a nervous system that can support your ambition.

sessions.title: The Science of Visibility: Embodied Personal Power in Technical Leadership
sessions.abstract:
Technical excellence earns a seat at the table. Embodied power determines whether you speak once seated.
Research in embodied cognition and personal sense of power shows that what we wear and how we physically present ourselves influences cognitive performance, decisiveness, and risk tolerance. At the same time, shame research and Daring Leadership work highlight that visibility requires values alignment, boundaries, and grounded confidence.
This session introduces a research-informed framework built on four Image Needs—Alignment, Authority, Safety, and Expression—to help women in tech reduce self-monitoring, strengthen executive presence, and increase leadership visibility without sacrificing authenticity.
Participants will leave with practical tools to use personal image as a behavioral reinforcement system for high-stakes moments: promotions, presentations, negotiations, and C-level transitions.

sessions.title: Who Is Responsible When AI Is Wrong? Break, Test, and Secure a Live AI Agent
sessions.abstract:
We built an AI agent for a bank. In a demo, it's flawless. In the real world, it's a liability, and most teams wouldn't catch why until it's too late. 

AI failures aren't dramatic. They're subtle, confident, and expensive. The model doesn't crash. It fabricates an answer that sounds perfect. It doesn't throw an error. It quietly leaks data to someone who knew the right thing to type. And when it goes wrong, your customers pay the price. 

In this highly interactive workshop, three practitioners work alongside you through live polls, hands-on exercises, and cross-role debriefs to stress-test a live AI agent. You'll evaluate it for hallucinations, red team it with prompt injection attacks to extract sensitive data, identify high-risk automation decisions and harms that ship when nobody's looking. 

Whether you're an engineer, PM, or leader, you'll walk out with frameworks to catch these failures and the confidence to own them. 

No ML experience needed. Just a laptop and curiosity.

sessions.title: Welcome the Elephant: Hacking Tech Culture for Better Results and Happier Humans
sessions.abstract:
The tech industry is in a continuous state of transformation, yet a staggering number of organizational change efforts fail or deliver mediocre results. Why? Because standard playbooks address the "what" and "how" but consistently underestimate the human factor--the "funny things about humans"—our emotional dynamics, cognitive biases, and hidden stories. Drawing from Practice Makes Culture and decades of leading change in technology and business, author Christine Hudson delivers a practical system for creating positive change.

Attendees will learn how to apply the three missing ingredients: welcoming elephants (emotional, systems, and room), creating deep psychological ownership, and facilitating daily practice. We'll unpack "Five Critical Culture Hacks," showing how to use everyday interactions and meetings to smooth silos, avoid "watermelon projects," and build powerful alignment. You'll leave with a playbook to transform your organization's Culture—regardless of title or formal authority—to deliver better business results with happier humans.

sessions.title: One Service, Many Storms: Building Traffic Isolation with Multi-Clustering
sessions.abstract:
At LinkedIn, authentication runs at 1M+ QPS and supports fundamentally different workloads — latency-sensitive user logins, bursty partner traffic, and abuse-prone public endpoints — all within a shared legacy service. When one endpoint spikes, shared compute and thread pools can silently degrade unrelated, revenue-critical flows.
This talk presents a real-world case study of introducing multi-cluster traffic isolation without splitting the codebase or causing downtime. By segmenting workloads and routing them to dedicated clusters running the same binaries, we enabled independent autoscaling, contained blast radius, and eliminated cascading contention.
Attendees will learn:
- How to isolate workloads without decomposing a legacy service
- Designing traffic-aware routing for independent scalability
- Zero-downtime migration strategies at massive scale
- Tradeoffs in cost, capacity planning, and operational complexity
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Agent Up: A Practical Guide to Empowering Work With AI Agents for everyone.
sessions.abstract:
Your job is changing. Not someday. Now.
AI agents are already automating tasks, reshaping workflows, and transforming entire industries. And most people are watching it happen without knowing where to start.
The hardest part isn't the technology. It's the jargon. LLMs, RAG, orchestration, tools... it all feels overwhelming until suddenly, it doesn't.
I know because I built my own agent. And the moment it clicked, I realized this isn't just for engineers. It's for everyone.
In this session we'll demystify AI agents from the ground up, explore how they're transforming every kind of job, and walk through how to start building your own. No engineering background needed. Because the future of work isn't just being built by engineers. It's being built by everyone in this room.

sessions.title: Hire and Develop the Best: How to Communicate Your Impact and Stand Out in Technical Interviews
sessions.abstract:
Let's be honest — most interview advice sounds great until you're actually sitting across from someone and your mind goes blank. This session is for students and early-career folks who want to walk into interviews and sound like themselves, not like they memorized a script.

We'll work through how to actually structure your answers so you stop rambling (we've all been there), how to pick examples that show real impact — even if your experience is "just" a class project or a club you led — and how to talk about numbers and results without feeling like you're making stuff up. We'll also dig into the moments that trip people up most: "Tell me about yourself," explaining gaps, owning mistakes, and figuring out what to ask at the end so you don't default to "What's the team culture like?"

You'll walk out with answer frameworks you can reuse, a bank of practice questions, and a checklist that'll make your next interview feel a lot less scary. The goal isn't to perform — it's to communicate clearly and let the real you come through.

sessions.title: You Got the Return Offer — Now What? Thriving as a Full-Time Employee
sessions.abstract: Landing the return offer is a milestone worth celebrating, but it is just the beginning. The transition from intern to full-time employee comes with a new set of expectations, challenges, and opportunities that no one fully prepares you for. This session is for those who have accepted the offer and are ready to hit the ground running. Speakers will share practical advice on how to navigate the shift from intern to full-time contributor, build credibility quickly, establish meaningful relationships, and set yourself up for long-term success. Whether you start in three months or three weeks, you will leave equipped with the tools and confidence to thrive in your new role from day one.

sessions.title: Apply With Confidence: Building the Online Presence That Gets You Funded
sessions.abstract:
A strong digital presence is no longer just a networking advantage — it's a funding strategy. As the creator economy is projected to reach $480 billion by 2027, the students and early-career professionals who brand themselves intentionally online are the ones winning grants, fellowships, and fully funded opportunities.

In this session, a tech professional shares how she built her online presence from the ground up and used it to unlock competitive academic and industry opportunities. You'll walk away with a clear, actionable approach to crafting a digital identity that funding committees cannot overlook.

speakers.name: Monica Para
speakers.title: Data Analyst & MS Applied Data Science Candidate

sessions.title: AI Without the Tech Bro Narrative: Guardrails, Governance, and Real Outcomes
sessions.abstract:
AI skepticism is rational. Too often, adoption is driven by hype or executive pressure—while the risks land on employees, customers, and marginalized communities. But AI isn’t going away. This talk is a practical playbook for leaders who want to capture real value only when it’s safe, accountable, and worth the tradeoffs.

We’ll cover the technical realities leaders need to understand: data security with AI, what “guardrails” can and can’t do, why “it worked in the demo” isn't a strategy, and how cost and resource use change at scale. Then we’ll shift to actionable patterns: keep humans in the loop where it matters, evaluate reliability with repeatable tests (not vibes), establish governance that doesn’t kill momentum, and recognize when AI is the wrong tool-and how to justify that decision.

You’ll leave with a decision framework, a governance checklist, and evaluation patterns you can apply immediately to adopt AI responsibly without overusing it or being pressured into it.

sessions.title: The AI Career Board: Building a Multi-Agent System to Hack the Job Hunt
sessions.abstract: The modern job search is a grueling battle against automated screening tools. It’s time to level the playing field. In this hands-on workshop, participants will move beyond basic prompt engineering and learn to architect a Multi-Agent AI System designed to automate and optimize their job hunt. Using frameworks like crewAI and cloud-based IDEs, attendees will build a personalized "Career Board"—a collaborative team of AI agents. You will engineer a "Researcher" to analyze job descriptions, a "Strategist" to tailor your resume against ATS keywords, and an "Interviewer" to simulate live, context-aware technical interviews. Aligning with the GHC "Unbound" theme, this session breaks the limits of traditional job hunting, empowering technologists to deploy cutting-edge Agentic AI for their own career advancement. Attendees will leave with a working codebase, actionable AI engineering skills, and a massive competitive advantage.

sessions.title: How AI and you can get through this brutal job market
sessions.abstract: In this session, I will break down how I transformed my internship and job application preparation process using AI, not as a shortcut, but as a strategic tool. From creating tailored study plans and optimizing resumes to practicing technical interviews and building projects, I leveraged AI to reduce friction, increase clarity, and stay consistent. This is not about replacing effort, it is about multiplying it. Attendees will walk away with practical frameworks, real prompts, and observing a repeatable system they can implement immediately while navigating through internships and full-time roles.

sessions.title: Beyond the Resume: Hiring for Agency, Grit, and Execution in the AI Era
sessions.abstract:
AI capabilities are evolving faster than any degree program can track - which means the traditional hiring playbook is obsolete. The question is no longer who knows the right tools, but who has the right internal wiring to thrive when those tools change overnight.

This panel brings together four powerhouse women at the frontier of AI to deconstruct the new blueprint for high-impact hiring. We move beyond static resumes to discuss why "diverse execution" is the new gold standard and how to spot the "founder mindset" in a sea of applicants. We will share proven strategies for identifying Grit, the resilience required to navigate the "Fog of AI" and why personal, hands-on experimentation often outweighs a decade of legacy experience. Whether you are building an AI startup or transforming an enterprise, this session provides the tactical insights needed to hire for agency over pedigree.

speakers.name: Mansi Shah
speakers.title: Director of Strategic Partnerships & Business Development

sessions.title: The Invisible GateKeeper: Engineering Anti-Money Laundering Controls at Global Scale
sessions.abstract:
Every "Buy Now" button hides invisible gatekeepers protecting billions in transactions. What happens when you must screen millions without adding a millisecond to checkout? When government APIs crash and you can't block legitimate shoppers—but also can't let money launderers through? This is compliance engineering at global scale—at the intersection of distributed systems, regulatory requirements and Gen AI.

Through a real-world implementation, you'll discover how to build Anti-Money Laundering systems. Learn architectural patterns that prevent cascading failures, launch strategies that minimize blast radius, and state management that keeps services consistent. Walk away with battle-tested patterns for coordinating workflows, handling failures, and scaling elastically. Whether building Fin Tech, e-commerce, or regulated systems, gain insights into managing complexity while serving business needs. The best compliance systems? Customers never notice them—but they protect everyone.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Endurance, Not Balance: A framework for Sustainable leadership in high-performance careers
sessions.abstract:
Leaders are often encouraged to pursue balance, yet long and meaningful careers rarely unfold in perfect equilibrium. Drawing on lessons from distance running and her experience leading large-scale technology transformation, Sree reframes sustainable leadership as an endurance practice built on intentional pacing, focused priorities, recovery, and interdependence. Rather than giving every demand equal attention or approaching every career season at maximum intensity, participants will learn how to direct their energy toward what matters most while keeping ambition durable over time.

Through the practical 4 P’s of Endurance Leadership: Pace, Priorities, Permission, and People, this session will help participants assess their current career season, recognize where they may be sprinting unnecessarily, and identify the support required to sustain performance.

Attendees will leave with a simple leadership diagnostic, guided reflection questions, and a focused 30-day challenge designed to translate insight into action. The goal is not to lower ambition, but to build a career and leadership approach that can thrive, adapt, and go the distance.

sessions.title: AI Powering Modern Medical Technology: Engineering Systems That Impact Lives
sessions.abstract:
Artificial Intelligence is transforming medical technology, but building AI-enabled systems in healthcare requires more than models — it demands reliability, safety, and thoughtful engineering.

In this session, I will share practical insights from working at the intersection of AI, medical technology, and mobile development. Attendees will learn how AI is applied in real-world healthcare systems, how iOS and Android applications integrate into medical technology platforms, and how AI-driven insights are delivered to users through health monitoring system

I will also showcase a live demonstration of a mobile application to illustrate how AI-driven features are implemented in practice. You’ll leave with clear takeaways on designing intelligent mobile systems and navigating opportunities in MedTech and healthcare AI.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: 2026 Connected Consumer Trends for an AI-Native Future: Living with Super Intelligence
sessions.abstract: We’re no longer entering an AI-first world—we’re living inside an AI-native one. In 2026, intelligence shifts from assistance to execution—reshaping how we lead, build, and operate. This talk is for women at the forefront of that shift: navigating agentic systems, synthetic teams, and a world where AI doesn’t just support decisions—it makes them. In my 7th annual report, AI-Native Future: Living with Super Intelligence, I unveil the Top 10 Trends shaping 2026—from agentic systems and synthetic teams to a world where intelligence is operational infrastructure. This session is a call to lead, not react—to inspire, influence, and inform the future—before it decides for you. To learn more, download the full report here.

sessions.title: Real stories, real skills: How women at Microsoft are growing their careers with AI
sessions.abstract: AI is reshaping how we work—and how we grow. But there’s no one “right” way to figure it out. In this panel, women across career stages at Microsoft share how they’re building AI skills in real time—learning, pivoting, and growing as the technology evolves. You’ll hear how they’re developing AI fluency, combining technical and human skills like creativity and communication, and finding their path in a fast-changing field. Walk away with real stories, practical takeaways, and ideas you can actually use to grow your own career in the AI era.

sessions.title: GHC POWER UP
sessions.abstract:
Morning Movement for Stronger Bodies, Sharper Minds & Better Days 

Before the sessions start, the meetings begin, and the ideas start flowing, take 45 minutes for you. 

GHC Power Up is a new morning movement series designed to help attendees start the day feeling energized, grounded, and ready to take on GHC. Across three mornings, attendees can choose from yoga, HIIT, and full-body fitness experiences led by dynamic wellness instructors Reina Dominguez and Paris Jackson. 

Because showing up as your best self isn't just about what you know. It's also about taking care of the body and mind that make everything else possible. 

Whether you want to stretch, sweat, reset, or simply make space for yourself before a full conference day, Power Up is your invitation to move. 

Wednesday | POWER UP: Cardio Dance with Paris Jackson, Founder of Sweat Sessions 

Kick off GHC with energy. Join Coach P for a high-energy Cardio Dance workout combining upbeat music, rhythmic movement, and muscle-focused exercises for a full-body, feel-good fitness experience. 

Participants will dance, groove, and sweat through movements designed to elevate the heart rate and work the body from head to toe. No dance experience is required, and the class is designed for all fitness levels. 

Thursday | GHC POWER UP: HIIT Reset with Reina Dominguez, Founder of The Inner Edge Training 

Turn up the energy before the conference day begins. This high-energy fitness experience is designed to get your heart pumping, challenge your body, and build strength while allowing participants to work at their own level. 

Reina brings more than 15 years of experience in intentional movement and combines functional fitness, performance coaching, and an inclusive approach designed to leave participants feeling energized, capable, and connected. 

Friday | GHC POWER UP: Flow State with Reina Dominguez, Founder of The Inner Edge Training 

Close out GHC with Flow State, a mindful yoga flow designed to improve mobility, release tension, and reconnect mind and body. 

Through intentional movement and breathwork, participants will build space, restore balance, and leave feeling grounded, energized, and ready for the day ahead.

sessions.title: Closing Plenary
sessions.abstract: Close out Grace Hopper Celebration 2026 with a thought-provoking plenary focused on leadership, accountability, and the future of tech. This inspiring session will feature reflections from Telle Whitney, co-founder of the Grace Hopper Celebration of Women in Computing Conference and former CEO of AnitaB.org, recognition of this year’s ABIE Award recipients, a fireside chat between AnitaB.org CEO Brenda Darden Wilkerson and author, comedian, and cultural commentator Baratunde Thurston, and a keynote from award-winning journalist Kara Swisher. Together, these conversations will challenge attendees to think boldly, lead intentionally, and carry the momentum of GHC forward long after the week concludes.
