sessions.title: Senior Career Reception
sessions.abstract: Lead the way, shape the future, and expand your legacy Join us for an exclusive gathering designed for senior leaders, executives, and seasoned tech professionals looking to cultivate high-level connections, share strategic insights, and explore executive leadership roles within the AnitaB.org community.

sessions.title: Respawn: A Practical Guide to Career Transitions (Layoffs, Pivots, and Level-Ups)
sessions.abstract:
Career transitions are identity shifts. Whether you’re choosing a pivot or you’ve been laid off, the hardest parts are rarely tactical (resume, LinkedIn). They’re emotional processing, clarity about what you actually want, and the ability to explain your story without sounding apologetic or bitter.
In this session, we will cover a repeatable “Respawn” system built from decades of career pivots across functions (customer service, operations, partnerships, product) and from mentoring hundreds of professionals navigating advancement, reinvention, and job loss. Attendees will learn how to stabilize emotionally, define their “why,” translate transferable skills, craft a credible narrative, and execute a simple transition plan with templates they can use immediately.

sessions.title: Ethical AI by Design: Building Fair, Trustworthy AI in the Real World
sessions.abstract:
AI ethics is often discussed at a policy level, but many ethical outcomes are shaped by everyday decisions made across product, engineering & leadership teams. This session explores how responsible AI is built through practical choices made during design, development, and delivery.

Attendees will learn how teams can operationalize responsible AI across the AI lifecycle, from problem framing & data decisions to feature design, prioritization & launch, while navigating real-world tradeoffs between speed, performance, and responsibility.

Designed for product managers, engineers, designers, data scientists, and executives, this session introduces practical tools such as bias reviews, human-in-the-loop systems & transparency techniques that can be applied regardless of role. By the end of the session, attendees will leave with a shared language, concrete frameworks, and actionable practices they can apply immediately to build AI systems that are trustworthy, inclusive, and high-impact.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Saving Lives Through Resilience: How Securing the Cell & Gene Therapy Supply Chain Protects Patients
sessions.abstract: Cell and gene therapy (CGT) is an expensive last-resort solution for treating cancers such as lymphoma or leukemia. That’s one reason why the value chain and intellectual property (IP) used by CGT companies are prime targets for cybercriminals. Any disruption in operational processes could result in financial or property loss, but most importantly: loss of patient life. Join us as we navigate cybersecurity challenges for CGT companies, illustrate the resilience journey, detail problem-solving methods from business and cyber perspectives, and explain how manufacturing cyber resilience applies across industries.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Leading Through the Middle: How Influence, Trust, and Clarity Drive Real Transformation
sessions.abstract:
Large-scale transformation rarely fails because of vision or technology—it fails in the middle, where leaders are translating strategy into execution while navigating ambiguity, competing priorities, and human resistance to change.

This session focuses on what effective leadership looks like when you are not the executive sponsor setting direction, nor the frontline team executing tasks—but the leader holding alignment, momentum, and trust across both. Drawing from real-world transformation environments, this talk reframes leadership as an act of influence, decision clarity, and credibility rather than authority or control.

Attendees will gain practical strategies for leading complex initiatives without burnout, maintaining trust under pressure, and delivering outcomes while staying deeply human. This session is designed for experienced technologists and leaders who are already operating at a high level and want to increase their impact, confidence, and sustainability.

sessions.title: Undiscovered Luck: The Power of Asking a Simple Question
sessions.abstract:
What if your next career opportunity is right next to you, and all you had to do was ask for it? At GHC, we gather because of our shared passion for empowering women in tech, and that makes this the perfect place to discover the luck that comes from meaningful connections.

In this interactive presentation, you'll learn practical networking strategies, and the magic question that got me, a quiet introvert, 100+ coffee chats in 10 weeks and a SWE internship. Through this hour, you'll discover how one coffee chat can transform into unexpected opportunities, mentorships, and friendships.

You'll leave with coffee chat requests already sent, new connections at your table, and the confidence to continue building your network long after GHC ends. Whether you're a networking novice or looking to refine your approach, this workshop will help you unlock the power of authentic professional relationships.

Come ready to connect, learn, and discover the luck that's already around you!

sessions.title: From Intern to Full-Time: The Communication Skills That Turn Analytics Work Into Career Opportunities
sessions.abstract:
Many talented women in analytics and technology deliver exceptional work - yet still struggle to be seen, trusted, and hired. The gap is rarely technical. It's visibility, credibility, and knowing how to communicate impact in a way that builds trust with the people who make hiring decisions.

This highly interactive session draws from real experiences converting analytics internships into production systems and permanent roles. It shares practical, human centered strategies for building credibility, aligning with stakeholders, and confidently communicating impact to managers and non-technical leaders - even when the work is still in progress, imperfect, or recovering from a setback.

Attendees will leave with actionable tools to position their work with clarity and confidence, advocate for themselves without overselling, and build the kind of visibility that turns good work into real career momentum.

sessions.title: Quiet Power, Bold Connections: Authentic Networking in Tech
sessions.abstract:
Networking isn’t about being the loudest voice in the room-it’s about creating meaningful connections that align with who you truly are. For early-career technologists and students, especially introverts or those from underrepresented backgrounds, traditional networking advice can feel performative or uncomfortable.

In this session, we’ll challenge the myth of the “perfect networker” and explore research-backed strategies for building relationships rooted in authenticity, curiosity, and purpose. Attendees will learn how to communicate their stories with confidence, engage in conversations that feel natural, and turn everyday opportunities — from conferences to interviews — into genuine moments of connection.

By the end, participants will leave with a practical framework for navigating professional spaces with authenticity and confidence, proving that you don’t have to change who you are to get where you want to go.

sessions.title: The Show Must Go On: Leadership Lessons from Theatre for Women in Tech
sessions.abstract:
Leadership is often described as strategy and execution — but at its core, it is about people. In high-performing tech environments, effective leadership demands more than expertise - it requires the ability to align teams, foster collaboration, and inspire confidence.

Drawing from her 18 years as a Transformation and Program Leader and a decade on stage as a theatre actor, Parul believes the boardroom can benefit greatly from the study of theatre.

On stage, a successful production depends on shared purpose, creative risk-taking, emotional intelligence, and the discipline to perform when uncertainty strikes.

In this session, she explores how building a successful production mirrors leading high-performing teams. Through storytelling and interactive demonstrations, participants will gain practical techniques to strengthen alignment, foster psychological safety, build trust, and elevate team performance - demonstrating that leadership is not positional, it is lived.

Because in both theatre and technology, the show must go on.

sessions.title: Quiet Power Big Impact: Branding,Career Ownership & Advocacy for Introverts—For Yourself & Your Team
sessions.abstract:
In a tech culture that often rewards the loudest voice, introverts can struggle with visibility, networking, and self advocacy. This discussion reframes those challenges as strengths.

Drawing from real-world leadership experience, this conversation explores how introverts can build an authentic professional brand, own our career path, and grow meaningful networks—without forced self-promotion. We can share practical ways to advocate for ourselves with clarity and confidence, and to let our work speak strategically.

The conversation also highlights a powerful leadership skill: being our team’s biggest cheerleader. From an introvert’s perspective, we and participants can share how to amplify our team’s impact, advocate for ourselves in leadership spaces, and create trust and visibility—while staying true to our style.

This discussion is for technologists who want to lead, influence, and grow—quietly and effectively.

sessions.title: How to successfully incorporate AI, blockchain in Textiles & Handcrafted based Startups to scale
sessions.abstract:
Handcrafted sees meteoric rise and growing at 11 YOY and valued at 2 Trillion by 2034

Elevating Marginalized communities, creating sustainable livelihoods, emancipating rural artisans

Preserving artforms from becoming extinct, upskilling, adhering UNSDG by alleviating poverty and bridging social inequities, recycling, using ecofriendly materials

For many of our artisans, craft is more than just a source of income. It’s a form of expression that’s closely connected to their history and identity. 

These crafts - and the stories that come with them - form the foundation of each handcrafted product. Each one is a celebration of the unique and longstanding tradition of Indian design.

We value our relationships with the artisans that they bring our products to life and are focused on making an increased impact in their life too. The ability to hire women artisan from Rajasthan’s villages and contribute to their economic empowerment is joy.

sessions.title: The Intersection of Leadership, Personal Branding, and AI: Creating Your Unique Narrative
sessions.abstract: In an era reshaped by AI, authentic leadership and a strong personal brand are more critical than ever for women leaders, engineers, and innovators. This session explores how they can craft a unique narrative that fuses personal values, professional strengths, and ethical leadership in an AI-driven world. Through insights from diverse voices across technology, leadership, and communication, the discussion highlights how authenticity, emotional intelligence, and strategic visibility define influence today. Attendees will learn actionable strategies to develop a personal brand that amplifies trust, fosters inclusive leadership, and remains distinctly human amid rapid digital acceleration, while also navigating bias, visibility gaps, and the unique challenges women face as they grow into influential, AI-savvy leaders.

sessions.title: Being Adaptable and Effective in Diverse Multicultural Environments
sessions.abstract: Adaptability and Effectiveness in diverse multicultural environments; Engaging with young college graduates to provide real-world insights and relatable experiences. Providing practical guidance for navigating in today’s professional landscape. While this is not new to any era, I would like to share experiences growing up in these environments. Also provide practical guidance for modern workplace while fostering growth in Diverse Environments. Building relationships and breaking down the cultural barriers to develop better soft skills. Be a self-advocate by showcasing your knowledge, skills and abilities while remaining a team player. Have a mentor and discuss your strengths and weakness to understand your true abilities.

speakers.name: Radha Pilla
speakers.title: Senior Vice President - Senior Technology Manager

sessions.title: How AI Reads Your Resume: A Job Seeker’s Guide to Getting Seen and Hired
sessions.abstract:
AI is now the first reviewer of millions of job applications. Before a recruiter sees your resume, algorithms may already be parsing your experience, inferring your skills and deciding whether you move forward. Understanding how these systems work is now a critical job-search skill for anyone navigating today’s labor market.
In this session, Tina Shah Paikeday explains how AI evaluates resumes and profiles and what candidates must do differently to stand out. She will cover how hiring systems interpret skills and career progression, why keyword matching is giving way to skills intelligence, how online signals affect visibility and where AI can introduce bias or blind spots that may filter candidates out.
Attendees will leave with practical strategies to make resumes and profiles more discoverable, more interpretable by AI and more compelling to human recruiters so they can job search with confidence in an AI-powered hiring landscape.

sessions.title: How to Become Irreplaceable in the AI Era!!
sessions.abstract:
AI is not replacing most professionals. It is replacing low-leverage work.

In a world where AI can generate code, analyze data, draft content, and automate workflows, execution alone is no longer a differentiator. What becomes scarce is ownership, judgment, influence, and the ability to shape how AI is used.

For mid-career technologists, especially women in STEM who are often relied on for high-volume delivery but excluded from strategic decisions, this shift is critical.

This session introduces a practical framework to help attendees move from task execution to problem ownership, from productivity to leverage, and from contributor to orchestrator. Participants will leave with a clear 90-day repositioning strategy to increase visibility, authority, and long-term career resilience in an AI-driven workplace.

sessions.title: Relationship Analytics: Using Data to Engineer the Right Connections
sessions.abstract:
Founders often track product metrics in meticulous detail but leave the relationship building to gut instinct. In this session Christina L. Glancy introduces a framework for applying data-driven decision making to amplify your connections to move your career and project forward. 

Attendees will learn how to:
Use relational mapping to identify high-value vs. low-value connections to support design, sales and relevancy. 
Classify relationships in 4 categories - mentor, sponsor, collaborator, ally to build sustainable systems to support product lifecycle.
Apply data points to product lifecycle, fundraising and partnership conversations to reduce wasted time on misaligned opportunities and return it back to building your product.

Walk away with a practical system to engineer relationships with the same precision you apply to product roadmaps.

sessions.title: Women, Wealth & the Workplace: The Case for Building Teams Where Women Thrive
sessions.abstract:
Women will command $30 trillion in global wealth by 2030. They drive 85% of consumer purchases. Yet they remain significantly underrepresented in technology, and the ratio has been declining for 30 years.

This session combines powerful economic data with a real-world case study: the story of our Amazon Web Services (AWS) EMEA Women's Community built across multiple countries and cultures, and the measurable impact it had on women's career development, retention, and engagement.

From the broken rung, to the motherhood penalty, we'll examine why women drop out of the pipeline and what leaders can actually do about it. You'll leave with clear, actionable steps, whether you're an individual contributor, a team leader, or an executive, to make your team a place where women want to work and thrive.

sessions.title: The Hardest Promotion: What No One Tells You About Becoming a Manager
sessions.abstract:
The move from Individual Contributor(IC) to Manager is often framed as a promotion. In reality, it is an identity shift. This talk explores what happens when high-performing engineers step into management and attempt to operate at 200% capacity- coding while leading. We will share the hidden challenges of learning to trust instead of fix, delegate without disempowering, balance depth with strategic oversight, and carry the weight of words and decisions.

The session reframes what the manager role truly entails: growing people, setting direction, designing systems, and making hard trade-offs. Attendees will leave with clarity on whether management aligns with their strengths and how to approach the transition intentionally.

Because management is not about writing less code. It is about multiplying impact.

sessions.title: Building Engineering Careers in the AI Era: Insights Across Industries, Roles and Levels
sessions.abstract:
AI is reshaping engineering careers at every level—and the uncertainty can feel paralyzing. What skills actually endure? What do leaders value now? Are you moving fast enough?
This presentation answers those questions with data, candor, and cross-generational dialogue. Two co-presenters, an experienced engineer and an early-career technologist, share findings from original interviews with founders, engineers, and executives across industries and across different levels. They surface surprising alignments and honest tensions: which mindsets are evolving, where generations disagree, and how to build a career with confidence when the tools keep changing.
Attendees leave with a practical Career Confidence Framework grounded in real industry voices, and the reminder that the qualities that made them engineers are exactly what the AI era needs most.

sessions.title: Platform Engineering: The Evolution of DevOps at Scale
sessions.abstract: Over the last decade, DevOps has become the backbone of modern software delivery, enabling teams to automate workflows, accelerate deployments, and break down organizational silos. Yet as enterprises scale, many DevOps practices begin to strain under increasing complexity—developers juggle fragmented toolchains, infrastructure responsibilities grow, and operational consistency becomes harder to maintain. Platform Engineering has emerged as a natural evolution of DevOps, offering a structured, product‑centric approach that centralizes common tooling and workflows while empowering developers through self‑service and well‑designed “golden paths.”

sessions.title: The Autonomous Enterprise: How AI Will Redefine Company Operations, Leadership, and Talent
sessions.abstract:
Artificial intelligence is becoming the operating layer of the modern enterprise. Autonomous AI agents are beginning to orchestrate work across finance, product, HR, sales, and operations—reshaping how companies run.

The organizations that win won’t just automate tasks; they’ll redesign their operating models.

This session explores what it takes to build the Autonomous Enterprise. Most companies are layering AI onto legacy systems—fragmented tools, siloed workflows, and reactive reporting—creating more complexity instead of transformation. We’ll examine how progressive leaders are using autonomous agents to reduce coordination friction, improve capital efficiency, and reshape org structure as execution becomes automated.

The future enterprise will be defined by how intelligently it integrates agents into its core operations. The future of company operations is autonomous.

speakers.name: Rachana Kumar
speakers.title: Global CTO | AI, Product & Board Leader

sessions.title: Dear Rejection Email: Thank You, Next — How AI Changed My Job Search Forever
sessions.abstract:
I applied to hundreds of jobs. Showed up to events where I knew no one. Messaged strangers on LinkedIn hoping someone — anyone — would respond. I carried my resume everywhere, walked into offices uninvited, and tracked every application in a spreadsheet that never ended. I wasn't being lazy. I was doing everything right. And none of it was working.

Then one shift changed everything: I stopped being the busiest applicant and started being the most prepared one. AI didn't get me hired — but it turned months of chaos into a system I wish I'd had from day one.

This talk is that story — unfiltered. The desperation, the breakthroughs, and the moments AI almost made things worse. You'll walk away with a playbook you can use tomorrow, built by someone who learned every lesson the hard way.

If you're in the middle of a job search right now — or dreading the one ahead — this session was made for you.

sessions.title: Become Irreplaceable: Turning Your Multi-Dimensional Edge into Career Leverage
sessions.abstract:
In today’s AI driven world, many technologists are asking: if AI can do more of my job, what actually makes me valuable? This panel answers that directly. Your range of experiences is not something to narrow, it is your biggest advantage.

Featuring a data scientist, developer & ex-founder, and an entrepreneur & educator, this session brings together leaders who have navigated nonlinear careers and turned diverse experiences into real impact. Through honest stories from hiring, promotions, pivots, and building a business, panelists will show how their edge helped them see what others could not and turn it into results.

You will leave with an actionable way to identify your EDGE, rethink career growth by expanding who you, and turn your experiences into compelling stories so you can communicate your value with confidence and stand out.

Your edge is not something you need to find, it is something you need to own and your unique combination of experiences is what truly sets you apart.

speakers.name: Namrata Singh
speakers.title: Entrepreneur and Educator
speakers.company: MountRiver Farm LLC, Arlington School District, WA

sessions.title: When Opportunity Means Leaving Home: The Hidden Costs of Tech Careers
sessions.abstract:
Leaving home for opportunity is often framed as a success story, but the hidden costs are rarely discussed. For many women, pursuing a tech career can mean distance from family, evolving identity, financial responsibility, and rebuilding community from scratch.

This panel features Latina leaders across product, engineering, and marketing who each relocated far from distinct hometowns. While united by culture, their upbringings, career paths and toughest challenges differ, creating a layered conversation about ambition, obligation, independence, and belonging.

Attendees will gain actionable strategies for building intentional support systems, evaluating relocation decisions, maintaining long-distance relationships, and defining sustainable success aligned with both growth and core values.

sessions.title: From Coder to Corner Office: Leadership Lessons at Every Level
sessions.abstract: This talk spotlights key lessons from three stages of my technology career — individual contributor, mid-level manager and executive. Early career technical excellence is imperative, but other traits are equally critical to distinguish yourself. As responsibility expands, success becomes greatly dependent on how you engage and motivate others, the systems and culture you build and relationships you cultivate. Understanding the success factors of each stage will enable you to adapt and transition effectively. Finally, across every stage, there are core values that are essential to building lasting impact, including lifting other women along the way. Stories relating to these hard-won lessons will be shared to make them memorable to the audience.

sessions.title: Translating Code Into Capital: An Insider’s Guide to Fundraising for Technical Founders
sessions.abstract:
Great products don’t automatically translate into great pitches. Fundraising rewards clarity of narrative as much as quality of engineering.

In this session, Isha Mehrotra, a former engineer and entrepreneur now turned venture capitalist, shares what actually happens inside early-stage investor conversations. Learn how VCs evaluate technical founders, which signals matter most, and why strong builders often struggle to tell a fundable story.

Attendees will leave with a practical pitch framework, common mistakes to avoid, how to balance technical depth with market narrative, and concrete strategies to communicate vision, opportunity, and momentum.

This session is designed for engineers considering entrepreneurship, first-time technical founders, and builders interested in joining founding teams at early-stage startups.

sessions.title: If AI Can Do Your Job, What’s Left for You? A New Playbook for Early Career Technologists
sessions.abstract: Is AI going to replace me?! The fear makes sense. AI now writes code, builds pipelines, and automates many of the foundational tasks early career technologists were trained and hired to do. But the real shift isn’t that technical work is disappearing — it’s that the definition of valuable technical work is being rewritten. Drawing on experience deploying production AI systems at Walmart, this session reveals what creates impact on modern AI teams. As execution becomes automated, engineering value moves upstream: framing the right problems, integrating complex systems, and exercising judgment when a model is technically correct but contextually wrong. Technologists are now increasingly valued for how well they understand systems, navigate tradeoffs, and take responsibility for outcomes. Attendees will leave with a practical framework for three skills that grow in value as AI scales — and a clearer model for how technical work evolves as intelligence becomes embedded into modern systems.

sessions.title: Architecting Self Healing Cloud Security with Agentic AI
sessions.abstract:
Cloud environments have outpaced human-scale security. With 70% of incidents now traced back to identity-led intrusions and misconfigurations, the old playbook “alert, triage, respond” is broken. The future is autonomous, AI native defense that thinks, adapts, and heals itself.

In this session, we’ll take you beyond the buzzwords and into the architecture. Discover how Large Language Models and autonomous agents are redefining cloud security ,detecting low and slow attacks before they escalate, automating incident forensics, and building infrastructure that remediates itself in real time

You’ll walk away with:

Concrete architectural primitives for AI native cloud security

Hands-on insight into behavioral baselining and automated remediation workflows

An honest look at the hard problems like data sovereignty, AI bias, and keeping agentic systems from becoming a risk themselves

A blueprint for decentralized cloud mesh architectures built for the next generation of threats

Whether you’re architecting security systems, leading cloud strategy, or simply ready to move from reactive firefighting to resilient, self-healing infrastructure, this session will change how you think about defense.

sessions.title: From Runway Model to Machine Learning Model
sessions.abstract:
Non-traditional backgrounds are often seen as a disadvantage when transitioning into machine learning, yet they can become a powerful advantage when positioned effectively. This talk draws on the speaker’s journey from fashion journalism and creative industries to building production machine learning systems, illustrating how unconventional experiences translate into technical strengths.

Key lessons include identifying transferable skills such as pattern recognition and adaptability, bridging the credibility gap, and building a portfolio that signals readiness. Attendees will learn how to craft a compelling career narrative and confidently answer “Why the transition?” By reframing past experiences as strategic assets, professionals can position themselves for success in machine learning and other technical careers.

sessions.title: Fast Starts, Real Impact: Thriving as an Early Career Technologist
sessions.abstract:
Starting in a new technical role can present challenges at any career stage, but the learning curve can be especially steep early in your career. This session features early-career professionals sharing how they have successfully navigated this challenge, from learning unfamiliar codebases to finding their voice among more experienced peers, working directly with clients, and how they successfully steered their first weeks and months into their roles. Through real world experiences, panelists will share insights into how they built credibility with more experienced teammates, communicated effectively with stakeholders, and found meaningful ways to contribute and create impact despite limited professional experience. 

Moderated by Michelle Scheuerman (Vice President), an experienced IT professional, this session will feature interactive discussions with live prompts and reflective questions for attendees to engage directly with presenters. Attendees will gain key insights into how early career technologists can successfully engage with a new team while making meaningful impact through practical strategies for ramping up in a technical role quickly, contributing to project work without the years of experience, and the importance of communication and collaboration as core strengths on any successful team. With emphasis on practical strategies, inclusive dialogue, and audience participation, attendees will gain actionable insights for how they can apply lessons learned immediately in their current positions as they transition into new technical roles. 

As early career professionals continue to grow in their careers across an expansive tech industry, this session features panelists representing different technical roles and backgrounds on a software development team at a leading information technology company. Hanlu Wang (UI/UX Developer) brings a user centered perspective to the panel, sharing how early career technologists can add value by focusing on the end user from day one. She will discuss how focusing on usability, accessibility, and end to end user experience helped her build credibility quickly and collaborate effectively with engineers and stakeholders early in her career. Selina Tette (Business Analyst) will offer the perspective of someone who sits at the intersection of users, stakeholders, and the development team. She’ll share strategies for early career professionals to ask better questions, clarify expectations, and translate ambiguity into actionable next steps—helping teams move forward with alignment and confidence. Zoe King (Full-Stack Software Developer) specializes in Angular and Java, known for delivering user-centered solutions and providing support for both the front end and back end of applications. She’ll share how she pairs strong communication and analytical skills with modern engineering practices and her focus on building, modernizing, and maintaining mission-critical Federal government applications that improve reliability, performance, and customer outcomes.

Each presenter will bring a unique perspective from their roles, creating a dynamic and engaging discussion. 
With a shared passion for technology and its potential for good, this panel will provide an energetic and engaging learning experience that highlights the impact early career professionals are already making in the industry.

sessions.title: Designing Purpose from Day One: Building a Life – Not Just a Career
sessions.abstract:
What if your first job wasn’t just a steppingstone but the foundation for the life you want to build?

Designing Purpose from Day One: Building a Life – Not Just a Career challenges early talent to approach career decisions with intention, clarity, and purpose from the very beginning. This session explores how to evaluate roles beyond compensation, avoid common financial pitfalls like lifestyle inflation, and use income as a tool to support not define success.

Blending practical frameworks for managing money with a broader conversation on meaning and fulfillment, attendees will learn how to align career growth with personal priorities and long-term goals.

Through engaging storytelling and interactive moments, the session guides participants from the excitement of a first job to the real tradeoffs of career progression – ultimately shifting the mindset from “climbing the ladder” to deliberately designing a life. Key takeaway: Your career funds your life but you define what that life looks like.

speakers.name: Mike Wisser
speakers.title: SVP; Remediation Governance Executive
speakers.company: Global Information Security / Bank of America

speakers.name: Daniella Santana
speakers.title: SVP, Business Operations Manager - Global Information Security

sessions.title: Breaking Into Cloud: Cross-Industry Expertise & Alternative Pathways for Women in Tech
sessions.abstract:
Cloud is transforming every industry — and you don't need a traditional CS background to be part of it. This session delivers a dual roadmap: first, a framework for building versatile cloud expertise that translates across sectors, and second, a practical guide to breaking into cloud through alternative pathways.

We introduce the Cross-Industry Cloud Competency Framework — three tiers covering foundational skills, domain-adaptive knowledge (industry-specific compliance and workflows), and strategic expertise. Through real examples spanning healthcare, fintech, and retail, we show how diverse industry backgrounds sharpen — not limit — your cloud career.

Attendees will explore entry points including Industry certifications, bootcamps, self-study platforms, and hands-on labs. We address imposter syndrome head-on, reframing non-traditional backgrounds as competitive strengths. Attendees leave with a concrete action plan to position themselves as multi-domain cloud experts.

sessions.title: AI & Human-Centred Productivity: Benefits, Challenges, and the Future
sessions.abstract:
As AI becomes embedded in everyday workplace tools, productivity is often framed narrowly around speed, output, and efficiency. This session introduces human-centered productivity, an approach that examines how AI can support meaningful work while preserving trust, autonomy, and well-being. Drawing on research in human–AI interaction and real-world workplace examples, the session explores when AI genuinely reduces drudgery and enhances performance—and when it creates friction, resistance, or unintended consequences.
Attendees will learn how design and deployment choices shape AI adoption, how to evaluate productivity beyond traditional metrics, and how to ask better questions when introducing or using AI at work. The session offers practical frameworks and perspectives for technologists, researchers, and leaders seeking to ensure AI systems enhance human capability rather than undermine it.

sessions.title: From skincare startups to AI Product Management: rebranding yourself to break into tech
sessions.abstract:
This session will highlight my journey pivoting from skincare startups and nonprofit leadership to AI product management. I will share how I intentionally rebranded my resume, LinkedIn presence, and narrative to land multiple tech internships, from LinkedIn to Hewlett Packard, and ultimately, my full-time role AI product Management role at IBM. 

Attendees will learn how to translate non-technical experience into tech-relevant positioning to tell a cohesive story and stand out in a hiring market dominated by automated screeners and referral-driven pipelines. This talk is designed for students and early-career professionals navigating career transitions seeking a practical playbook for rebranding themselves to break into their dream tech roles.

speakers.name: Trisha Beher
speakers.title: Product Manager - App Modernization and AI Operations

sessions.title: Accelerating Tech Mastery Through AWS Experience-Based Learning
sessions.abstract: Discover how AWS Experience-Based Acceleration (EBA) revolutionizes professional development by combining immersive hands-on learning with leadership capability building. This session explores EBA's proven methodology that accelerates technical mastery through real-world problem-solving, cross-functional collaboration, and outcome-focused learning. Attendees will learn how EBA's learn-by-doing approach transforms traditional training paradigms, enabling professionals to gain deep technical proficiency while developing strategic thinking and change management skills. We'll examine case studies showing how EBA shortens project timelines, enhances team engagement, and builds future-ready technical leaders who can navigate complex digital transformations with confidence and expertise.

sessions.title: Finding Your Voice as an Immigrant - A Venezuelan's Journey
sessions.abstract:
What does it take to find—and trust—your voice while navigating new cultures, languages, and expectations? In this session, I share my journey as a Venezuelan immigrant building a career in tech and the often-unspoken challenges that come with it.

From the quiet weight of loneliness to the pressure to assimilate, this talk explores the emotional and professional realities immigrants face when entering influential rooms where decisions are made. I reflect on moments of silence, moments of courage, and the intentional work of reclaiming confidence and presence without losing authenticity.

Attendees will gain practical strategies for empowering themselves as immigrants—recognizing isolation before it becomes invisible, reframing accents as markers of resilience, and showing up boldly in spaces not originally designed with them in mind—along with a call to action for leaders and allies to create psychological safety and ensure immigrant voices are truly heard.

sessions.title: Beyond the Code – Navigating Your Future Role in Tech
sessions.abstract: This exciting panel is a premier opportunity to illuminate the vibrant tech ecosystem for students and early-career professionals. While many initially view "Tech" through the lens of "Software Engineering," this session celebrates the industry’s success as a thriving, symbiotic community of diverse disciplines. Attendees will gain an inspiring and clear understanding of the fulfilling day-to-day realities, innovative mindsets, and collaborative boundaries that define the essential SWE (Software Engineer), PGM (Program Manager), SRE (Site Reliability Engineer), and PM (Product Management) roles.

sessions.title: Stop Doing Everything Start Growing Something
sessions.abstract:
Early-career technologists face many projects, tools, and certifications, making it hard to know what is worth their time. This session provides a practical framework to filter opportunities, focus on deep technical skills, and prioritize work that advances careers. Using first-principles thinking and examples from our early cybersecurity careers, we show how to cut wasted effort and build skills and reputation over time.

What Attendees Will Do / Gain
Practice evaluating opportunities and prioritizing actions.
Apply a Signal vs Noise framework to make smarter career decisions.
Explore real-world tradeoffs and technical examples from cybersecurity projects and certifications.
Learn to spend time effectively and grow skills and reputation strategically.

sessions.title: Found in Translation: The Hidden Superpower of the Non-Linear Career
sessions.abstract:
Years ago, I mentored a group of high school seniors from an under-resourced school in North Philadelphia. A decade later, I ran into one of them. She built a life at the same university where I earned my own degree. I hadn't taught her anything special. I could just reach her faster, because I recognized what she was living. I'd lived it too.

That recognition has a name: translation. It's the skill built by every part of a career that doesn't look like a straight line - parenting, a career change, an unrelated degree, a hard chapter nobody puts on a resume. Most of us learn to hide or apologize for those chapters. This session makes the case that they're where your real professional advantage was built the whole time.

Drawing on over a decade in enterprise Customer Success, this session shows how to name a skill you already have, find exactly where it shows up at work, and use it with customers or coworkers, in a performance review, an interview, or a case for your next role.

Attendees leave with three practical exercises: the Translation Audit, the Cross-Functional Mapping Exercise, and the Superpower Lens.

If your path hasn't been a straight line, this session is for you

sessions.title: Where Bias Hides: How Our Values Quietly Shape Algorithms
sessions.abstract: We often think of AI as objective—just math and data, free from human bias. But the truth is more complex: every algorithm reflects the values, assumptions, and blind spots of those who create it. From the datasets we choose to the metrics we optimize, from the problems we prioritize to the edge cases we ignore, human judgment shapes AI at every turn. In this talk, I'll reveal how our values quietly infiltrate algorithms—sometimes with serious consequences for fairness, inclusion, and trust. Through real-world examples spanning facial recognition, hiring systems, healthcare, and beyond, we'll explore why seemingly "neutral" AI can perpetuate inequality, and what it takes to build systems that truly serve everyone. This isn't just about fixing bugs; it's about examining our own assumptions and committing ourselves to ethical, inclusive design from the ground up.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Designing Real-Time Data Platforms: Bridging Streaming and Analytics
sessions.abstract:
Modern systems generate continuous streams of events but transforming those streams into reliable, analytics-ready data products remains a major engineering challenge.

This session explores architectural patterns for converting real-time event streams into governed, queryable data lake tables that power analytics, operational reporting, billing, compliance and machine learning workloads. We’ll examine schema evolution, data contracts, quality enforcement and the trade-offs between batch, streaming and hybrid architectures.

Through real-world production lessons, attendees will gain practical strategies for building scalable, resilient data platforms that unify operational and analytical systems and learn how to design streaming pipelines as long-lived data products rather than temporary integrations.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: 10x Product Teams in the AI Era: Flatter, Faster and More Fluid
sessions.abstract:
Software product teams are undergoing a fundamental transformation. AI-powered tools are compressing delivery timelines, reducing the headcount needed to ship at scale, and raising the bar for what it means to be a high-performing engineer or product manager. This isn't a distant future - it is happening now, and many teams are racing to catch up.

This talk offers a candid, practical look at where product teams are headed. We'll examine what the new "lean, AI-leveraged team" actually looks like, what skills will separate those who thrive from those who struggle, and how the very definition of a successful product delivery is evolving from shipping features to delivering measurable outcomes.
Whether you lead a team, are part of one, or are building your career with an eye on where the industry is going, this session will give you a clear-eyed view through real world examples of what is coming and a concrete framework for adapting.

sessions.title: Building Your Future: International Students & Professionals Navigating Tech Careers & Visa Pathways
sessions.abstract:
International students & professionals face unique challenges building tech careers while navigating complex visa requirements, creating compelling portfolios, and understanding their professional options. 

This presentation features professionals who successfully transitioned from international student status to thriving tech careers, sharing practical guidance on the intersection of career development and immigration.

sessions.title: Campus to Cloud: How We Cracked the Interview in Big Tech and What Came After
sessions.abstract: Breaking into Big Tech is hard. Staying and growing is a different challenge entirely and nobody hands you a map. This session is designed for students and early-career professionals who want both: a real shot at landing the role and a plan for what comes next. We'll share the strategies that worked building the skills and projects that get you noticed, networking that opens real doors, and crafting resumes that show impact rather than just activity. Then we'll take you inside two very different growth paths at AWS: one built on lateral moves across roles; one built on going deeper within one. Both are valid. Both taught us things no job description could have prepared us for. You'll leave with concrete strategies you can act on immediately, from building your presence before you apply, to navigating growth once you're in, and the confidence that preparation, not perfection, is what gets you in the room and keeps you there.

sessions.title: "Are You Really Listening? A Leadership Skill That Separates High-Performing Teams from Others"
sessions.abstract:
Most leaders think they're good listeners. They're not. And it's costing them in missed innovation, preventable turnover, and teams that never reach potential. Research shows 85% of what we hear is filtered through biases and assumptions. Result? Team members stop sharing ideas. Problems fester. Top talent leaves.
Most leaders think they're good listeners. They're not. And it's costing them in missed innovation, preventable turnover, and teams that never reach potential. Research shows 85% of what we hear is filtered through biases and assumptions. Result? Team members stop sharing ideas. Problems fester. Top talent leaves.
The difference between mediocre and exceptional teams isn't talent or resources—it's whether the leader has mastered listening to understand, not just listening to respond. This interactive session breaks down why we listen poorly, the hidden cognitive filters that distort communication, and the proven framework that transforms how teams collaborate and perform.

sessions.title: Healthcare AI Is a Systems Problem. Let's Talk About the System
sessions.abstract:
Getting into healthcare data science is more difficult than most industries and this is not because tech skills are different, but because the domain is unlike anything else. And nobody really teaches you that part. That’s what this talk is for.
The U.S. spends $4.5 trillion a year on healthcare, and yet doctors spend more time charting than caring for patients. Hospitals lose millions of dollars due to preventable readmissions and coding errors, most of which are hidden in claims data. The data is already there. What’s needed is context like where it comes from, why it looks like it does, and how to model it so it actually works in the real world.
We will take a patient journey from the point of hospitalization to data, billing, and finally to a modeling task. We will then discuss where AI adds value and how to build responsibly when real patients are involved. 
This talk is for data scientists and analysts interested in healthcare but feel like they are missing the bigger picture.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Introduction to Venture Capital: How Funding Decisions Get Made
sessions.abstract: This session introduces how venture capital works, how firms evaluate startups, and how founders and aspiring investors can better prepare for the funding process. Drawing from my experience as a Venture Fellow at Alumni Ventures and my completion of Berkeley’s Venture Capital Executive Education course, I will walk through how funds are structured, how investment decisions are made, and what makes a company fundable. We will examine evaluation criteria, common misconceptions, and practical steps founders and operators can take to position themselves for capital. Attendees will leave with an understanding of how venture capital functions and how to navigate it more strategically.

sessions.title: Decentralized Funding for Women in Tech: Access Web3 Grants Without Being a Crypto Expert
sessions.abstract:
Billions in non-dilutive funding flow through Web3 grant ecosystems every year, yet most women in tech have never heard of Gitcoin, quadratic funding, or on-chain crowdfunding. This session breaks down the barrier between "crypto feels inaccessible" and "I just secured $50K for my project."
Drawing from a grants consulting practice that has secured $150K+ for 15 clients and raised $90K+ through quadratic crowdfunding campaigns, this talk delivers a clear, repeatable framework for identifying, applying to, and winning Web3 grants, no blockchain background required.
Attendees will leave with a working map of the Web3 funding landscape, practical criteria for evaluating grant fit, and an AI-assisted workflow for building their own opportunity pipeline. Whether you're building a startup, an open-source tool, or a community initiative, this session gives you a concrete path to funding that exists outside traditional VC and institutional gatekeepers.

sessions.title: The Next Chapter of Networking: Making and Keeping Connections Through Shared Interests
sessions.abstract: Traditional networking has often prioritized the elevator pitch over creating connections. While happy hours and career fairs foster professional bonds for some, many - particularly introverts and marginalized groups - are often left to navigate the landscape of transactional interactions. This presentation explores the more inclusive, community driven approach to professional growth: the power of shared interests. By examining the success of organic initiatives like the Women in Tech Book Club, we demonstrate how focusing on genuine personal connections through non-work topics builds a foundation of professional trust. We will share practical strategies for turning any event into a connection point, shifting the focus from primarily professional accomplishments to shared interests. Ultimately, we show that a supportive community is the single most powerful professional asset an individual can possess.

sessions.title: An Imposter in My Own Life? Radical Acceptance and the Courage to Advance
sessions.abstract:
In the 1890s, women were warned that riding bicycles would cause “bike face” — a strained expression brought on by overexertion. The real concern wasn’t facial distortion. It was women moving freely.
Today, many mid-career technical women hesitate to advance, not because they lack expertise, but because they feel like imposters in their own lives.
This session reframes imposter syndrome as a systems signal rather than a personal flaw and offers a tactical framework for advancing before confidence fully catches up. Attendees will learn practical strategies to test new levels of leadership, translate technical depth into executive impact, and build influence without waiting to feel perfectly ready.

sessions.title: Behind the Wheel of Zootopia 2's Vehicles - Walt Disney Animation Studios
sessions.abstract:
The urban metropolis of Zootopia is filled with high-speed police car chases, flaming "hogrods," multi-tier bunny tour buses, and cars of all shapes and sizes zooming down its streets. Throughout this presentation, we will explore the challenges of bringing vehicles to life during the production of “Zootopia 2” through the lens of a software engineer and a technical director. 

Some challenges included adopting Pixar's "driving system" within Presto and building new show-specific tools for animation workflows. This exploration of “Zootopia 2” vehicles will highlight how technical directors and engineers collaborate closely with artists during the production process, provide insight into how technology is used to enable a film's story and creative vision, and bring a fun inside look into the making of Disney animated movies.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Unbounding Your Data: Finding the Graph Hidden in Your SQL Tables
sessions.abstract:
Your SQL database is hiding a secret: it's already a graph!

Every foreign key is an edge. Every row is a node. The relationships you need for powerful predictions are already there in your normalized tables. But when we build ML models, we flatten everything into spreadsheets, hand-craft features for weeks, and lose what makes the data valuable. 

Relational Deep Learning (RDL) unbounds your data. By treating primary and foreign keys as graph edges, RDL applies Graph Neural Networks directly to your existing database schema. No migration to graph DBs. No complex ETL pipelines. Just change how your model sees your tables. 

In this session, we discover the graph hidden in your tables. Watch live comparisons showing how RDL captures multi-hop relationships traditional ML misses, eliminates manual feature engineering, and learns end-to-end across tables, all through enterprise usecases. 

Walk away with the RelBench toolkit, implementation roadmap, and a new way to see your data!
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Driving Scalable Design Innovation Through Advanced Frontend Architecture
sessions.abstract:
As products scale, frontend systems often begin to fracture-not because of bad developers, but because of growing complexity, inconsistent architectural decisions, and shortcuts made under pressure. The result is familiar: fragile codebases, slow feature delivery, and systems that become harder to reason about over time.

In this session, I’ll explore how to design frontend architectures that remain scalable and maintainable as systems evolve. We’ll break down practical approaches to modular design, reusable component structures, state management strategies, and performance optimization patterns that help teams build with long-term clarity instead of short-term speed.

These ideas are drawn from real-world experiences building and scaling frontend systems across teams and products, and from a broader framework I’ve been documenting as part of my ongoing work in this space.

We’ll also look at how AI tools like Gemini can act as an architectural thinking partner, helping engineers reason about design trade-offs, improve code quality, and maintain consistency across large codebases. Attendees will walk away with practical, battle-tested strategies for building frontend systems that scale across users, teams, and products without collapsing under their own complexity.

sessions.title: The Tech Behind the Taste – the Platform that Powers McDonald’s
sessions.abstract:
At enterprise scale, innovation is only as strong as the foundation beneath it. This session explores how McDonald’s drives large‑scale infrastructure and platform transformations to enable future innovation while navigating aggressive timelines and global complexity. Attendees will learn why investing in foundational platforms matters, how upfront strategy and planning accelerate execution, and what it takes to scale technology when the runway is short and the stakes are high.
The discussion highlights how data and meaningful metrics guide decision‑making, measure success, and reduce risk throughout transformation efforts. Through real‑world lessons, we’ll explore how teams fail fast, learn faster, leverage stakeholder feedback, and course‑correct across scaled deployments. Finally, the session connects high‑impact transformation work to career growth, showing how leading complex, visible initiatives builds skills, credibility, and readiness for future leadership.

speakers.name: Dani Salonen
speakers.title: Senior Manager, US Technology, EDGE Deployments

sessions.title: No Internship Experience? No Problem: Building a Resume That Gets Interviews
sessions.abstract:
No internships? No FAANG logo? No “real” experience?

At conferences like Grace Hopper, it’s easy for students to feel behind before recruiting even begins. But here’s the truth: most students already have more signal than they think.

This session reframes what “experience” actually means in technical recruiting and shows attendees how to transform coursework, hackathons, clubs, and personal projects into compelling, interview-generating resumes. Instead of waiting for permission in the form of an internship, students will learn how to position what they’ve already built as proof of impact, ownership, and technical depth.

Attendees will leave with a tactical resume upgrade plan - and the confidence to walk into career fair conversations knowing they belong.

sessions.title: Your Story is Someone's Starting Point: Sharing Your Journey to Open Doors in Tech
sessions.abstract: Tech doesn't require one "right" path, and the proof lives in the stories we share. This panel brings together women who transitioned into tech from non-traditional backgrounds: special education, electrical and computer engineering, and cognitive science. We'll explore how sharing your journey publicly can inspire diverse individuals to pursue technology careers. We'll discuss how non-traditional backgrounds create unexpected advantages, why failure and redirection are more valuable than polished success stories, and how mentorship shaped our paths. Panelists will share early career challenges, how they navigated barriers unique to career changers, and the skills from their previous fields that became strengths. Attendees will leave with strategies for storytelling for career advocacy. Whether you're pivoting into tech, early in your career, or looking to inspire others, this conversation will show you why your unique background isn't a limitation, but instead your greatest asset.

sessions.title: Engineering the Physical Backbone of AI-Era Networking Infrastructure
sessions.abstract: Artificial intelligence workloads are driving unprecedented demands on networking hardware, pushing traditional air-cooled architectures toward their limits. This technical session explores how AI-era networking infrastructure evolves from air cooling to hybrid and fully liquid-cooled systems to support increasing power density and rack-level performance. Through a real-world case study, attendees will learn how mechanical, thermal, electrical, and systems engineering fundamentals- heat transfer, fluid mechanics, structural design, and reliability engineering are applied to build scalable AI infrastructure. Designed especially for entry-level engineers and recent graduates in mechanical, thermal, aerospace, electrical, and hardware disciplines, this session connects classroom principles to the physical backbone powering today’s AI technologies.

sessions.title: AI as the business model - Rethinking product strategy
sessions.abstract:
Most product teams treat AI as a feature to optimize. But when your ranking, relevance or retrieval algorithm decides which sellers get visibility across millions of transactions, or your recommendation engine shapes purchasing behavior at scale, you're not just improving metrics - you're designing an economic system.

I learned this at eBay. We shipped a ranking model that increased revenue in testing. A few weeks later, seller behavior had shifted in ways we didn't anticipate, small merchants were losing ground, and our support channels were flooded. The model wasn't supporting our business - it had become the business model.

Over six years building AI-powered search, advertising, and recommendations systems at eBay, Oracle, and Amadeus, I've seen this pattern repeat: small algorithmic changes don't just optimize - they redistribute value, reshape incentives, and fundamentally alter how money flows through an ecosystem.

In this session, you'll walk away with:

1) The Feature-to-Foundation Framework: A diagnostic tool to identify when your AI system has crossed from optimization feature to core business model - with warning signs to watch for

2) Incentive Mapping for AI Products: How to trace your model's economic impact beyond metrics - mapping value redistribution, behavioral shifts, and second-order effects before you launch

3) Real Failure Modes & Fixes: Specific examples from production systems where optimization improved but outcomes broke - and the strategic guardrails we built to prevent it

4) Strategy for AI-Native Products: Practical approaches to treating models as economic engines requiring business model thinking, not just feature roadmaps

Whether you're launching your first ML model or scaling AI products to millions of users, this session will give you a new lens for product strategy - one that acknowledges AI doesn't just power your business model, it often becomes it.

sessions.title: Beyond the Task List: Pacing Your Impact in the Mid-Career Unknown
sessions.abstract:
Like many in their 20s, I took up marathon running, and discovered a truth I now apply to my career at Workday: software engineering is not a sprint; it is an endurance race that requires strategic pacing. For those moving past the entry-level phase, succeeding as a mid-level and moving towards the path to seniority can often feel like an uncharted "mid-career unknown."

This session explores the mindset shift required to move from execution to design—moving from "doing" to "deciding." Drawing on my transition from product teams to building Document Driven Accounting AI frameworks for Workday Financials, we will discuss how to gain momentum through ownership and cross-team visibility. We will cover how to evolve from a task executor to an innovator who spikes solutions and manages complex dependencies across teams. We will learn how to start thinking like a seasoned engineer and architect a sustainable "pacing" plan to pave our way towards a senior level engineering role.

sessions.title: Before You Get Hired: What Most New Grads Don’t Know About Landing Their First Tech Job
sessions.abstract:
Many new graduates are told that landing a tech job is a numbers game. Apply more. Learn more. Work harder. Yet hiring decisions are rarely made on effort alone. They are made on clarity, credibility, and perceived risk.

This session exposes the invisible mechanics of early-career hiring. You will learn how recruiters actually evaluate candidates, why scattered applications dilute signal, and how perceived readiness is constructed long before an interview begins. Instead of reacting to rejections, attendees will build a pre-application career strategy: aligned role targeting, compelling impact stories, focused proof of work, intentional referral pathways, and much more.

This is not resume advice. It is hiring strategy. Participants leave with a structured framework to transform preparation into positioning and shift from reactive applying to deliberate, high-signal positioning.

sessions.title: Mid-Career Reception
sessions.abstract: Pivot, power up, and own your next professional chapter Join us for a dynamic session tailored for mid-career technologists ready to break through boundaries, scale their impact, and step into intentional leadership.

sessions.title: 30 Minutes. One Prompt. A Decision-Ready BRD: How Product Managers Use GenAI to Ship Faster
sessions.abstract:
A strong PRD often takes 8+ hours to write, yet many still fail to drive clear decisions. Senior product managers know the challenge isn’t effort — it’s turning complex thinking into concise, decision-ready documentation. The ability to write fast and think rigorously is a career differentiator.

This session introduces a disciplined framework to turn a blank page into an executive-ready BRD or PRD in under 30 minutes. I’ll show how experienced PMs use GenAI with engineering depth: defining constraints, measurable success criteria, and trade-offs — not generating filler. The result is up to 70% faster documentation with stronger alignment and decision confidence.

Attendees leave with a production-grade template and repeatable workflow that accelerates influence, clarity, and senior-level growth.

sessions.title: Product, Program, or Obsolete? Navigating Tech Job Market in the Age of AI
sessions.abstract: AI is quietly rewriting the rules of product and program management—not by eliminating roles overnight, but by changing which kinds of leaders matter. Many experienced PMs and TPMs feel the ground shifting: execution is accelerating, decision-making is being automated, and long-held career assumptions no longer hold. This session explores what is actually happening to product and program leadership roles inside AI-enabled organizations and how women can reposition themselves from delivery-focused roles to decision-making and systems leadership. Drawing from real-world experience leading Technical Product Management organizations across Fortune 100 companies, Mariya Breyter shares what survives, what fades, and what grows when AI enters the room, and how to navigate the modern job market with clarity and intent. This is not a future prediction—it is a pragmatic, step-by-step guide grounded in how organizations are already operating at scale.

sessions.title: AI, Access, and the Economy: Designing the Future of Work for Inclusive Growth
sessions.abstract: As artificial intelligence reshapes industries and labor markets, leaders must ensure AI-driven growth expands opportunity rather than concentrates it. This session explores how accessibility-first AI strategies unlock new markets, accelerate product adoption, and fuel job creation by expanding workforce participation among historically excluded talent. By embedding accessibility into AI from design through deployment, organizations stimulate innovation, reduce economic risk, and strengthen long-term competitiveness. Attendees will gain practical frameworks for aligning AI advancement with measurable economic impact, inclusive hiring, and sustainable growth in the digital economy.

sessions.title: Translating Between Domains: Leadership Lessons from Software & Steel
sessions.abstract:
In high-stakes industrial environments, software engineers don’t just write code—they act as the vital bridge between legacy physical processes and modern digital innovation. Translating between these domains requires more than just technical skill; it demands a leadership mindset and a framework for building trust across knowledge silos.

Drawing on lessons learned from developing Level 2 automation software for steel manufacturing—bridging the gap between complex metallurgical processes (casting, rolling, and SEM) and cutting-edge software solutions—this session explores how to lead and influence when you aren't the subject matter expert. You will leave with "industrial-strength" communication strategies to prevent costly misalignments and foster innovation, regardless of your industry.

While grounded in the rugged world of industrial systems, these principles apply to any engineer looking to collaborate more effectively in today’s cross-functional tech landscape.

sessions.title: From new hire to next level: A five-year journey of growth at AWS
sessions.abstract: Career growth isn't linear, and it's rarely easy, but it is learnable. In five years at AWS, we earned two promotions and successfully transitioned roles, but not without missteps, and self-doubt. This session pulls back the curtain on what actually drives career advancement: identifying your unique strengths, mastering self-advocacy, cultivating sponsors, and strategically aligning your work with high-impact business priorities. We will share our individual stories of the process, mindset shifts that transformed how we approached visibility, the uncomfortable conversations that unlocked promotions, and the support systems that kept us from burning out. This isn't a highlight reel but an honest roadmap through setbacks and breakthroughs. Attendees will leave with practical, immediately applicable tactics to set clearer career goals, navigate promotion cycles with confidence, build strategic relationships, and create sustainable momentum toward their next level.

sessions.title: Breaking the “Too Late” Myth: A Mid-Career Pivot from People to Product
sessions.abstract:
What happens when you’ve built a decade-long career, earned credibility, and then choose to pivot?

In this session, I’ll share my journey from HR leader to Principal Product Manager at Amazon — not as a reinvention, but as a deliberate shift grounded in transferable skills, intentional branding, and confronting the mental barriers that often hold us back mid-career.

Through candid lessons and practical strategies and honest reflections, I’ll focus on (1) How to influence hiring teams when your résumé doesn’t “match,” (2) Reposition your experience to build credibility in a new role, and (3) Overcome self-restricting beliefs that limit bold moves.

Whether you’re exploring product management or a career change at mid / senior levels, you’ll leave with clear frameworks and the confidence to pivot with purpose — without losing the value of everything you’ve built.

sessions.title: What Fills Your Cup?  How to evaluate job opportunities to decide if they are right for you.
sessions.abstract:
Choosing the “right” tech job is harder than ever. Compensation, title, company brand, growth, work-life balance, mission, every opportunity promises something different, and many engineers struggle to know what they truly want. 

In this talk, a Senior Director of Engineering at The Farmer’s Dog and personal job coach will share a practical, values-driven framework for evaluating offers. Drawing on experience from startups to Big Tech, she’ll help attendees identify what truly “fills their cup” and assess if a role delivers on those needs. 

Attendees will learn to clarify values, ask the right interview questions, spot misalignment early, and gain confidence in choosing roles that fit for the long term, not just on paper.

sessions.title: When AI Writes Better SQL Than You: Redefining the Analyst Role
sessions.abstract:
For years, my value came from being better than the tools. I could write cleaner SQL, debug faster, and fix queries myself instead of waiting on automation.

Then GenAI changed.

Last year, I watched it go from “almost right” to writing flawless queries — and even reasoning beyond my instincts, like structuring a difference-in-differences analysis and normalizing customer cohorts without being prompted. That was the moment I realized the highest-leverage skill was no longer writing the query. It was designing the system that teaches AI to do it better.

In this talk, I share how I shifted from SQL-first executor to hypothesis-driven enabler, how we’re piloting multiple AI approaches responsibly, and how analytics teams can evolve from answering questions to accelerating strategy.

sessions.title: Take Charge: Say What Matters, When It Matters Most
sessions.abstract: In today’s fast-moving environments, it's not enough to do great work—you must communicate with clarity, confidence, and intention. Whether in the boardroom delivering high-impact updates or in a 1:1 on career progression, how you navigate an organization can define what comes next. Blending interactive, scenario-based decision-making with candid storytelling, this session will equip participants with real-world insights to navigate situations that don’t come with a script. It’s not about talking more—it’s about saying and doing what matters, when it matters most.

speakers.name: Angela Williams

sessions.title: Modern Banking Fraud Detection: From Simple Rules to AI
sessions.abstract:
Every day, millions of financial transactions take place, and behind the scenes, banks work to detect and prevent fraud in near real time. But what do these systems actually look like in practice?

In my role as a Data Science Professional at HSBC, working with financial crime compliance use cases, I have seen how fraud detection works beyond theory. This session explores how modern banking systems have evolved from simple rule based checks to ML/AI approaches.

Using practical examples, we will look at how signals like transaction velocity, location, and behavior are used to flag suspicious activity. We will also discuss trade offs, including balancing false positives with actual fraud risk, and why perfect detection is not realistic.

This session is designed for students and early career professionals who want a clear and practical understanding of real world fraud detection systems.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Code to Capital: The V.A.L.U.E Framework to Architect Buy-in
sessions.abstract:
Technical excellence is a prerequisite for an architect, but securing funding transforms vision into reality. For many women and non-binary technologists, the "broken rung" appears at the Senior Engineering level, where the challenge shifts from solving bugs to generating ROI.

Join four technical architects to deconstruct the V.A.L.U.E. Framework, a strategic blueprint bridging the gap between "cool engineering" and "viable business design." This session moves beyond the pitch, teaching you to apply architectural patterns to technical proposals through five pillars: Vision(V), Analysis(A), Layout(L), Units(U), Evidence(E).

Whether advocating for Platform Engineering or Agentic AI, you will learn to speak the language of stakeholders without losing your technical soul. This is your roadmap to gaining the visibility, budget, and authority to lead mission-critical innovations. Stop waiting for a "green light", learn how to engineer a VALUE-based approach.

speakers.name: Subha Narasimhan

sessions.title: AI, But Make It Production: The Continued Importance of Solutions Architecture
sessions.abstract:
AI is often discussed through the lens of models, breakthroughs, and research innovation. But none of that matters if the system fails in production.

This session looks behind the curtain of how AI actually works at scale — not from the researcher’s perspective, but from the viewpoint of the people responsible for making AI systems reliable, performant, and usable in the real world.

Because AI doesn’t magically go from notebook to product. Someone has to design the infrastructure, manage the GPUs, navigate tradeoffs, and translate research ambition into production reality.

That role is increasingly the Solutions Architect.

We’ll explore the AI infrastructure pipeline, why GPUs sit at the center of modern AI systems, and why Solutions Architecture has become more critical than ever. Or, more simply:

AI, but make it work.
AI, but make it scale.
AI, but make it production.

sessions.title: From Regs to Riches: How I Built a Career at the Crossroads of AI, Tech & Trust
sessions.abstract:
What if the next big opportunity in tech isn’t just about building the future—but protecting it?
In a world racing to harness AI, the demand for leaders who can navigate the gray space between innovation and regulation is exploding. Join Nicole Barbour, Sr Director of Health & Life Sciences Trust & Compliance at Microsoft, as she shares her journey from auditor to tech leader in AI governance, healthcare privacy, and regulatory strategy.
Part career roadmap, part call to action, this session explores how a passion for compliance became a purpose-driven career influencing how AI is built, deployed, and trusted. You’ll hear behind-the-scenes stories of navigating high-stakes compliance, building influence without a blueprint, and shaping policy in one of tech’s fastest-moving spaces.
Whether you're curious about Responsible AI or exploring your next move, this session will show how to turn your values into your superpower.

speakers.name: Nicole Barbour

sessions.title: Competitive Programming: Turning Algorithms into Opportunity
sessions.abstract:
Many aspiring developers question the practical impact of competitive programming on their professional trajectories. Join us as we demystify the path from programming competitions to a career in Big Tech companies like Uber. 

We will break down the anatomy of programming contests, exploring the types of problems used in contests like the ACM's International Collegiate Programming Contest, covering data structures and algorithms, and drawing connections between these challenges and the technical questions asked by companies. The session also covers how to participate in programming competitions, where to find contests and how to practice effectively using platforms like LeetCode, and HackerRank.

Finally, we’ll feature a live demo where we walk through a solution example, detailing the specific strategy used to deconstruct and solve a complex problem.

sessions.title: Leading with Purpose and Care to Develop Emotionally Intelligent, High-Impact Leaders
sessions.abstract: This session will explore how leaders create meaningful impact by grounding their leadership in self-awareness, emotional intelligence, and a commitment to balanced, people-centered decision making. It highlights how a strong leadership brand, intentional mentorship, and sustained leadership wellness shape a leader's ability to empower others to cultivate high-performing, psychologically safe environments.

sessions.title: Transportation Technology: Work that Saves Lives aka Careers You Never Thought of But Should Have
sessions.abstract: Nearly 5,000 people are killed and 100,000 injured in large truck crashes every year. This panel session will consist of experts in the field of commercial motor vehicle, transportation, and highway safety technology that is being used to prevent crashes and save lives on the Nation's highways. Panel experts will discuss how technology is being used to predict and prevent crashes, predict human behavior and to eliminate the risk of human error in driving large trucks. They will talk about the interesting and diverse jobs that exist in the commercial and public transportation sector that are meaningful and save lives. We will discuss autonomous trucking, advanced driver assistance systems, crash notification, and crash and traffic analysis and the kinds of jobs in this sector that are available and going to expand in the future.
