sessions.title: From Packets to Partners: Architecting a Strategic Career Pivot
sessions.abstract: The transition from a technical individual contributor to a strategic business leader is often described as a leap.  It should not be, it should be an architecture. Drawing on 15+ years of experience—building cloud infra at Cisco and Microsoft, leading Business Development through Strategic Partnerships at NVIDIA, building an ecosystem of AI ISV Partners at Tata Communications & completing an MBA at Wharton—this session provides a blueprint for technical professionals looking to pivot into business roles while staying technical.

sessions.title: Queens of The Castle: Women Executives Powering the Magic of Disney
sessions.abstract: Every Disney story features a heroine who faces obstacles, evolves, and ultimately shapes her own destiny. In this executive panel, senior women executives across product, engineering, and design share the real-world versions of those journeys. From pivotal career inflection points to navigating high-stakes executive rooms, this conversation explores the challenges, tradeoffs, and resilience required to lead at the highest levels while opening pathways for the next generation of women in technology.

sessions.title: The Strategic leader: 7 Habits for Scaling Your Impact
sessions.abstract: What separates a good engineer from a highly effective technical leader? It’s not just writing better code, it’s about strategy, mindset, and resilience. In this session, we will explore 7 on the ground tested habits that drive long-term success in tech. From leveraging AI and mastering the Art of saying No, to strategically selecting the right teams and building financial freedom, you will walk away with an actionable blueprint to amplify your impact and accelerate your career.

sessions.title: From Alerts to Insights: Keeping Critical Platforms Reliable Without Burning Out Engineers
sessions.abstract:
Today’s complex distributed systems rely on alert-heavy observability, which overwhelms engineers, causing burnout and slow incident response. As platforms scale, more alerts increase cognitive load and burnout without improving reliability.

This session presents a framework to build enterprise-scale observability, moving from reactive monitoring to a proactive human-centered approach.The talk emphasizes how to move from a tool-centric approach to using meaningful SLOs and standardized dashboards.

Attendees will learn key strategies for designing a reliable platforms with shared visibility across services, moving to SLO-driven practices, reducing alert fatigue, and managing observability costs without sacrificing visibility. This talk demonstrates that true reliability at scale is achieved by empowering leadership and engineers with the right insights at the right time, ensuring critical platforms remain stable.

sessions.title: Same room, different playbook: AI and the modern tech interview
sessions.abstract:
AI has changed the tech interview on both sides. Candidates use it to prepare, practice, and refine their thinking. Interviewers use it to screen, structure, and evaluate. Both sides are using AI but neither has a playbook. This session provides practical frameworks for both, reframing the technical interview as what it's always been at its best: a conversation about fit, potential, and alignment.

Candidates will learn how to use AI ethically to structure responses and demonstrate real judgment, not just surface polish. You'll walk away with prep materials including a prompt bank for AI-assisted interviews, plus perspective on how interviewers use AI so you can walk in informed.

Interviewers will leave with a rubric for evaluating candidates fairly when AI is part of the process.

Whether you're preparing for your next technical interview or conducting one, you'll leave with actionable tools to raise the quality of the conversation.

sessions.title: Control the Inputs, Redefine the Outcome.
sessions.abstract: In early-career tech journeys, outcomes often feel out of our control: internship offers, interview timelines, recruiter responses, and decisions that seem to define what comes next. When those outcomes don’t go as planned, it’s easy to feel stuck, behind, or uncertain about how to move forward. This session introduces a practical shift that helps separate outcomes from inputs. Rather than focusing on results that can’t be controlled, this talk outlines a structured way to focus on what can be. Attendees will learn how to identify controllable inputs, adjust their approach, and continue building momentum even during periods of uncertainty. Through a clear and repeatable framework, this session will help attendees strengthen how they prepare, how they present their experiences, and how they move forward without letting a single decision define their path.

sessions.title: You Don’t Have to Pick Just One: Navigating a Cross-Functional Career in Tech
sessions.abstract: As a user experience designer who has worked across product ownership, software engineering, and risk-focused business analysis, I’ve lived a career that doesn’t fit neatly into a single job category. This talk explores how cross-functional careers in tech are a strength, not a liability; they are intentionally shaped by curiosity, systems thinking, and real organizational needs. Drawing from first-hand experience moving between technical, analytical, and human-centered roles, I’ll share how to build credibility across functions, translate skills without “starting over,” and create a career narrative that makes breadth feel strategic rather than scattered. Attendees will learn practical frameworks for identifying their career anchor, maneuvering pivots with confidence, and thriving in roles that reflect how modern tech teams actually operate. The session is for anyone who’s been told to “pick a lane” and suspects their best work lives at the intersections.

sessions.title: From Reactive to Predictive: AI in Modern Program Management
sessions.abstract:
Teams lose hours every week stitching together status reports from Jira, Asana, and Slack - and even then, projects look green right up until they suddenly slip. This is the "watermelon" trap:healthy on the outside, red in the middle.

We'll show how AI closes both gaps. First, Automated Reporting: using Model Context Protocol (MCP), Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and AI-assisted "vibe coding," we turn a 4–6 hour monthly reporting grind into one-click Monthly Business Reviews and org-wide weekly flashes. Then, Predictive Reporting: reading signals in PR activity, ticket age, and team context-switching to detect stalls early, and turning them into clear, actionable interventions rather than more noise. We'll also challenge the single-date estimate, using probability-based forecasting to give stakeholders a more honest and defensible view of when things will ship.

You'll leave with a practical framework, live demos, and an ethical, human-in-the-loop model for moving your team from reactive to predictive.

sessions.title: Get Interview-Ready in 34 Days: Hands-On Steps & Exercises
sessions.abstract: Struggling to land your next tech role? This interactive session gives early-career professionals a practical, step-by-step 34-day roadmap to prepare for technical and behavioral interviews. We’ll break down each week with hands-on exercises, real-world examples, and actionable strategies you can implement immediately. You’ll learn how to refine your resume, craft compelling stories for behavioral questions, practice coding challenges efficiently, and build confidence for virtual and in-person interviews. By the end of the session, attendees will have a clear, structured plan to transform their interview readiness, making the path to offers faster, less stressful, and more predictable. Walk away with tools and techniques you can use immediately to secure your next tech opportunity.

sessions.title: Kill the Script: Why Human-Centered Tech Needs Human-Centered Experiences
sessions.abstract:
Technology is built for people, yet the teams building it often strip the humanity out of how they engage customers. We obsess over product features and sprint velocity while ignoring the one thing customers actually remember: how we made them feel. This session challenges tech’s addiction to scripted, metric-driven customer interactions and presents a practical framework for embedding authentic human connection into every touchpoint, from onboarding to support escalations to renewals.
Drawing on about a decade in this space and scaling CX teams across global locations. I’ll share how to replaced robotic processes with adaptive, trust-building engagement at scale, achieving retention without sacrificing consistency. You’ll walk away with a repeatable framework for balancing personalization with scalability, tools to build emotional intelligence into cross-functional teams, and a mindset shift that redefines CX as everyone’s job, not just one department’s problem.

sessions.title: From Data to Decisions: How Women at Airbnb Are Building the Future of Tech
sessions.abstract:
What happens when trustworthy data, actionable metrics & marketplace intelligence come together? Innovation that transforms how millions travel & belong anywhere! Join us for a panel featuring four exceptional women from Airbnb's data & engineering teams, moderated by Kim Easley, Principal Recruiter.

Our panelists:
- Tanushree Mehra, Analytics Engineer, Trust – Building data pipelines & metrics for trust
- Jasmine Omeke, Software Engineer, Event Logging – Building scalable logging foundations
- Elizabeth Ponce, Software Engineer, Dev AI – Revolutionizing developer experience
- Yvonne Wang, Data Scientist, Marketplace Intelligence – Matching guests with perfect listings

They'll share journeys breaking barriers in tech & advice for women in data and engineering careers. Whether exploring your first role or leveling up, you'll leave inspired & equipped to make your mark.
Come for the insights. Stay for the belonging.

sessions.title: From Solo Coder to Multi-Repo Engineer: Designing Systems That Scale Across Teams
sessions.abstract:
In school and interviews, we write code in isolation. We can refactor freely, rename fields, and rewrite modules without worrying about downstream impact. In production, it’s different. Your application is already running, already integrated with multiple APIs and services, and already depended upon by teams you may not even know.

A small change can ripple across repositories, dashboards, and systems.

This talk explores the shift from solo coder to multi-team engineer where success isn’t just about making something work, but about evolving systems safely. We’ll discuss practical strategies rarely taught in classrooms: backward-compatible API design, safe schema evolution, incremental migrations, and thinking in contracts rather than just implementation.

Because real system design isn’t just about building new systems, it’s about changing live ones without breaking trust.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Lead with Heart: Motivate, Delegate, Elevate
sessions.abstract:
A women leader’s secret weapon is the ability to lead with her heart. While many may see leading with heart as a weakness, it is actually our superpower.  

Women in leadership often navigate a tightrope of contradictions - be strong, but not too strong. Be empathetic, but not a pushover. Be hands-on but never micromanaging. The result? Many women leaders find themselves overextended, under-supported, and questioning whether they belong in the room at all. 

In this session, Sandy Kingdon and Pavithra Kannan draw from their experiences as people leaders in tech to explore three pillars of heart-centered leadership:  

Motivate - Building trust and psychological safety through empathetic leadership.  

Delegate - Empowering others by letting go of control and scaling your impact.  

Elevate - Fostering inclusion and championing growth to lift entire teams.  

Along the way, they address the common struggles women face as leaders from workplace bias to navigating visibility and advocacy. Walk away with practical strategies to lead with both heart and impact.

sessions.title: From Interview Prep to Impact: Landing Your First Tech Job and Thriving in It
sessions.abstract:
Breaking into tech is challenging — but succeeding after landing the job can be even more overwhelming. In this session, I’ll share practical, real-world strategies from my journey to securing my first software engineering role and navigating the critical first year as an SDE 1.

We’ll cover effective interview preparation techniques, resume positioning strategies, and structured approaches to technical study. Then we’ll shift to thriving on the job — using GENAI, handling code reviews, accelerating learning in large codebases, and transitioning from “new hire” to impact-driven engineer.

Attendees will leave with actionable frameworks to both land their first role and build momentum once they’re in it.

sessions.title: Confident Money Moves: A Financial Playbook for Women in Tech
sessions.abstract:
Your compensation package is more complex than most people will ever deal with — RSUs, stock options, corporate benefits, and a career that can pivot overnight. Yet most financial advice wasn't built with you in mind.

Certified Financial Planner (CFP) Joy Dow has spent her career helping women in tech turn financial complexity into financial confidence. In this no-nonsense session, you'll walk away with a personalized roadmap to optimize your equity compensation, build a tax-efficient investment strategy, and plan for the goals that matter most to you — whether that's buying a home, building long-term wealth, or retiring on your own terms.

Leave with clarity, a concrete action plan, and the confidence to make your next money move count.

sessions.title: Your Personal Board of Advisors: A Data Science Approach to Career Growth
sessions.abstract: In a world where AI and digital platforms shape how we learn and work, the next frontier of career growth is building a data‑driven personal board of advisors. Just as organizations depend on strategic boards, high performers can advance faster by combining human mentorship with AI‑powered insight. This session shows how to turn personal data—skills signals, productivity patterns, learning history, work outcomes, and feedback—into intelligence that guides career decisions. You’ll learn how to choose the right mentors, sponsors, and peer advisors; enhance them with AI tools; and analyze inputs to reveal strengths, blind spots, and growth opportunities. By blending data principles with human relationships, you become the strategic CEO of your career, supported by an advisory ecosystem that evolves with you. Participants leave with frameworks, templates, and AI‑enabled techniques to design and refine their personal board for clarity and impact.

speakers.name: Nirmala Anne
speakers.title: Vice President, Data Architect, Authorized Data Source Strategy Lead

sessions.title: Administrating Innovation: Creating the culture to make innovation a habit!
sessions.abstract:
Myth: Only a technical genius can generate patentable technology ideas.

Truth: Innovation isn’t about technical mastery—it’s about curiosity, courage, and consistency.

In this session, Anna Berry challenges the conventional narrative around innovation and patents by sharing her personal journey as a non-technologist embedded in the technology space. With 11 granted patents and two additional applications pending, Anna proves that breakthrough ideas don’t require a technical title—just a willingness to ask questions, speak up, and make innovation a habit.

Her journey began just six years ago with a single idea. In 2022, that idea became a granted patent—and within days, she led “Team 8” to win Bank of America’s Global Information Security Patent Collab. What started as a randomly assembled team has since evolved into a sustained innovation engine: together, they’ve generated 22 patent submissions, with 8 granted and others still progressing through the pipeline.

This session goes beyond inspiration. Anna will share practical strategies for building a team culture that consistently generates high-quality, patentable ideas—focusing on how to foster psychological safety, encourage bold thinking, and turn innovation into a repeatable practice. Attendees will walk away with actionable approaches to unlock creativity within themselves and their teams—no technical background required.

speakers.name: Anna Berry
speakers.title: SVP, Info Security Controls Sr Specialist

sessions.title: Beyond the Ladder: The Myths That Keep You on the Ladder (and How to Leap Anyway)
sessions.abstract: Most career pivots are driven by desperation — a bad manager, a stalled role, a layoff. This session is about something rarer and more powerful: moving from strength. Sakshi Patil — System Design Engineer at Apple, Carrier Cert TPM at Google Pixel, and now TPM Lead in Consumer Payments at Google Ads and Commerce — has never pivoted out of fear. Every move was made from a position of success, driven by evolving goals and deliberate upskilling. Through the Strength Pivot framework, Sakshi shows that bold career moves are not reserved for exceptional women — they are available to any woman willing to be intentional. You will leave with a concrete map for your next move, made on your own terms.

sessions.title: Shape the System: A Framework for Women Navigating the AI Era
sessions.abstract: Women face three times the automation exposure that men do in the AI era, yet hold only 26% of AI roles. The gap is not a pipeline problem. It is a positioning problem. This session delivers a three-move framework — Outcome Ownership, System Proximity, and Narrative Control — with exact scripts for the hard conversations: asking for sponsorship, negotiating scope, and declining task work that does not build toward your number. You will leave with a self-diagnostic you can use Monday morning and a specific play to claim space in AI governance, the fastest-growing career whitespace in enterprise technology.

speakers.name: Pati Prince-Taggart
speakers.title: General Counsel and Head of Talent

sessions.title: Redefining the Room: Women Leading Differently in Tech
sessions.abstract: Do you identify as an introvert? Have you wondered whether leadership is the right next step for you—if your natural style fits what leadership is “supposed” to look like? Many women in tech identify as introverts. We’re often drawn to technical work because it rewards deep thinking, problem‑solving, and creating solutions—sometimes quietly, from behind a laptop. Yet many of us also feel the pull toward leadership, while questioning whether that path is compatible with who we are. This panel brings together three women leaders—a CEO, a Vice President, and a Senior Project Manager—who have navigated that journey in their own way. They’ll share stories, lessons learned, and practical strategies for growing into leadership while remaining authentic. This panel will challenge assumptions about what leadership looks like, offer honest insight into what introverted women face as they take on bigger roles, and leave you with practical guidance—and confidence—as you consider your next step.

sessions.title: Why High-Performing Women Don’t Get Promoted and How to Position Yourself for the Next Level
sessions.abstract:
Many of the most capable, hardworking women in tech do everything right, they deliver results, take ownership, and consistently exceed expectations, yet still find themselves overlooked for promotions.
This talk challenges the deeply ingrained belief that excellence alone leads to advancement.
Drawing from real-world leadership experience and patterns observed across high-performing technical teams, this session explores the hidden dynamics behind promotion decisions, what actually happens in rooms you’re not in, long before roles are posted or decisions are announced.

sessions.title: Ask for It All: Overcoming the Fear of Expressing Your Needs at Work
sessions.abstract: Why do so many women feel compelled to downplay their needs to preserve others’ comfort? In this session, high-stakes communications expert Katie Lawson breaks down the cultural, historical, and deeply personal factors that keep women from asking for what they deserve. Through candid insights and practical strategies, participants will confront their fear of asking, learn to navigate anxiety and shame, and master the art of the “Empowered Ask.” By reframing needs as non-negotiable and reclaiming your value, you will leave with the clarity, confidence, and tools to unlock enduring self-belief and take bold steps toward the careers you desire.

sessions.title: The Future-Proof Professional: Built Different in the Age of AI
sessions.abstract:
“The Future-Proof Professional: Built Different in the Age of AI” is a career-defining session for emerging talent preparing to launch and grow in the age of AI. As technology reshapes industries in real time, early-career professionals are uniquely positioned to step into opportunity, not just react to change.

Through real-world stories and practical frameworks, this session equips attendees to translate their skills into business value, stand out in competitive job searches, and navigate internships and early transitions with confidence. Participants will learn how to become intentional connectors between technology and people, ambition and execution, and potential and impact, leaving with clear, actionable strategies they can apply immediately.

speakers.name: Zoe Johnson
speakers.title: Lead AI Solution Architect, GenAI Governance

sessions.title: You're probably already a Product Manager
sessions.abstract:
You don’t need a PM internship, or even a traditional “product”, to think like a product manager.

In this session, Sandra Radić (PM @ Mundo AI, founder of youCode, previously @ Microsoft AI) shares how product thinking shows up everywhere: from launching a 200+ person hackathon to working as a restaurant server. Through practical frameworks, real-world examples, and a live AI-powered prototyping demo, attendees will learn how to reframe their experiences, articulate transferable skills, and build confidence without waiting for permission.

Participants will leave with a repeatable product-thinking framework, tools to combat imposter syndrome, and concrete strategies to position themselves for product and leadership roles, regardless of their background.

sessions.title: High-Impact Engineers in the AI Era: Building Influence, Moving Fast, and Leading with Intelligence
sessions.abstract:
AI can now generate code, draft documentation, propose architectures, and spin up prototypes in minutes.
So what differentiates engineers when execution is no longer the bottleneck?
In the AI era, impact is no longer defined by how fast you code — but by how clearly you think, how well you decide, and how effectively you influence.
The engineers who stand out today are not competing with AI. They are directing it. They are building meaningful products — not just shipping features. They understand users, align technical decisions with business goals, and bring the right stakeholders into the room before problems scale. They ask better questions. They surface ambiguity early. They create clarity where speed could otherwise create chaos.
This session reframes what it means to be a high-impact engineer in an AI-accelerated world — and provides a practical roadmap for building influence, velocity, and leadership without losing technical depth.

sessions.title: Monolith is Not a Dirty Word Anymore
sessions.abstract:
Microservices became the gold standard, and the industry followed. But what promised agility often delivered complexity, operational overhead, and systems harder to reason about than the monoliths they replaced.
At PayPal, every architectural decision carries real consequence for reliability, velocity, and cost. That experience makes one thing clear: the right architecture isn't the trendiest one. It's the one that fits your team, your problem, and your moment.
This session challenges the assumption that microservices are always the answer. We'll explore why companies are reversing course, examine the Modular Monolith as a middle ground with clean boundaries and less complexity, and build a framework for deciding what's right for your team & not the team that wrote the blog post.
Attendees will leave with the tools to evaluate tradeoffs, push back on hype, and advocate for pragmatic decisions even when conventional wisdom points the other way
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Smart Work Wins: Cut Friction, Align Priorities, and Launch Work That Lands
sessions.abstract:
Teams today aren’t struggling because of lack of effort—they’re struggling because of friction. Competing priorities, unclear ownership, constant rework, and manual coordination slow progress and disconnect work from business outcomes.

This session shares practical methods to remove execution friction and help teams focus their energy where it matters most. Drawing from real experience leading large, multi-team platforms, you’ll learn how to align priorities to outcomes, improve delivery predictability, and create clarity without adding heavy process.

We’ll also explore how AI can reduce manual work, improve visibility, and support faster decision-making through simple, low-barrier use cases. Participants will leave with lightweight frameworks, diagnostic tools, and a 30-day action plan they can apply immediately to increase team velocity, confidence, and impact—whether they’re early in their career or leading at scale.

sessions.title: Play or Perish: Why a Playful Mindset Is a Survival Skill in Times of Change
sessions.abstract:
AI is rewriting roles. Reorgs are constant. The old playbooks no longer apply.

For mid-career technologists, this moment is especially destabilizing: you’ve built expertise and credibility, but suddenly the rules are changing. In volatile times, many default to certainty, control, and risk-avoidance. But what if that instinct is exactly what holds us back?

This moderated panel brings together leaders from product, design, and workplace experience. Through guided prompts and audience engagement, the moderator will surface productive tensions: What does strategic play look like when stakes are high? Can experimentation coexist with accountability? Does experience make play easier or harder?

Panelists will share stories of career growth and reinvention, ultimately demonstrating how playful mindsets enable better decision-making under uncertainty, help teams recover from failure faster, and unlock innovation. Learn how leaders use play to navigate ambiguity and build resilient careers.

speakers.name: Natashia Tjandra
speakers.title: Director of AI Product Design & Research

sessions.title: Before You Say Yes to Management: The Trade-Offs No One Talks About
sessions.abstract:
You're a strong individual contributor. Management feels like the logical next step. But should you take the job? And in the era of AI, does the role even matter the way it used to?

Becoming a people manager is not just a promotion. It's a career shift. Your success is no longer measured by your own output, but by your team's performance, engagement, and growth. You're no longer just impacting the product, but the livelihoods of the people you lead.

In this candid session, Leslie Chen, seasoned people manager and Chief of Staff turned executive coach, returns to the GHC stage to unpack the real trade-offs of moving into management. You'll walk away with an eyes-wide-open view of what you're actually signing up for and the three things every new manager wishes they'd known going in.

If you're considering management or newly promoted, this session will help you decide intentionally and lead effectively in a world where human leadership matters more than ever.

sessions.title: Harness AI for leadership influence in octopus organisations
sessions.abstract:
To harness AI for leadership influence in an "Octopus Organisation," you must shift from a traditional hierarchical "machine" model to a distributed intelligence framework.Leaders should act as the "central brain" that sets strategic intent, while empowering the "arms" (frontline teams) to make autonomous, AI-augmented decisions. 

Core Principles for Leadership

Distributed Decision-Making: Push 2/3 of decision-making power to the frontline,to act without awaiting top-down approvals.

Connected Context: Replace organizational silos with an AI-driven "nervous system" that allows information to flow laterally. Leaders influence by ensuring every "arm" has the context it needs to remain aligned with the whole, even when acting independently.

Leadership Rhythms: Balance three distinct leadership modes to maintain momentum:
Analytic Heart, Agile Heart, Aligned Heart

Middle Management Transformation: Translate high-level DNA (strategy) into practical local actions and coaching teams.

sessions.title: Early Career Reception
sessions.abstract: Launch your journey, build your toolkit, and find your pack Join us for an energetic meetup designed specifically for early-career technologists, recent grads, and career-switchers looking to make a splash in the industry. Meet inspiring mentors, connect with fellow rising stars, and unlock the community support and foundational skills you need to navigate your tech career with absolute confidence.
